issues.title: server: the shared direct metadata listener runs named-group applies inline, so one Welcome fetch blocks every group's events (up to ~115 s)
issues.body:
Found while fixing #1207/#1217 (PR #1222, review round 3). Pre-existing behaviour; not changed by #1222.

The shared direct metadata listener (`src/server/mod.rs` ~2069) awaits each named-group metadata apply inline. A valid seating event that needs a Welcome fetch therefore blocks the listener until the Welcome arrives or the fetch times out (~115 s). During that time, direct metadata events for **every other group** on this daemon wait.

#1222 makes sure its new cold-recipient wait adds little to this: cheap rejection, plus one wait per source per 60 s. But the underlying head-of-line blocking remains.

## Done looks like
- Applies that can wait on the network (Welcome fetch, catch-up) run off the shared listener, with per-group ordering kept: a per-group queue or task.
- A test: a slow Welcome fetch for group A does not delay a metadata event for group B beyond a small bound.
- Watch the ADR-0066 epoch and membership-lock rules: no wait under the membership lock.

Likely W3 lane 1 (touches `src/server/routes/named_groups.rs`), after the harness case exists.

issues.title: sdk: bare Agent subscriptions can run without the revocation and Blocked stores
issues.body:
Found by the Codex review of #1114 (PR #1223); pre-existing.

Delivery-time revocation and Blocked checks are wired only through `Agent::set_contacts` (`src/lib.rs` ~9736); the builder does not attach these stores. `PubSubManager` snapshots the optional handles at subscribe time (`src/gossip/pubsub.rs` ~1868), and the checks are conditional on them (~2997). So an SDK subscription created without contacts, or before they are attached, delivers signed messages from revoked or Blocked agents. x0xd itself attaches contacts at startup; embedders using the crate directly are exposed.

## Done looks like
- The builder attaches the revocation set and contact store, or subscriptions resolve them at delivery time rather than snapshotting at subscribe time.
- A red test: a subscription created before `set_contacts` delivers a message from a revoked agent today; green after the fix.

issues.title: groups/ws: stored and backfilled messages are delivered without current revocation/Blocked checks
issues.body:
Found by the Codex review of #1114 (PR #1223); pre-existing, outside that PR's live-ingress guard.

- Stored public messages are deserialized and merged into responses without checking the sender's current revocation or Blocked status (`src/server/routes/named_groups.rs` ~16401). Before #1223, a Blocked member could inject a signed public message inside unsigned V1; it was admitted (~17392) and persisted (~16917). Those records stay deliverable after upgrade.
- WS topic backfill emits history directly (`src/server/ws.rs` ~1135) with no sender authorization check.

## Done looks like
- History, cache and backfill delivery re-check the sender against the current revocation set and Blocked list at delivery time.
- A red test: a message stored from a sender who is later revoked or Blocked is still served today; green after the fix.
- Charter invariant I3.

issues.title: server: some group routes have no actor check (session tokens can clear fork quarantine; /mls/groups has none)
issues.body:
Found by the GroupAccess inventory (#1166, PR #1227 report; checked by the controller at main 6544555). Riders are deny-by-default in the auth middleware, so these are reachable by the durable API token **and by short-lived browser session tokens** (`src/server/auth.rs`), which elsewhere are held to session-membership rules (#821/#870).

| Route | Check today |
|---|---|
| `POST /groups/:id/quarantine/clear` (`clear_group_quarantine`, named_groups.rs ~15216) | none: a session token can clear an ADR-0064 fork-quarantine marker |
| `/mls/groups*` (7 routes, `src/server/routes/groups.rs`) | no `ActorContext` use at all (legacy; removed by W3 one-crypto) |
| `GET /groups/:id/requests` (~24958), `DELETE /groups/:id/requests/:rid` (~26204) | no actor-based check |
| `PUT /groups/:id/display-name` (~19614) | Home durable fence only; no admin/role check for ordinary groups |

## Plan
Each tightening lands as its own reviewed change in GroupAccess slices S3/S4 (lane 4), never hidden inside a behaviour-preserving refactor. Targets: quarantine/clear → durable owner; requests list → durable owner, cancel → the requester; display-name → admin; /mls/groups → durable owner until removed.
Each change needs a red test showing a session token is accepted today.

issues.title: pubsub: relays still forward frames whose inner payload is unsigned V1
issues.body:
Follow-up to #1114 (PR #1223). After #1223 receivers refuse to deliver inner V1, but relays still forward such frames. Dropping them at relay ingress is optional hardening: it saves bandwidth (Track E) and removes a spam carrier. No released x0xd emits inner V1, so no compatible traffic is lost.

## Done looks like
- A relay drops a frame whose inner payload decodes as V1, with a counter.
- A test shows the frame is not forwarded.

issues.title: pubsub: remove inner-V1 (unsigned) emission from PubSubManager without a signing context
issues.body:
Follow-up to #1114 (PR #1223). After #1223, receivers never deliver inner V1 to apps. The only V1 emit site (`src/gossip/pubsub.rs` ~2222) runs when a `PubSubManager` is built without a signing context (`PubSubManager::new(_, None)`): tests, the bench and third-party users. No released x0xd emits V1.

Removing emission changes the public constructor contract, so it is a separate PR (semver: v0.47.0 train).

## Done looks like
- `PubSubManager` cannot publish without a signing context (constructor requires it, or publish refuses with a typed error).
- Tests and the bench are migrated; no test loses coverage.

issues.title: groups: unsigned GroupCards are accepted on discovery (charter invariant I3)
issues.body:
Found while fixing #1114 (PR #1223). Group discovery still accepts an unsigned GroupCard (`src/server/routes/named_groups.rs` ~2469 at main 6544555). Charter invariant I3 says nothing unsigned or unverified reaches an app or internal consumer as authenticated.

## Done looks like
- An unsigned or unverifiable GroupCard is refused before it reaches the discovery index or any API response, with a counter and a debug log.
- A red test proves an unsigned card is currently listed, then green after the fix.
- Check whether any released version (0.45.x, 0.46.x) publishes unsigned cards before refusing them; if one does, the fix needs a compatibility plan.

Lane S of the agent team (`.planning/team-2026-10-05/PLAN.md`).

issues.title: test(e2e): Home fixture setup can fail with TimeoutExpired and an empty log (g463b home-a1; maybe g46r6 home-a2)
issues.body:
## What happened

The Home e2e fixture (`e2e_home_fixture`) failed in setup, before any gate row ran:

- **g463b, node home-a1:** setup raised `TimeoutExpired`, and the captured log was empty. It happened once. The rerun gave the normal baseline.
- **g46r6, node home-a2 (earlier):** setup raised an `AssertionError`. This may be the same fault.

Reported by Root during the v0.46.x gates.

## Why it matters

A setup flake looks like a product failure in a release gate and costs a full rerun. An empty log means we cannot tell harness fault from daemon fault.

## Done looks like

- Setup timeouts capture the daemon log, the setup command and its stderr before the fixture gives up, so the log is never empty.
- The setup step names the failing sub-step (start, readiness probe, identity, join) in the error.
- The cause of both runs is found, or the fixture retries the named transient step once and records that it did.

Related harness work: #1208 (mixed-version fleets), #1214 (private fixture readiness without the TreeKEM Welcome key), #1216 (survivor-rekey fixture).

issues.title: test: the paired #501 meter test cannot detect doubled or missing retry metering
issues.body:
## What is wrong

The paired #501 controlled-load test does not catch wrong retry metering. It checks only that D5 shows positive EAGER/IHAVE dissemination and that O5 shows zero egress. A change that counts each deferred EAGER retry twice, or not at all, still passes.

Found by the Codex review of #1210 (saorsa-gossip 0.5.87 pin and the move of the #501 meter premise). That review found no double-count or missing-count path in 0.5.87 itself. The gap is in the test, not the meter.

## Where

- `src/legacy_bus_interop_tests.rs`: the D5/O5 measurement case (around lines 384 and 1361).
- Meter: `record_outbound`, `record_publish_origin`, `record_publish_origin_bytes` in saorsa-gossip pubsub.

## Done looks like

- The test reconciles the exact number of EAGER attempts per peer, and their encoded frame lengths, for a scenario with a known number of deferred retries.
- A deliberately doubled retry record, and a deliberately dropped one, both make the test fail (negative controls).
- It runs in the isolated CI job like the existing case.

Priority P3: test coverage only; no known defect in shipped code.

issues.title: groups: MemberRemoved notice can miss a quickly-joined removed member after an owner restart (old resolver path)
issues.body:
## Summary

After an owner restart, a member that joined quickly and is then removed may never receive its `MemberRemoved` notice. The direct delivery fails at once with `recipient_undiscovered`, and the gossip copy does not arrive within 120 s.

This happens on the general (old) resolver path, which PR #1190 does not change. #1207 has the same root cause: a cold discovery cache fails at once instead of waiting a bounded time.

## Evidence (ephemeral testnet run `g10-1190c`, 2026-10-05)

**Setup:** arm B′. nyc and sfo run the #1190 candidate (`a42c08a`, x0xd `31034964…f407`). The other five nodes run v0.46.2.

**Failure:** `private` fixture run p4 ended at 31/32 checks. The failed check was `private_secure revocation reaches former member did not converge in 120s`.

**Sequence:**
1. sydney (v0.46.2) joined in 1.2 s.
2. About a minute later, candidate owner sfo removed sydney.
3. sfo logged `err_agent_not_found` and `failed to direct-direct-deliver named-group event: recipient_undiscovered: agent not found` 10 times, both direct and delayed.
4. sydney's journal shows no membership event.

**Frequency:** it happened in 1 of 3 mixed rounds. It did not happen in either all-candidate round.

## Likely cause (not proven)

The weakness is newly visible because PR #1190 made joins fast. Earlier, joins took 86–117 s, so the old cache had learned the joiner by the time it was removed.

## Fix direction

Apply the verified-source resolution with a time bound, from #1190, to the general

issues.title: test(e2e): survivor-rekey fixture — remove/ban, survivors decrypt, removed member cannot (run against v0.46.3)
issues.body:
## Summary

No canonical e2e fixture tests survivor rekey on the real network. G10 condition (2) for #1190 has never been covered. D174 lets v0.46.3 ship without it, but the fixture should run against v0.46.3 afterwards.

## The fixture

- **Groups:** a GSS (MlsEncrypted, legacy plane) group and a TreeKEM group, each with 4 or more members spread across regions.
- **Remove case:** remove one member (M), then check:
  - every remaining member gets the new epoch's class-K share (GSS) or commit (TreeKEM) and can decrypt a message sealed after the removal;
  - M cannot decrypt that message, and is refused any further share or Welcome (D60).
- **Ban case:** the same checks after a ban.
- **Restart variant:** the remover restarted 10–20 s before the remove, as in the #1190 owner-restart shape.
- **Mixed versions:** the remover on v0.46.3 with a v0.46.2 survivor, and the reverse.
- **Timings to record:** survivor rekey latency, and any `recipient_undiscovered` or typed resend.

## Notes

- There is a ban only in `tests/e2e_treekem_membership.py` and in `e2e_*.sh`. Neither is in the eph `$E fixture` table.
- Related: #1190, #1214 (readiness does not prove the key is installed), D60.

issues.title: test(e2e): private fixture readiness passes without the TreeKEM Welcome key
issues.body:
## Summary

The `private` e2e fixture's join-readiness check passes even when the joiner failed to fetch its TreeKEM Welcome. The check looks only at the roster and the local "active" state, not at whether the epoch key was installed.

## Evidence (ephemeral testnet run `g10-1190b`, 2026-10-04)

In runs p4, b4 and d4, the joiner sydney logged `failed to fetch TreeKEM Welcome blob after retries` about 1 s before its readiness check passed. This happened in every arm, including the one where every node ran v0.46.2.

## Fix

Add a readiness check that the joiner holds the current epoch key. For example, decrypt a message sealed after the join, or compare the installed epoch with the authority's epoch. Fail the check when the Welcome fetch failed.

issues.title: groups: GSS share can be lost after an owner restart (pre-existing in v0.46.1 and v0.46.2; ~2/18)
issues.body:
## Summary

In v0.46.2, a GSS (class-K) group key share can fail to reach a joiner when the **owner restarted 12–14 s earlier**. The joiner's secret never arrives (409 "no shared secret" at 120 s). It happened in 2 of the 4 runs whose owner had just restarted, including on a fleet running only v0.46.2. In the earlier run g10-1190a, v0.46.1 delivered the same case in 0.123 s, but that was one sample only.

## Evidence (ephemeral testnet run `g10-1190b`, 2026-10-04)

- **Release binary:** x0xd `f6c91b0d…a621`, the published v0.46.2, source `d7f7b07`.
- **Failures:**
  - `gss` fixture run b2: v0.46.2 owner sfo, candidate joiners.
  - `gss` fixture run d2: every node on v0.46.2.

- **Owner log:** `err_agent_not_found` and `failed to direct-direct-deliver named-group event: recipient_undiscovered: agent not found` for helsinki, right after the restart. The gossip fallback did not deliver the share inside the 120 s window.

- How often does it happen? We need a ded

issues.title: test(e2e): the Home fixture rejects mixed-version fleets (one binary sha required)
issues.body:
## Summary

`tests/e2e_home_fixture.py` cannot run a mixed-version Home test. It requires every node to run the same x0xd binary, so a mixed fleet aborts before any Home step (0/4).

## Where

`tests/e2e_home_fixture.py` lines ~413–418:

```python
binary_hashes = {receipt[1] for receipt in receipts.values()}
evidence.check("fixture custody receipt is reproducible", len(binary_hashes) == 1, ...)
```

## Evidence

Ephemeral testnet run `g10-1190a` (2026-10-04), arms B and B3. These arms mixed v0.46.1 and a candidate build across 7 nodes. `home` failed at the custody check, 0/4 in both arms. The `gss` and `private` fixtures ran mixed without problems.

## Impact

Mixed-version Home behaviour (an old owner device with a new joiner, and the reverse) is not covered by any canonical fixture. Release gates that need mixed-version Home evidence cannot produce it.

## Proposed fix

Record the binary sha256 per node in the custody receipt and manifest, instead of requiring one value. Keep the reproducibility check per node: the receipt matches the binary deployed to that node. Add a `--mixed` or plan-driven expectation, so a single-binary run still asserts that every hash is equal.

issues.title: groups: a recently restarted joiner cannot resolve the authority (err_agent_not_found → fetch_retry_stalled), in v0.46.1
issues.body:
## Summary

A joiner restarted shortly before it joins cannot resolve the group authority. Its join stalls with `err_agent_not_found` and then `fetch_retry_stalled`. This is present in **v0.46.1**; it is not caused by #1190.

## Evidence (ephemeral testnet run `g10-1190a`, 2026-10-04)

- Arm D runs v0.46.1 on all 7 nodes (x0xd sha256 `ca0d641b…3708`).
- `private` fixture runs d1 (joiner helsinki) and d3 (joiner singapore) fail join readiness. In both, the joiner had restarted shortly before in the previous fixture.
- Joiner logs show `send_direct_raw_quic` → `outcome = "err_agent_not_found"` (`src/lib.rs` ~7785), then the TreeKEM Welcome fetch logs `stage = "fetch_retry_stalled"` (`src/server/routes/named_groups.rs` ~36256).
- The same fixture passes when the joiner has not restarted recently (d2, d4: 69/69).

## Likely cause

After a restart the agent-discovery cache is cold. Direct sends to an agent that the cache has not yet seen fail at once with `err_agent_not_found`, instead of waiting a bounded time for discovery or resolving the agent through a verified binding (for example the committed roster binding).

## Related

- #1190 (#1150): the same cold cache affects the *authority* side after an owner restart. #1190 removes the gossip fallback that used to hide it, so the share or Welcome arrives late (~120 s) or not at all. #1190 is held for v0.46.3 (D116).

## Next step

A bounded discovery wait or binding-based resolution before a direct send gives up, with a W3-H or in

issues.title: upgrade: startup update check on systemd hosts always refuses (runs ~3 s after start, inside the 10 s StartLimitInterval guard)
issues.body:
**Observed in prod during the v0.46.1 canary, 2026-10-04.**

saorsa-8 and saorsa-9 (on v0.46.0) had `[update] enabled` restored and were restarted at 07:13:51Z and 07:14:39Z. The startup update check found v0.46.1 but refused to apply it:

```
07:14:00Z  x0xd ActiveEnterTimestamp
07:14:03Z  ERROR x0x::server::routes::upgrade: Startup upgrade failed: refusing self-update: this instance reports INVOCATION_ID but the loaded systemd unit policy does not guarantee a restart after exit 0 (the unit's current activation has not outlived StartLimitIntervalUSec; ...). No binaries were replaced.
07:14:03Z  ERROR ... Upgrade failed: (same reason)
```

The unit is `Restart=always` and `RestartSec=5`, with the defaults `StartLimitIntervalUSec=10s` and `StartLimitBurst=5`.

**Cause:** the guard in `src/upgrade/restart.rs` (around line 1185) refuses until the current activation has outlived `StartLimitIntervalUSec`, which is 10 s by default. The startup check (`src/server/routes/upgrade.rs:218`) runs about 3 s after activation, so on a default systemd unit it ALWAYS refuses. The version is then skipped, and the node waits for its next 6-hourly fallback poll.

**Impact:**
- A restart never applies a pending release on systemd hosts. Only the 6-hourly fallback poll (or a gossip receipt after the 30-min skip) does.
- This adds to #1169: release pickup takes up to 6 h.
- For v0.46.0 on 10-03 the same restart DID apply within about 8 min, because those hosts ran 0.45.0, whose startup path didn't

issues.title: pubsub: an IWANT serve whose reply claim was pruned before the attempt lock still arms a recovery probe that is then stranded (PR #106 follow-up)
issues.body:
A follow-up from the final cross-model review of PR #106 at 919c0e0. That review approved the PR with nits and found no P1.

**Where:** `crates/pubsub/src/lib.rs` ~9029: `claim_topic_send_attempts_for_reply` on the IWANT-serve path.

**Problem.** If the serve's reply claim is pruned (TTL) or dropped by disconnect cleanup while the serve waits to take this lock, claiming the send attempts still arms a recovery probe. Attaching the probe to the claim is skipped, because the token is stale. Then the completion and the `Drop` booking both book nothing, because the reply is stale. The newly armed probe is left in flight, and sends to that peer stay suppressed until inbound activity or a disconnect.

**Fix.** Check reply-token ownership BEFORE arming an IWANT recovery probe, under the same lock. A stale claim must refuse to arm.

**Test.** Prune or disconnect the reply claim while the serve waits before the attempt lock. Assert that no probe is armed, and that a later send to the peer is not suppressed. It should be red before the fix and green after, in debug and release.

Severity: a narrow ordering window; it self-recovers on inbound activity or disconnect.

issues.title: groups: a timed-out join with no carry that redeems a base-seated invite leaves its attempt entry; remove + re-invite then 409 join_already_pending until restart
issues.body:
A pre-existing bug, found while implementing #1150 (a) (PR #1190, ADR 0107). It is not fixed there. Filed under D36.

**Steps**
1. A joiner's join attempt times out with no carry remnant.
2. The device then redeems an invite whose base already seats it. It goes to keyless `active`, which is the #1148 path, not the ADR 0107 re-arm.
3. The attempt entry for that group is never removed. Finalize returns `NotApplicable` because the device looks seated, and the poll exits as superseded once a removal drops the group.
4. The owner's recovery exit, remove-member then re-invite, now gets **409 `join_already_pending`** until the device restarts.

**Expected:** every path that ends a join attempt removes its attempt entry, including NotApplicable and superseded. The remove + re-invite exit must work without a restart.

**Acceptance:** an in-process test runs the sequence above and asserts that the re-invite redemption is accepted (no 409). The ADR 0107 Shape B control in PR #1190 currently avoids this with two fixtures; with the fix, it can use one.

Related: #1150, #1148, #1139, ADR 0088 L3 (no silent wedges).

issues.title: D27 removal: delete dead BootstrapConnector (src/bootstrap.rs:48)
issues.body:
Remove the dead \`BootstrapConnector\` type from \`src/bootstrap.rs\` (around line 48). This is a D27 removal-only PR: no behaviour change, no new code.

## Why

D27 ruling: dead code identified in the charter review is removed. \`BootstrapConnector\` is unreachable from any call path on \`origin/main\`; seeds are dialled address-only (TOFU) via the live bootstrap path, and \`pinned_bootstrap_peers\` is never consulted on the seed path. The dead type adds noise to future readers of \`src/bootstrap.rs\`.

## What done looks like

- \`BootstrapConnector\` and any transitively dead items it pulls in are deleted.
- \`cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings\` and \`cargo test\` pass with no changes elsewhere.
- The PR body references this issue and the D27 ruling.

## Links

- D27 ruling (charter)
- #1112 (related dead-code removal context)

issues.title: W4 entry gate: ADR 0095 (scope) and ADR 0096 (R12) with team-record and message-board definitions
issues.body:
Two ADRs that together form the W4 entry gate: ADR 0095 records the agreed scope (D19), and ADR 0096 accepts R12 ("x0x is maintained by its own agents"; D20). Neither has been drafted yet.

## Why

D19 and D20 rulings (charter, 2026-09-29): both decisions are agreed and need ADRs for acceptance. W4 goal build cannot start until these ADRs are accepted, because subsequent W4 work depends on the agreed scope and on R12 as an accepted requirement.

## What done looks like

- **ADR 0095** is drafted, reviewed and accepted. It records the D19 scope: x0x is the glue between people, their machines and their agents; it does not provide agents; shared places (scratchpads, message boards, project data) are core; sharing whole agent teams between people is core; goal E efficiency is core. It supersedes ADR-0017's positioning section. It folds in the team-record definition and the message-board definition as scope items.
- **ADR 0096** is drafted, reviewed and accepted. It adds R12 to the requirement set: x0x is maintained by its own agents.
- Both ADRs are Accepted (with David's signature) and merged to main before any W4 code PR is opened.

## Links

- D19 and D20 rulings (charter, 2026-09-29)

issues.title: Track E: agent-usability eval — fresh agent onboards, sends a DM, joins a group, and writes a scratch entry, scored in CI
issues.body:
An automated eval that confirms a fresh agent, given only the output of \`x0x onboard\` plus the core skill file, can successfully send a first DM, join a group and write a scratch entry. The eval runs in CI and produces a pass/fail score.

## Why

Goal E headline requirement (D19): "any agent that sees x0x knows how to use it." Without an automated eval there is no CI gate on this property. If the skill file or the API changes and breaks agent usability, it goes undetected until a field report arrives.

## What done looks like

- A CI job (or test marked `agent_usability`) that:
  1. Starts two isolated loopback-only daemon instances.
  2. Feeds one instance's \`x0x onboard\` output plus the core SKILL.md section to a deterministic test agent (no LLM required: the test agent follows a scripted decision tree derived from the skill output).
  3. The test agent sends a DM, joins a group and writes a scratch entry, using only the API surface documented in the core skill.
  4. The eval passes if all three actions complete without error, fail if any action requires information not present in the onboard output or core skill.
- The eval is gated in CI; a regression in skill clarity or API surface fails the job.

## Links

- #1173 (SKILL.md split — the core skill this eval consumes)
- Planning notes: `.planning/x0x-efficiency-plan-2026-09-29.md` (agent-usability eval)

issues.title: Track E / E-D12: split SKILL.md (82 KB, ~20.7k tokens) and add a CI token budget
issues.body:
SKILL.md has grown to 82 KB (~20.7k tokens), exceeding the headline requirement that an agent given only SKILL.md output can use x0x. Split it into focused sections and gate each section's size in CI.

## Why

Goal E (D19): "any agent that sees x0x knows how to use it". A single 82 KB skill file is too large for agents with small context windows, and it prevents selective loading. E-D12 from the efficiency plan calls for splitting it per capability domain.

## What done looks like

- SKILL.md is split into at most 4–5 files, each under a token budget agreed with David (suggested: a core file ≤8k tokens, supplementary files ≤4k each).
- A CI check (`just check-skill-size` or equivalent) fails if any file exceeds its budget.
- The core file is sufficient for a first DM, group join and scratch write without loading any supplementary file.
- Existing embedders that reference `SKILL.md` by path work without changes (the main file becomes an index or re-exports the core).

issues.title: Track E / M1: per-kind gossip counters (verify, bus, delivered, published) for efficiency baselines
issues.body:
Add per-message-kind counters for the four most important efficiency signals: verify cost, bus cost, delivered count and published count. These counters feed the M1 health verdict and the Track E baseline measurements.

## Why

Goal E: explicit, measured budgets for CPU, bandwidth and latency. Track E has no counters yet for per-kind verify cost or per-kind delivery success rate. Without them, the E0-b soak and future efficiency regressions cannot be attributed to a specific message kind.

## Depends on

- #869 (gossip observability primitives, which this issue extends)

## What done looks like

- `GET /diagnostics/gossip` includes per-kind counters:
  - `verify_ok` / `verify_err` (count and total CPU time) per message kind.
  - `bus_dispatched` / `bus_dropped` per kind.
  - `delivered` (to local consumers) per kind.
  - `published` (sent to peers) per kind.
- Counters survive a rolling reset and expose a `since_ts` field so consumers can compute rates.
- The M1 health verdict uses these counters to identify a kind contributing more than a configured share of CPU or bus pressure.

issues.title: M2 (ADR 0094) must cover a binary that cannot exec: old-binary exec probe, supervisor recovery, and CI rollback test
issues.body:
ADR 0094 (M2 safe apply) has a gap: it relies on the NEW binary's boot counter to detect a restart loop, so a binary that cannot be executed at all (exit 203/EXEC) is not covered and will restart-loop without triggering rollback.

## Why

Row 7b of the v0.46.0 canary observed exactly this: a non-executable binary restart-looped with exit 203/EXEC without triggering rollback, because the boot counter lived in the NEW binary which never ran. The M2 design in ADR 0094 and in `src/upgrade/apply.rs` must be extended to address this case.

## What done looks like

- **Pre-swap exec probe by the OLD binary:** before overwriting the binary, the installer calls `execve` (or equivalent) on the downloaded file in a sandboxed way to confirm it is executable. If the probe fails, the swap is aborted and rollback occurs immediately.
- **Supervisor-owned recovery:** the recovery path does not depend on the new binary running. For systemd hosts, `OnFailure=` (or an equivalent stable launcher) restores the backup binary before re-starting the service.
- **Exit test covering both cases:** a test that installs (a) a crash-looping binary and (b) a non-executable binary, then confirms rollback completes and the node comes back on the previous version in both cases.
- **CI test of the transactional rollback:** the swap + commit + rollback sequence is exercised in CI with a real filesystem, confirming atomicity under failure injection.

## Links

- #1115 (ADR 0094: flush, rollback, one binary writer

D21 ruling: Track M-safety starts right after v0.46.0, in parallel with W3. D35 ruling: publish a minimum supported version and support window for embedders, owned by M1's census. Goal M (R12, ADR 0096 once accepted): agents maintain x0x.

issues.title: W3/W4 pre-work: GroupAccess extractor, Outbox<T> consolidation, and fetch-by-hash primitive
issues.body:
Three chokepoint primitives that W4 depends on. Tracked here together because they share no code path but all must exist before W4 goal-build work starts.

## Why

D18 ruling: TreeKEM only plus `Outbox<T>`, enforced in CI. D23 confirms that typed-route consolidation proceeds as planned. The W4 A-goal depends on `GroupAccess`, `Outbox<T>` and fetch-by-hash being available before the scratch store (A5) and the team record land.

## Checklist

- [ ] **GroupAccess extractor** — a single axum extractor that checks group membership for the session or rider, replacing the ~82 inline authz checks across the group routes (`src/server/routes/`). All group routes use it. CI enforces no bare inline checks.
- [ ] **`Outbox<T>` consolidation** — a single generic typed-message outbox replacing the 4–5 hand-rolled outboxes. The request/approve flow is the first consumer; the DM-inbox topic extension follows.
- [ ] **Fetch-by-hash primitive** — a wire-level mechanism (holder store per ADR 0085; hash-referenced carrier) that any ADR 0088 slice can use to reference and retrieve evidence. This is the home for S5's inline-carry-up-to-K plus hash-remainder design, and for catch-up as control blobs.

issues.title: fix(groups) residue: synthetic size assertion and fixture bypasses FetchRequest serving path (ADR 0087 review finding, PR #1140)
issues.body:
Two P2 findings from the Greptile review of PR #1140 that require issues or written dismissals under ADR 0087 rule 9.

## Why

ADR 0087 rule 9: review findings on merged PRs become issues or written dismissals within 24 h.

### Finding 1: size assertion uses a synthetic event

The test for the JoinResult carry size asserts against a manually constructed event rather than one produced by the real commit path. A synthetic event may not match the encoding, signing overhead, or field layout of a real `MemberAdded` event, so the assertion does not guard against actual size regressions.

### Finding 2: fixture bypasses the FetchRequest serving path

The fixture used to prove row 4b (restart cold, then rehydrate from a peer) loads the carry blob directly rather than going through the `FetchRequest` handler. This matters for ADR 0107 / S8(a): the fix's correctness guarantee depends on the serving path behaving correctly under real fetch conditions.

## Done looks like

- The size assertion is derived from an event produced by the real commit path, not a hand-constructed one.
- The fixture exercises the `FetchRequest` handler end-to-end (offer → fetch → verify), matching what production nodes do.

## Links

- PR #1140 (reviewed change, now merged)
- #1139 (the underlying bug)
- ADR 0106 (accepted, the S1 slice)

issues.title: fix(groups) residue: restart recovery untested and removal-delivered path silently skippable (ADR 0087 review finding, PR #1148)
issues.body:
Two P2 findings from the Greptile review of PR #1148 that require issues or written dismissals under ADR 0087 rule 9.

## Why

ADR 0087 rule 9: review findings on merged PRs become issues or written dismissals within 24 h.

### Finding 1: restart recovery path is untested

The `not_member` fix in PR #1148 has no test that restarts the daemon with a persisted `not_member` row and confirms the corrected recovery path is taken on reload. A restart between the intermediate apply and the re-invite could leave the node in an untested state.

### Finding 2: "removal delivered" path can be skipped silently

In the removal flow, a code path that should confirm removal delivery can exit without logging or raising an error when a condition is not met, leaving the authority's obligation unacknowledged. The skip is silent: no counter is incremented and no error propagates.

## Done looks like

- A restart-recovery test: persist a `not_member` row, restart the daemon, confirm the expected recovery state and the correct REST response.
- The "removal delivered" path either completes (records the acknowledgement) or returns a visible error; it does not exit silently.

## Links

- PR #1148 (reviewed change, now merged)
- #1161 (sibling finding from the same review)

issues.title: fix(groups) residue: not_member + no invite_lineage classified as Other and stays stuck (ADR 0087 review finding, PR #1148)
issues.body:
A `not_member` row with no `invite_lineage` field is classified as `Other` by the join-result classifier and left without a recovery path, so the device stays stuck.

## Why

ADR 0087 rule 9 (review findings become issues or written dismissals within 24 h) applies. The finding is from the Greptile review of PR #1148, marked P1. The relevant code is `src/server/routes/named_groups.rs` around lines 17718–17728 on origin/main. An absent `invite_lineage` in a `not_member` row is a valid post-D39(A) state (the carry was applied but the device's own seat failed or timed out), and the `Other` arm provides no user-visible remedy.

Note: `invite_lineage` was present in v0.45.0, so this is a v0.46 regression in the classification logic, not a migration gap.

## Done looks like

- The classifier handles `not_member` rows with no `invite_lineage` explicitly, mapping them to a defined state (e.g. `JoinFailed`) rather than `Other`.
- The REST response for that state includes a user-actionable remedy (e.g. request a fresh invite via the authority device).
- A test covers this exact row shape, including the `not_member` + absent `invite_lineage` combination.

## Links

- PR #1148 (the reviewed change, now merged)
- #1146 (JimCollinson's report of the stuck device)
- ADR 0106 (the S1 slice; the carry is the source of the intermediate state)

issues.title: Home: a sealed-but-unconfirmed device can't recover its keys; fresh invite is keyless (authority step 7 rejects MemberJoined from Active)
issues.body:
**Priority:** P2 · **Target:** v0.46.x. David's ruling (c), 2026-10-01: this is a known limitation for v0.46.0, with options (a) and (b) to be done properly in v0.46.x. There is related work in #1149 and D39 (#1147 and #1148, both closed, not merged).

## Symptom
A Home (TreeKEM) device whose join timed out **after the authority had already sealed its add** cannot get its keys back through a fresh invite. It ends up locally `active` with **no TreeKEM group**, so it cannot read or post. The await_treekem poll never confirms, and the attempt ends `timed_out`. This is the usual #1139 / D39(A) shape: in rc5 the authority roster had the joiner (`expected_member_present: true`).

## Mechanism (eb4c6b7)
1. **The authority ignores the re-join.** Step 7 of its MemberJoined handler (`src/server/routes/named_groups.rs` ~13397–13402) treats a MemberJoined from a joiner it already holds **Active** as an idempotent replay and returns REJECTED. It stages nothing new and issues no new Welcome.
2. **The fresh invite base-seats the device.** The authority sealed the device's add, so any fresh invite's base snapshot already seats it. `base_seats_joiner` (~18413) then makes the device durably `active` from that snapshot alone.
3. **The Welcome is never consumed.** The device's Welcome rides only on its own MemberAdded. That event is at the same revision as the base, so it is stale and dropped. No other Welcome path exists; the only other `join_from_welcome` site is JoinRequestApproved.

issues.title: groups: a base-seated invite counts as admission with no current-authority confirmation (self-rejoin and D39 recovery)
issues.body:
Pre-existing on v0.45 and v0.46 (eb4c6b7). Found by the Codex round-2 review of #1148 (D39 A).

**What happens.** `base_seats_joiner` (src/server/routes/named_groups.rs ~18413) treats an invite whose base roster snapshot already seats the joiner as the confirmation, and immediately persists durable local membership. That is the #468 A5 self-rejoin shape. Sequence: the authority admits J, mints an invite whose snapshot holds J's ACTIVE seat, then bans J, and J never observes the admission or the ban. Using that invite, J reports local `active`. For non-TreeKEM groups the join poll (~35579) confirms it on `info.has_member`. #1148 lets a stuck D39 remnant reach the same path.

**Impact.**
- On Home/TreeKEM groups: none beyond a misleading local state. No Welcome comes from the banning authority, so there are no keys and the device can't read or post, and peers reject its traffic because the authority roster keeps the ban.
- On non-TreeKEM groups: the exposure is the same as today's pre-existing self-rejoin.

**Fix direction (v0.46.x, probably ADR-worthy):** an unconfirmed-membership state for base-seated joins. Do not report `active` and do not write durably until the authority's join Result or current roster confirms; the non-TreeKEM poll confirms on an authority result; the authority answers a MemberJoined from an already-seated device.

issues.title: Refused join retains a non-member group record and blocks a later valid invitation
issues.body:
## Summary

A consumed invitation is correctly refused, but the refused joiner can retain a
local named-group record with `membership_state: "not_member"`. When this happens,
a new valid invitation addressed to that same identity returns HTTP 200 with
`already_joined: false` and `join_state: "not_member"`, without starting a new join.

This blocks legitimate later admission. It is **not an observed authorization
bypass**: the used invitation was refused and both tested secure operations on
the refused joiner returned HTTP 403 `not a member`.

Related: #477 (typed consumed-invite refusals and finalization, closed) and #481
(deferred pending-join lifecycle work). This report identifies the retained-row
plus subsequent-valid-invitation failure rather than a missing refusal receipt.

## Tested Version And Environment

- Released [v0.45.0](https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/releases/tag/v0.45.0),
  commit `0988ce46b8e3eddb7389ac45178ee3c73a5b0ef9`.
- Apple Silicon macOS; official `x0x-macos-arm64.tar.gz`, SHA-256
  `f821fae46cb1a63493b8babd5bef1af6900043b59365ed264957f3f1eee4f483`;
  Apple code-signature and notarization checks passed.

issues.title: Back-to-back Home/private joins: the second joiner stays pending_authority_commit (never applies r+2 without r+1) — #818 / D16 hole (a)
issues.body:
Seen in every eph gate run with Home: g46r2 diag, g46r3 b1/b2, g46r4 b1/b2 and g46r5 b1 (rc5 f3e3dcd, which includes ADR 0089 S1–S5). The later joiner (nuremberg or london) times out at 'Home seat reaches owner and local readiness'.

**Evidence** (g46r5 b1, analysis by x0x-32; logs at omp-reports/testnet-runs/g46r5/live/home-b1-*.log.gz):

- sfo is active after 0.9 s. nuremberg stays `pending_authority_commit` for 120 s.

- nuremberg validates `join_result` (95,666 B) about 44 times between 18:30:36 and 18:32:06, then logs `timed out polling authority for join result … await_treekem=true`. No other WARN appears.

issues.title: PeerId-carrying dials still abort on the ~2.08 s direct-stage budget under CPU contention (#292 residual)
issues.body:
Follow-up to #292 (closed) / #293. Downstream tracker: saorsa-labs/x0x#1110 (x0x#623 residual).

## Problem
#293 gave **address-only** `connect_addr` dials the caller's remaining overall budget, fixing terminal `ConnectionFailed` under CPU contention for that path (#292).

Dials that carry a **target PeerId** still use the adaptive direct stage: in v0.27.54 that is 4×RTT + 750 ms clamped to ≥ 1 s (`src/connection_strategy.rs` ~223–240; `direct_stage_timeout` in `src/p2p_endpoint.rs` ~564–581 leaves non-address-only dials unchanged). That is ~2.08 s at the default 333 ms initial RTT, and down to the 1 s floor when a small RTT is cached.

Under CPU contention downstream measured completed loopback handshakes taking up to ~5.9 s (x0x#623), so PeerId dials can still abort terminally even when the caller has budget left.

Affected downstream callers (x0x): agent connect, machine connect, enrolled owner-sync dial, and the reconnect scheduler.

## Proposed fix

issues.title: Calls: outbound call gate ignores the Call ShareGrant that the inbound gate honours (asymmetric, ACL Enabled)
issues.body:
From the #802 Greptile P1 'Call grants fail outbound checks' (D36 24 h rule; verified by Root against main).

`call_gate_inbound_with` (src/calls.rs:799-826) admits a caller through `gate_peer_machine_inbound_with_call_grant`, so a Call-scope ShareGrant counts. `call_gate_outbound` (src/calls.rs:837-866) uses `gate_peer_outbound` + `stream_acl_gate(&policy, &[callee], owner_trusted, &machine)`, and **no grant check at all**. issues.title: TreeKEM self-leave never rekeys: the leaver can derive later epochs' keys (ADR-0014's second half is unimplemented)
issues.body:
Planned as **N20** in the 2026-09-28 resolution plan (§9, W3). It was not filed until the 2026-09-30 D32 hygiene pass. This is a confidentiality gap with no tracker. N-numbers are local planning labels.

**Rulings**
- **D18:** one group crypto (TreeKEM only, ADR 0091) and `Outbox<T>`.
- **D34(2) (2026-09-30):** "any online admin that receives a revocation evicts and rekeys automatically, within a bound", and group membership joins the I7 live-session rule. Self-leave is the same "member gone, rekey" obligation.

**Wave / milestone:** W3, the seal-service chokepoint (invariant I4). v0.46 known limitation 9 applies until then: "Self-leave does not rekey".

## Problem (verified in code on main 6100b78)

ADR-0014 splits self-leave into two halves:
1. a signed roster removal, which is **implemented**;
2. an owner-driven `remove_member` rekey, which is **not**. The ADR marks it "tracked", with no issue number.

**What the code does**
- When a member self-leaves a TreeKEM group, the remaining members remove it from the roster, but nobody commits a TreeKEM removal (`src/server/routes/named_groups.rs` ~11850–11925; `leave_treekem_group` ~20446).
- TreeKEM remove commits are produced only by admin remove (`remove_treekem_named_group_member` ~20600) and ban (`ban_treekem_group_member` ~23821). There is no other rekey trigger in production code.
- **Result:** the group stays at the same epoch, and the leaver can still derive keys for later traffic until an unrelated commit rotates them.

issues.title: ShareGrant accept rolls a grant out of memory on a post-rename fsync error, but disk keeps it (grant reappears after restart)
issues.body:
Untracked review finding on merged code. Filed under D32 and the D36 rule that review findings on merged PRs become issues. Source: the 2026-09-30 design health check §4 (W2).

**Source:** a Greptile P1 on #802, "Grant rollback leaves disk changed", with no reply: https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/pull/802#discussion_r4120809194.

## Problem (verified in code on main 6100b78; low severity)

- `ShareGrantStore::accept` (`src/share_grant.rs` ~635–676) removes a received grant from memory, and withholds the durable ACK, whenever `persist` fails (~669–674).
- `persist` (~679–700) calls `storage::write_private_bytes_durable` (`src/storage.rs` ~322–386). That helper returns the same `Err` for a failure **after** the atomic rename (the parent-directory open or fsync, ~379–384) as for a failure before it. After the rename, `share-grants.bin` already contains the grant.
- Memory then says "not stored" while disk has the grant, and a restart loads (`share_grant.rs` ~505) and enforces a grant that was reported as refused.
- The next successful persist of any *other* grant rewrites the file from memory without it. The grant can therefore appear and disappear across restarts.

By contrast, `OwnerSyncStore` separates pre-rename from post-rename failures and poisons the store on the latter.

## Fix

- Have the durable-write helper return a typed error that says whether the failure came before or after the rename.
- On a post-rename failure, keep the grant in memory. Withhold the ACK or poi

issues.title: x0xd startup update check blocks API bind ~30 s when GitHub is unreachable
issues.body:
Found during v0.46.0 gate row 1 (ephemeral testnet g46r2, where TCP 443 egress is closed). It affects v0.45.0 and rc2 (05ca738) alike, so it is not a regression.

**Symptom:** with `[update]` enabled (the default) and api.github.com unreachable, x0xd does not bind its API until the startup update check times out, about 30 s after start.

Debug trace on a fresh node (config: no `[update]` section, no peers):
```
00:17:40.942 DEBUG reqwest::connect: starting new connection: https://api.github.com/
00:18:10.943 WARN  x0x::server: Startup update check failed: failed to fetch manifest: GitHub API request failed: ...
00:18:10.991 INFO  x0x::server: API server listening on 127.0.0.1:14699
```

**Impact:** firewalled or offline hosts, and anything supervising x0xd with a readiness timeout under 30 s (it broke the Home e2e harness's 15 s tunnel readiness on both arms), see a 30 s startup stall.

**Expected:** the update check should not gate startup. Run it after the API is up, or in the background with a short timeout.

Evidence: omp-reports/testnet-runs/g46r2/G46R2-SUMMARY.md (finding 2).

owner-sync: unenroll leaves no tombstone; live SyncV1 sessions are not re-checked (ADR 0084 findings 3–4)
issues.body:
From the Codex review of ADR 0084 (#1052, accepted afacc56). These limitations are documented in the ADR's Trade-offs and are not v0.46.0 blockers.

1. **`OwnerSyncStore::unenroll` removes the record without a tombstone.**
   - If an old, still-unexpired owner-signed enrollment for that machine is re-inserted locally (a `sync/devices.json` restore, or re-running `enroll` with an old enrollment), admission comes back. This includes the #1040 enrollment-only SyncV1 path.
   - This is local only: enrollments are not accepted from the network.
   - Proposed fix: persist a deletion tombstone `(machine, deleted_at_ms)`, and make `enroll` refuse any enrollment with `enrolled_at_ms <= deleted_at_ms`.
2. **An admitted SyncV1 session is not re-checked while it runs.**
   - Revocation, expiry or unenroll takes effect only at the next admission.
   - Proposed fix: re-check enrollment and machine revocation between session phases or pages, and abort fail-closed.
3. **Expiry grace.** Expiry is checked with a 5-minute skew tolerance (`ENROLL_EXPIRY_SKEW_MS`). This is intentional and documented; no change is proposed.

Scheduling: after v0.46.0 (fixes-only moratorium), unless David pulls it forward. Related: #1040, #1054.

issues.title: KV direct-delivery fallback (#985) never delivers: serde_json encode of KvStoreDelta fails 'key must be a string'
issues.body:
Found in the R20 legacy window (testnet SFO, pin 74c34f2). It logged 80× in about 20 s:

```
WARN x0x::server::routes::stores: failed to serialize kv-store delta for direct delivery: key must be a string store_id="x0x-wiki-<gid16>"
```

**Where:** `src/server/routes/stores.rs` `encode_kv_store_delta_direct_payload` (~L74–88) calls `serde_json::to_vec(&KvStoreDirectDelta { store_id, peer_id, delta })`. `spawn_kv_store_delta_delivery_one` (~L118) logs the error and returns, so **the direct-delivery fallback added in #985 never delivers** for these deltas.

**Store type:** the legacy SOURCE stores created by `POST /stores {name: wiki|web, topic: x0x-<app>-<gid16>, policy: signed}`. These are plain signed stores, not group-encrypted ones. The failing deltas come from the fixture's seed puts plus a DELETE (the `legacy-removed` tombstone).

**Likely cause (unconfirmed):** `KvStoreDelta`'s top-level maps are keyed by `String` (`added`, `removed`, `updated`), so the non-string map key is nested: inside `KvEntry`, `UniqueTag` or `LwwRegister` (for example a map keyed by a struct, bytes or a tuple). JSON cannot encode those as object keys.

**Fix options:**
- encode the direct-delivery payload with bincode, as the gossip path does, keeping the prefix and making the decoder match; or
- use `serde_with` sequence-of-pairs for the offending map.

Old receivers must stay compatible; the decoder is at the other end of `KV_STORE_DELTA_DM_PREFIX`.

**Test (Rule 9):** encode and decode a delta

issues.title: Owner sync: restarted owner device denies its own enrolled owner machine's authenticated SyncV1 stream (empty discovery cache) → Home provisioning stuck
issues.body:
R20 Home 13/16 root cause (analysis: omp-reports/takeover-20260921/x0x32-r20-home.md; run 91ad428d).

A restarted owner device (SFO) has an empty discovery cache.
- It **cannot dial** its enrolled owner machine (`machine not in discovery cache`).
- It **denies** that machine's transport-authenticated inbound owner-sync `SyncV1` stream as `deny_not_verified`. The peer sees a stream reset with 0xA17C0244.

This continues until a gossip identity announcement arrives, which can take more than 120 s on loaded hosts. Home provisioning stays `provisioning_pending` (#824). R19 won the race after about 60 s; R20 lost it.

**Fix (Root, 2026-09-28; R21 scope):**
1. Admit an inbound `SyncV1` owner-sync stream **only** when the transport-authenticated machine id is in this device's **verified**, owner-signed enrollment set: the signature chain verifies, and the enrollment is not expired or revoked. No other stream kind is widened, and `deny_not_verified` stays for everything else.
2. On a discovery-cache miss, dial using only addresses from the signed enrollment or the bootstrap cache, by the enrolled machine id, so the transport authenticates the peer.
3. Re-announce identity when an enrolled owner machine connects, bounded and rate-limited.

**Tests:**
- A restart with an empty cache syncs and Home settles with no announcement delivered (red on 74c34f2).
- A non-enrolled machine with an authenticated stream is still denied.
- A revoked or expired enrollment is denied.

Likely closes #84

issues.title: membership: HyParView active view keeps never-connected random-walk peers; nothing prunes by transport connectivity
issues.body:
Found via saorsa-labs/x0x#1036 (a prod log flood of about 16 GB/day). Code refs are `saorsa-gossip-membership` 0.5.86 `src/lib.rs`.

- `handle_join` (~1247) and `handle_forward_join` (~1285) → `add_active` (~1741) add random-walk peers to the active view, including peers this node never connects to. They are marked SWIM-alive.
- Nothing prunes the active view by transport connectivity. SWIM probes (every 1 s), shuffles (always sent to the first active peer) and forward-joins keep sending to them, and every send fails with `Peer not found`.

x0x now works around this: `fix/1036-stale-send-targets` prunes active-view peers that have been disconnected for 60 s or more and restores them on reconnect.

**Proper fix:** membership prunes, or does not admit, active-view peers without a transport connection, while keeping HyParView's repair semantics.

issues.title: P1 ops: prod x0xd floods syslog with ant_quic::send_error 'send failed' WARN (~16 GB/day), filled Nuremberg disk to 100%
issues.body:
Observed 2026-09-28 on the fleet (read-only diagnosis by Root/Claude).

- Nuremberg (116.203.101.172) reached **100% disk**. The live /var/log/syslog grew to **16 GB in about 1 day**, and last week's syslog.1 was 17 GB. Logrotate's gzip then failed with ENOSPC and held the deleted file open, and rsyslog looped on 'No space left'. David approved freeing space by deleting the rotated syslog.1 and stopping the stuck logrotate/gzip. No daemon was restarted.
- Every host has a 14–25 GB rotated syslog. Helsinki is at 86%.
- Source (last 30 MB of syslog): roughly 35k lines from x0xd-443 and 15k from x0xd of the form `WARN ant_quic::send_error: send failed peer_id=PeerId([n, n, … 32 bytes])`, with ANSI colour codes, ~690 bytes per line. It's a per-send WARN for repeated sends to unreachable or stale peers (cf. the testnet: 5,103 'Peer not found' sends per hour to non-fleet machines, x0x32-r19-home.md §5).

Asks:
1. **Product:** rate-limit or demote the per-send ant_quic send_error WARN (aggregate per peer per interval), print PeerId as short hex, and disable ANSI when the daemon isn't writing to a TTY/journald.
2. **Product:** stop retrying sends to peers that fail fast with 'Peer not found' (stale plane entries).
3. **Ops (needs David):** cap syslog by size on fleet hosts (logrotate maxsize / daily plus compress, or rely on journald), because 38 GB disks can't absorb this.

issues.title: pubsub: recovery-probe in-flight flag leaks when the send permit is refused → peer stays suppressed on the topic indefinitely
issues.body:
Found while root-causing x0x#857. Code refs are `saorsa-gossip-pubsub` 0.5.86 `src/lib.rs`.

**Bug**
- A recovery probe for a peer whose suppression expired marks itself in flight (~3264–3268) **before** it takes its send permit.
- If the permit is refused (budget exhausted, ~8237–8268), the probe is dropped, and nothing clears the in-flight flag (~1912–1925).
- Every later claim for that peer on that topic returns nothing. The peer stays effectively suppressed until it disconnects, sends traffic on that topic, or is otherwise rescued.
- This may explain x0x runs that never delivered within 60 s.

**Fix:** take the permit before turning a claim into a probe, or roll the in-flight flag back when the permit is refused.

**Test:** a peer with expired suppression and a held permit is claimed twice. On current code the flag stays set and later claims skip forever (red). After the fix the next claim probes (green).

Refs saorsa-labs/x0x#857.

issues.title: pubsub: a local Normal publish can be fully claim-skipped (per-peer permit held by relays) and gets no lazy announcement → waits for 30 s anti-entropy
issues.body:
Found via x0x#857 (the root cause is here; x0x only supplies load). Code refs are `saorsa-gossip-pubsub` 0.5.86 `src/lib.rs`.

**Mechanism**
- `claim_topic_send_attempts_for_state` (~8162) skips a peer if it is disconnected, cooling, or its **single per-peer Normal/Bulk in-flight permit** (~283, 8237–8268) is busy.
- That permit is keyed by peer only. It is shared by all topics and by relayed and local sends, so a relay burst after restarts (each send holding the permit for 1.5–10 s) can make a local publish find **every** eager peer busy (`claim_skipped = admitted - attempted`, ~8804/8867/8888).
- The per-reason counts (~1832–1851) are discarded, and the WARN (~9315–9335) prints only the sum.
- A Normal publish with every peer skipped gets **no** lazy announcement. Only byte deferral (~8720) and the Critical path (~8629) queue one. #613's stranded-publish recovery needs at least one attempted send (~9308), and pending announcements go only to lazy peers (~10822). Delivery therefore waits for the 30 s anti-entropy round (~154), which matches x0x's observed 22–59 s.

**Fixes**
1. Report per-reason skip counts (disconnected / cooling / budget) in `FanoutCounts` and the WARN.
2. Stop relayed traffic starving local publishes: give local publishes their own permit, or a short bounded wait.
3. Queue every skipped eager peer for the 100 ms announcement flush, so a fully skipped publish is still announced.

**Tests:** extend `fanout_stage_counts_outbound_budget_claim_skip` (~15757) t

issues.title: Notes (ADR-0081): saves >256 KiB use loro update_by_line — can duplicate lines / resurrect deleted text
issues.body:
Follow-up from the #965 notes-store slice (branch `feat/965-notes-store`).

The notes store's property test found that loro's default `LoroText::update` (refined diff) can bring back text another member deleted concurrently. The slice pins `use_refined_diff: false` for normal saves.

ADR-0081 requires `update_by_line` for saves over 256 KiB. That path has not been checked and may duplicate lines or bring back deleted text in the same way.

**Owner:** the merge-path slice of #965.

**Required:**
- A concurrent-delete property test over the >256 KiB path; it must be able to fail.
- A choice of a diff mode that never brings back deleted text, or a documented bound on what it can do.

Refs #965, ADR-0081.

issues.title: P1: Home admission deadlocks when creator/owner device is offline — admin cannot hydrate its owner cert (OwnerCertMemberPending)
issues.body:
**Release blocker, found as the R19 Home 101/102 root cause** (kvtrace run `2748d576…`; `omp-reports/takeover-20260921/x0x32-r19-home.md` §7).

**What happens**
1. The fixture takes the creator and original owner device (NYC) offline during admission.
2. A joiner (Helsinki) sends its signed JoinRequest offer by raw direct DM to the promoted admin (Singapore). It is delivered, verified and machine-attested 52 times.
3. Singapore refuses to seal the add every time:
   `MemberJoined: failed to seal authoritative add: owner-certified group … has members pending certificate resolution: ["<creator agent>"] (retry after fetch convergence)`
   This is `StateCommitError::OwnerCertMemberPending` (`src/groups/state_commit.rs`, ADR-0038 round-4).
4. Singapore never hydrates the creator's owner-device certificate, and the creator is offline, so the fetch can never converge. The join stays `pending_authority_commit` forever.

This is not transport. The fixture sockets saw zero drops and every message was delivered.

**Decision (Root, 2026-09-27): option (i).** This implements ADR-0038's intent with no semantic change.
- **Every** owner-certified member's certificate, meaning the creator and all owner devices, travels with group state and events: state commits, the roster snapshot served at join, and JoinResult. Any admin, including a promoted one, can then hydrate it without the owner online.

issues.title: ShareGrant outbox P3s: expired entries not rewritten on load; reconnect nudge skips already-due entries
issues.body:
Follow-up from the post-merge audit of #983 (#926), deferred from #994.

1. **Expired entries are not rewritten on load.** Entries that expired while the daemon was down are filtered in memory but stay in `share-grant-outbox.bin` until a later write. Persist the pruned set on load, or make that deliberate and document it.
2. **The reconnect nudge skips already-due entries.** When the grantee's machine reconnects, the immediate-retry nudge does not pick up an entry that is already due. Make the nudge include every due entry for that peer.

Each needs a test that fails without its fix.

issues.title: Wire ShareGrant Call cap into the inbound call gate (ADR-0073 × ADR-0070)
issues.body:
#924 (ShareGrant) has merged into `codex/final-acceptance-candidate`, so `GrantCap::Call` now exists (`src/share_grant.rs:115`). The inbound call gate still admits contact trust only. See `src/calls.rs` `call_gate_inbound` and its `HOOK(ADR-0070 / #924)`.

**Scope (R5 share a subset, R8 calls):**
- Admit a caller that fails **only** on trust, and never on revocation or the connect ACL, if it holds a live, unrevoked, unexpired `ShareGrant` with the `Call` cap that covers the callee agent.
- No new bypass. The checks still run in this order: revocation, then expiry, then ACL, then `dm_verified`, then that the caller is on the machine.

**Tests (red/green, Linux CI):**
- A grantee with a `Call` grant can ring.
- The same grantee is refused once the grant is revoked on `x0x.revocation.v3`, and refused once it expires.
- A grant without `Call` (for example `dm` only) is refused.
- A `Call` grant does **not** override an ACL denial.

Refs #891, #892.

issues.title: Relay engine: fan out one obligation's targets concurrently (buffer_unordered) — 9h worst-case serial pass
issues.body: From the #942 r5 review (N1/N2). Per-obligation budgeting bounds a pass by obligations, but the total-target cap (CAUSAL_RELAY_TARGETS_PER_DAEMON_CAP = 4096) means one pass can still make up to ~4096 SERIAL sends; each strict attempt times out at 8s, so an unreachable-heavy pass can take ~9h, and a fresh obligation waits for the whole in-flight pass. Fan out one obligation's targets with buffer_unordered(8..16) to cut the worst case by that factor. Also note: now_ms is sampled at pass start, so next_retry_at_ms can be stale after a long pass, and retention-expired obligations are only pruned on the next pass. Out of #942's scope by review ruling; tracked here.

issues.title: KV put reports success when publish times out or is refused
issues.body: Found in the Claude review of #973. A KV `put` returns OK even when its publish times out or is refused (this behaviour predates #973). Callers can't tell that a write never propagated. Proposal: surface a typed "stored locally, publish pending/failed" result, or a retry obligation.

issues.title: Encrypted task lists: ungated snapshot→seal→publish can seal under pre-removal epoch (#969 class)
issues.body:
Found in the Claude review of #973 (#969 fix). Encrypted group task lists (`src/.../tasks.rs:396`, added by #914) snapshot the group secret, seal, then publish without the #969 publication gate. So a task delta can be sealed under the pre-removal epoch after a member removal commits, and the removed member could then read it. This is the same class as #969, on the task-list path.

Fix: route task-list delta sealing through the same gate or epoch re-validation as encrypted KV (#973), with a deterministic race test that fails on the base.

issues.title: Encrypted KV: frame sealed under old epoch observed after leave/rekey/restart (flake or post-leave confidentiality bug?)
issues.body:
Seen on CI mirror #956 (run 36226516899, job "Encrypted KV transport proof"): `tests/encrypted_kv_transport.rs::encrypted_kv_leave_rekey_restart_has_only_sealed_transport_payloads` panicked at line 517: **"relevant transport frame rejected: old epoch"**. The frame inspector saw a relevant frame sealed under an epoch below `minimum_epoch` after the leave → rekey → restart sequence.

#920 (ACL REST/CLI) does not touch kv, groups or rekey, and the same job has recent passes on the candidate. So this is either:
- a test timing race (an in-flight pre-rekey frame captured by the inspector), or
- a **real confidentiality bug**: a frame emitted under the pre-leave epoch AFTER the rekey could be read by the member who left.

Ask: determine which. If a publish can seal under an old epoch after the local rekey has completed, that is a P1 (removed members could read post-leave content). If the frame was only in flight, tighten the test's window and document why. The owner is the KV rekey / #914 path.

issues.title: Port forwarder never FINs QUIC streams: TCP half-close hangs and stream tails are lost to reset
issues.body:
**Found 2026-09-26 by read-only analysis of `origin/codex/final-acceptance-candidate`.**

Both forwarding directions go through `bridge()` (`src/forward.rs:1052-1059`):
```rust
let to_stream = tokio::io::copy(&mut tcp_read, &mut send);
let from_stream = tokio::io::copy(&mut recv, &mut tcp_write);
let _ = tokio::join!(to_stream, from_stream);
```
- Outbound reaches it through `finish_outbound` (`forward.rs:1755-1756`), inbound through `into_split` (`forward.rs:1037-1038`).
- `tokio::io::copy` never calls `shutdown` (tokio 1.53.1 `copy.rs`), so `SendStream::poll_shutdown`, which would call `finish()` (ant-quic 0.27.53 `send_stream.rs:324`), is never reached.
- `PeerStream` (`streams.rs:429-516`) has no `AsyncWrite` or `Drop` of its own.
- ant-quic's `Drop` resets any unfinished stream with code `0xA17C0244` (`send_stream.rs:340-352`).

**Effects:**
1. A TCP EOF never becomes a QUIC FIN, so half-close doesn't propagate. A client that writes a request and then calls `shutdown(Write)` hangs, as in the common request/response pattern.
2. Every exit drops `send` unfinished, which resets the stream. Bytes written but not yet read by the peer are lost, so the tail of the data goes missing.
3. The denial byte (`forward.rs:967-970`, `991-996`) is followed by `return`, and the resulting reset can overtake it, so the opener gets a reset error instead of the diagnostic.

issues.title: Implement ADR-0074 tailnet phase 2: names, persistent forwards, SOCKS5, revocation teardown (R4)
issues.body:
Tracking issue for implementing Accepted ADR-0074 (merged in #958). It serves vision **R4**: a better-than-Tailscale way to reach your own machines and the machines others share with you.

Slices, in the ADR's order. Each slice lands as its own PR, with a CI mirror and a cross-model review.
- [ ] **Slice 0:** run the ignored tailnet stream/forward suites in CI, and produce the #132 relayed-path proof. The CI part is #936 (mirror #938); the #132 proof runs on the testnet.
- [ ] **Slice 1:** names `[agent:|machine:]<label>.<owner>`. Owner labels are local petnames pinned to a key at first use. Machine names come only from ADR-0041-enrolled machines. An ambiguous label fails with `AmbiguousKind`.
- [ ] **Slice 2:** forwards persist by default (`--ephemeral` opts out) in `forwards.json`, including `target_host` and `target_port`. A pinned forward must reach its `MachineId`: `PeerStream::peer()` is checked before the forward header is sent, and a mismatch fails closed.

- [ ] **Slice 4:** a SOCKS5 listener, off until configured and bound to loopback. It uses RFC 1929 username/password auth with the daemon's API token as the password (Q7); NO AUTH is refused. Port ranges are allowed only for `principal="owner"`.

issues.title: R17 egress: legacy DM bus bytes ~2.6-4x per node during Home (+ egress snapshot timing artifact)
issues.body:
Found by R17 testnet e2e; analysis is in omp-reports/takeover-20260921/802-r17-home-egress-ANALYSIS.md.

1. **Fixture artifact:** the Home egress check takes snapshot B 37 s into continuous work, and judges it on a trailing 60 s rate. R16 happened to take it after 120 s of idle, so it passed; R17 failed on all 5 nodes. Judge instead on `hard_exceeded` seconds, or bytes per operation, or take snapshot B at a fixed offset after the last operation.
2. **Real increase:** total bytes are about 1.8x R16 for comparable work, almost all on `x0x/dm/v1/bus`, the legacy DM topic every node floods. That is 2.6–4x per node (nyc 5.4 → 14.1 MB). Group-topic traffic is flat, so #899 is not the driver. The likely cause is #876/#878 control blobs that R16 dropped at the staging cap now completing. This is unproven, because the per-topic rows lack message kinds.

Asks:
- Add per-kind message counters for the legacy DM bus.
- A/B one Home pass with `skip_legacy_dm_bus = true`.
- Decide whether the legacy bus can carry cert-bearing control blobs at all.
- Fix the fixture's snapshot timing.

issues.title: Default Leaf forwards far beyond its egress budget (635 MB in 17 min, 0.45.0) — risk for mobile embedders
issues.body:
**Version:** x0xd 0.45.0

**Setup:** one ordinary desktop x0xd (`mode=leaf reason=default_leaf operator_relay=false`), subscribed to one low-rate probe topic plus the daemon's defaults, on the public bootstrap.

**Result:** in ~17 minutes it forwarded **635 MB in ~38k epidemic messages**, exceeding its egress hard budget **942 times** (194 "peer cooled" warnings). Its own probe publishes stopped reaching a subscribed peer (3/10 delivered, then 0/10 on fresh topics).

**Why it matters:** we embed x0x in mobile apps. A Leaf on a metered (cellular) link must not become a relay by volume — this rate would consume a phone data plan quickly.

**Expected:** a Leaf's subscribed-topic epidemic forwarding stays within `relay_fanout_budget_msgs_per_sec` / the egress budget, or embedders can opt out of forwarding.

**Asks:**
1. Which topics typically dominate `epidemic_forward_bytes` for a default Leaf?
2. Is the Leaf egress budget enforced, or observe-only (`src/gossip/egress.rs` header says "Observe-only Leaf egress accounting")?
3. Could there be a per-topic cap, or a "publish-only / no-forward" participation mode for mobile embedders?

Logs from the run are available on request.

issues.title: Primary installer (curl x0x.md | sh) installs binaries without checksum or signature verification
issues.body:
`scripts/install.sh` is the primary install path (`curl -sfL https://x0x.md | sh`, per its header). It downloads `https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/releases/latest/download/<tarball>` and extracts it with **no SHA-256 check and no signature check**. On origin/main, `grep -niE 'gpg|verify|sha256|checksum|\.sig|\.asc' scripts/install.sh` returns nothing. `.deployment/install.sh` is the same.

Every release already publishes `.asc` and `.sig` for each tarball, plus `SAORSA_PUBLIC_KEY.asc` (fingerprint `CEB3506E7DCB8A2DD2D679E8EDDA4827D89C0F29`). The Windows installer in #937 and `install.py` in #940 verify them; the shell installer doesn't.

**Fix:**
1. Verify the tarball's SHA-256 against the release checksum.
2. Verify the GPG signature against the pinned fingerprint when `gpg` is present.
3. Fail closed if verification fails.
4. If `gpg` is absent: decide whether to fail closed or verify the checksum only, with a loud warning. This needs David's call; the Windows installer fails closed unless `-SkipSignature` is given.
5. Add `install.sh` to the fingerprint-drift CI check from #940.

Serves R11 (onboarding): the recipe `x0x onboard` prints (#909) points new agents at this installer.

issues.title: scripts/install.py pins the wrong GPG fingerprint, so it rejects every real release
issues.body:
`scripts/install.py` (origin/main, line ~32) pins the release-signing fingerprint as `9D1F3C64B5D3C2F6B4A2E6D8A5C7F8E9D0B1A2C3`.

Verified 2026-09-26 with `gh release download -p SAORSA_PUBLIC_KEY.asc && gpg --show-keys --with-fingerprint`.

**Fix:** pin `CEB3506E7DCB8A2DD2D679E8EDDA4827D89C0F29`, as the new Windows installer (#937) does. Add a test or CI check that compares the fingerprints pinned in every installer (install.sh, install.ps1, install.py) against the released key, so this can't drift again.

issues.title: An unattested gossip DM claim still rebinds DirectMessaging (follow-up to #898)
issues.body:
When a gossip DM arrives with no origin-machine attestation and no authenticated binding, `dm_inbox.rs` (~1397-1424) accepts the sender-claimed `sender_machine_id`. It then `mark_connected`s that pairing unconditionally (~1631-1634), and `connect_to_agent` (lib.rs ~4984-5001) copies the `DirectMessaging` machine into the discovery cache.

An agent holding its own key can therefore steer its routing entry to any claimed machine. It can't forge a victim agent's DMs, and owner trust and share grants are unaffected, because they pair only via `AuthenticatedMachineBindings` (#911, #924). It is still a routing-state rebind primitive in the subsystem #898 hardened.

**Fix:** mirror #898. An unattested claim with no authenticated binding must not `mark_connected` or rebind. Still deliver the message, annotated as unverified. Only an attested origin or an authenticated binding may update routing.

**Tests:**
- An unattested claim from M2 for agent A, whether A is bound to M1 or unbound, leaves A's connected machine unchanged.
- An attested move still updates it.

Found by omp's security review of #924, finding 4.

issues.title: ShareGrant: grantee-attached grant_id fetch for missed deliveries (ADR-0070 §2)
issues.body:
Follow-up from ADR-0070 slice 3 (#924, Refs #891).

Slice 3 delivers grants by durable typed DM: the ACK is sent only after storage, the sender makes 3 idempotent retries, then reports failure. If a shared agent's daemon is offline through all attempts, it holds no grant and denies the grantee until the owner re-issues.

Implement ADR §2's fetch:
1. The grantee attaches received grant ids to DM/stream opens, on a carrier old peers ignore.
2. When the shared daemon sees an unknown id for its own agent, it fetches the grant from the grantee over a durable typed request/response, verifies it exactly as on delivery, and stores it.
3. Rate-limit and bound fetches per peer.
4. Alternatively or as well, add a durable owner-side redelivery outbox, like the public-group bootstrap outbox.

Tests:
- A daemon that was offline at issue time gains access after a later contact.
- A forged or foreign fetched grant is refused.
- Fetches are bounded.

Serves R5 (sharing a subset of agents).

issues.title: [release triage] Requester predecessor offer lacks durable retry after send exhaustion
issues.body:
The requester publishes a `JoinRequestCreated` metadata event and then spawns a one-shot direct message carrying the exact signed predecessor envelope to the authority. If `send_direct_with_config` exhausts its retries, the task only logs a warning; there is no persisted requester-side offer obligation to retry after the channel drains or the process restarts. This is separate from the authority-to-witness `predecessor_relay_outbox` repaired under #903.

Source on the #802 candidate at `8544f3a`: `src/server/routes/named_groups.rs:23635-23670` constructs and spawns the offer; the sender config at `:323-337` can use raw fallback. #903 is changing predecessor delivery to avoid false success on a full typed channel, which makes exhausted one-shot sends visible but does not make this initial offer durable.

Release triage before #802 merges to `main`:
- Verify whether the published metadata event independently causes the authority to recover and relay the predecessor envelope after a failed direct offer. Do not infer that from the send log alone.
- If there is no reliable recovery path, persist and retry the requester-to-authority offer with a stable identity until authority acceptance or terminal refusal.
- Add a Rule-9 regression that forces offer delivery failure, then restores capacity/restarts the requester and proves the authority receives the exact envelope once without losing the obligation.

Refs #903, #837, #802.

issues.title: #837 follow-up: full relay channel drops+ACKs predecessor offer; prefix routing misdiverts ordinary DMs
issues.body:
Follow-up to #837 (#815 raw typed dispatch). The code is already merged into the #802 candidate. Greptile scored #837 2/5 and raised two P1s; x0x-32 surfaced them on 2026-09-25. **Verify each one first, then fix before #802 lands on main.**

1. **Silent drop on a full predecessor-relay channel.** When the channel is full, `try_send` drops the payload but still returns `true`. The raw ACK then clears the sender's outbox retry, so the predecessor offer is lost with no retry. Expected: on a full channel, return false (no ACK), so the sender retries. Alternatively, apply backpressure without dropping.
2. **Prefix-only routing misdiverts ordinary DMs.** A verified ordinary DM whose bytes start with a registered typed prefix is routed to the typed consumer. If that consumer rejects it, the DM is lost. Expected: when a typed consumer rejects a payload as not-its-type, fall back to the generic DM path. Alternatively, use an unambiguous envelope discriminator.
3. **Known gap:** before the inbox service starts, raw payloads take the generic path. Document it, or queue the payloads until the service is ready.

Rule 9 tests: each fix needs a test that fails without it. For (1), a full channel must lead to no ACK and a retry that delivers. For (2), a DM with a colliding prefix must still be delivered.

issues.title: Raw Direct listener records unverified AgentId-to-MachineId bindings
issues.body:
## Trigger and current behavior

The raw Direct listener reads `sender: AgentId` from the first 32 payload bytes (`src/lib.rs` around 13127-13143). It computes `verified=false` when the identity-discovery binding is absent or points to a different transport machine (around 13159-13166). After the existing revocation, pairing, and expiry gates, it still calls `DirectMessaging::mark_connected(sender, machine_id)` unconditionally (around 13303).

A connected machine can therefore prefix a Direct payload with another non-revoked agent's ID and overwrite that agent's connected-machine entry even though the listener explicitly observed a binding mismatch. `connect_to_agent` can subsequently copy the DirectMessaging machine into the discovery cache (around 4894-4907). This can misroute reverse Direct sends and contaminate later reachability decisions. This is a binding-integrity bug; no payload-authentication or account-takeover claim is needed to reproduce it.

## Expected behavior

An unverified raw Direct claim must not update an authoritative AgentId-to-MachineId routing or identity binding. Keep any legacy handling of unverified message content explicit and separate from binding promotion. A verified move must still update routing, and revocation/pairing/expiry gates must continue to apply.

## Regression test

1. Establish a verified binding for agent A on machine M1 and a live unrelated machine M2.
2. Receive raw Direct bytes from M2 whose first 32 bytes claim A, with no auth

issues.title: Agents can show their human a specific view in the GUI, on any of their machines (R10)
issues.body:
## Requirement (R10)
An agent can bring up the GUI (or a browser window) **showing specific information** to its human, on whichever machine the human is using.

## Current state (origin/main)
- `x0x gui` (`src/bin/x0x.rs` ~L2012-2059) opens `/gui?token=…` on the agent's own machine only, and needs the owner's full API token.
- The GUI reads only `?token=`; no deep links to a view (DM thread, task list, file, store).
- None of the 183 endpoints lets an agent push/display a view; `/apps` agent-served pages are proposal-only (ADR-0057 §4).
- No cross-machine display; ADR-0039 rider sub-agents cannot obtain a GUI session (`rider_auth.rs` ~L119-126).
- GUI session token has a fixed 10-min expiry (`auth.rs` ~L415) and the GUI never refreshes → an open window likely stops working after 10 min (inferred from code; please confirm).

## Proposed scope
1. GUI deep links (`/gui#/dm/<id>`, `#/tasks/<id>`, `#/store/<id>/<key>`…) + session refresh.
2. `POST /gui/show {view, target_machine?}` + `x0x show …`: opens the view locally, or on the owner's active machine via owner-trust (ADR-0070).
3. Rider scope `gui:show`.

## Acceptance
An agent on machine A runs `x0x show tasks/<id>` and the human's browser on machine B opens that task list; window still works after 30 min.

issues.title: Calling: ship voice to users and decide video (R8)

## Requirement (R8)
Humans (and agents) can make audio **and video** calls.
