issues.title: Owner trust + share a subset of agents with another human (R5/R3/R7)
issues.body:
## Requirement (R5 / R3 / R7)
A human can share a **subset** of their agents with another human; the owner's own machines/agents are mutually reachable without hand-configuration; machine-resident agents are reachable by the owner's agents and by sharees.

## Current state (origin/main)
- No ADR, data model, endpoint or issue for sharing a subset of agents.
- Trust is per-AgentId with no UserId (`src/trust.rs` ~L106-133); no same-owner auto-trust.
- `owner_sync` enrollment grants no trust: `open_peer_stream` consults only `contact_store`.
- Connect/exec ACLs are exact (agent, machine) TOML lines loaded once at startup (`src/connect/acl.rs`, `src/exec/acl.rs`); no REST/CLI edit, no reload. `grep owner|enroll src/connect/` = 0.
- Today one cross-machine forward = exchange cards, mark Trusted both sides, edit root TOML, restart, `x0x forward add --peer <hex>`.

## Proposal
ADR-0070 (Proposed, draft PR to follow): owner-certified implicit trust + owner-signed `ShareGrant{owner, grantee, agents[], caps, expiry}` revoked via ADR-0018, enforced at DM / exec / connect / group admission; REST+CLI ACL management with hot reload. Slices: (1) owner trust, (2) ACL REST/CLI + reload, (3) ShareGrant.

## Acceptance
- Two machines of one owner can DM/exec/forward with zero manual trust/ACL steps; a non-owner agent is still denied.
- Owner grants agent A (not B) to user U: U's agents reach A, not B; revocation takes effect without restart.

Error bodies leak the fork_quarantine annotation to non-member session bearers before any membership or write check. `POST /groups/:id/send` (`named_groups.rs:14535`) returns 409 with the full annotation (`:21869`); encrypt/decrypt/reseal do the same (`:24822, :24966, :25049, :25291, :25456`). issues.title: Home: control-blob staging cap (4/peer, TTL-only release) exhausted by cert-carrying join events (#850) → membership events dropped, role update silently rejected
issues.body:
## Summary
This is a regression surfaced by #850 (the join carries an AgentCertificate). The Home join event is now ~51.5 KB, over the 49,152-byte DM limit (`src/dm.rs:43`), so it travels as a **staged control blob**. The owner allows only `PER_PEER_ENTRY_CAP = 4` staged blobs per recipient (`control_blob.rs:18`, refused at `:175`). Staged blobs are held for 10 min (`PENDING_JOIN_RESULT_TTL`, `named_groups.rs:31606`) and are removed ONLY by TTL, not when fetched. After two joins, sfo's 4 slots were full, so singapore's MemberAdded and join event were refused (`control blob staging budget exhausted`) and **dropped**. sfo then silently rejected singapore's role update because the member was unknown (`named_groups.rs:11338`, no log).

## Evidence (R15 synthetic Home, 2026-09-25 00:33Z)
- nyc: `WARN failed to direct-deliver named-group event: control blob staging budget exhausted` ×4, right after singapore's MemberAdded.
- sfo: last control-blob receipt 00:33:36; singapore absent from members_v2; the role PATCH never applied → Home 95/96 ("singapore admin role on sfo" timeout).
- R14 (no carried cert): only MemberAdded went as a blob → 3 blobs → fit.

Note: #850's size check asserted that a cert-carrying MemberJoined fits 49,152. The live event is 51,546 B, so that test used an unrepresentative cert or payload. Re-check it.

## Fix
1. Release a staged blob when its recipient has completed the fetch (or supersede older blobs for the same group). The cap should bound IN-FLIGHT blob

issues.title: Authz follow-up to #821: GET /groups/:id/delegations exposes member identities + fork_quarantine to non-member session bearers
issues.body:
## Summary
This is a follow-up to #821/#866. `GET /groups/:id/delegations` (`src/server/delegations.rs:1111-1114`, annotation at `:1200-1209`) serves `from_agent`/`to_agent` (member identities) plus the `fork_quarantine` annotation to a **non-member session bearer** whenever the group is `read_open`. `GET /groups/:id` now refuses that same caller (#866). The same data class needs the same gate. The `/history` fork-quarantine annotation (`history.rs:197`) hasn't been audited either.

## Ask
Apply the #866 session-bearer active-membership gate to delegations. Audit `/history`'s quarantine annotation. Add a Rule 9 test through the real auth middleware.

issues.title: Propagate stable transport ID through PubSubMessage and WebSocket events
issues.body:
## Problem

The live `/ws` `message` frame currently carries topic, payload, and optional origin, with no stable transport message identity. Its public-message listener receives a payload-only PubSub notification. `HistoryRecord.msg_id` identifies a local store record, and a decoded signed-group message can have an application-level canonical ID; neither is the authenticated gossip header ID. Computing `BLAKE3(payload)` would collapse distinct intentional sends with identical bytes.

## Requested behavior

Once [saorsa-gossip #100](https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-gossip/issues/100) exposes validated `MessageHeader.msg_id` in subscription metadata, carry it through x0x's PubSub notification path and emit it in a clearly named, documented WebSocket field distinct from history and application IDs. Define compatibility when upstream metadata is absent; do not invent an authenticated ID from payload bytes.

Acceptance: tests prove one transport message retains its ID across repeated local delivery, two same-payload messages with distinct header IDs remain distinct, and the live-frame and local-history IDs keep their separate meanings. Bounded WebSocket queues and gossip do not promise exactly-once delivery, gap detection, a complete feed, or durable receipt; those are out of scope.

The current client-facing limitation is documented in PR #868. This tracks the source follow-up separately from #822's intermittent stale pre-restart payload reproduction.

issues.title: Preserve validated MessageHeader.msg_id in subscription metadata
issues.body:
## Problem

The PubSub wire header has an authenticated `MessageHeader.msg_id`, but the local subscriber delivery API currently returns `(PeerId, Bytes)` and fans out only payload bytes. Downstream consumers cannot correlate a received notification with that transport message's validated ID. Hashing payload bytes is not equivalent: two intentional sends with identical bytes can have distinct header IDs.

## Requested behavior

Expose the already-validated header `msg_id` alongside peer and payload through a compatible or versioned subscription API. Define the trust behavior for legacy or invalid headers without promoting a synthesized payload hash as authenticated metadata. This is an identity/correlation change, not a delivery or completeness guarantee, and should not require a wire change.

Acceptance: subscriber tests retain the same ID for repeated delivery of one transport message, and distinguish two messages with identical payload bytes but distinct valid header IDs. Invalid or unvalidated IDs must not be exposed as trusted metadata.

Downstream x0x needs this for live WebSocket message identity; see [x0x #869](https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issues/869). The intermittent stale pre-restart payload symptom is separately tracked as [x0x #822](https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issues/822).

issues.title: Home wait-for-sync: rank-0 released by an empty session with a peer whose Home pointer is not yet published → duplicate (residual from #826)
issues.body:
## Summary
This is a residual gap from #826 (#824), flagged by Greptile and recorded as open in ADR 0069 (PR #862). The rank-0 creator is released by **any successful owner-sync session**. If that session is with a peer device that already HAS a Home but has not yet published its canonical Home pointer, the session succeeds empty and rank 0 creates a second Home: a duplicate.

## Fix direction
Release rank 0 only when the successful session proves no peer has a Home. For example, the session exchange carries a "has local Home / pointer pending" signal, or the peer's Home pointer is published before its session reports success, so an empty session isn't taken as proof of "no Home". Add a regression test: a peer with an unpublished Home plus rank 0 gives no duplicate.

issues.title: Pubsub eager fan-out skips all candidates (claim_skipped=6) after testnet daemon restarts; discovery announcements delayed 22-60s+ (R14)
issues.body:
## Summary
In R14 (#802 a9265758) the mesh fixture's pubsub announcement on `x0x.test.discover.v1` reached runners 22-59 s late, or not at all within 60 s. The anchor (nyc testnet daemon) logged `zero successful ordinary EAGER fan-out ... candidates=6 claim_skipped=6 attempted=0` at 20:39:57Z: every forwarding candidate was skipped (cooling, control budget, or not connected). This followed the private-kv fixture restarting the nyc, sfo, helsinki and nuremberg daemons 3.5 min earlier, including a forced exit on sfo. Direct messages worked throughout, with replies in 15-280 ms. R12 mesh passed 30/30; that run may not have followed restarts, so the comparison isn't like-for-like.

## Suspects
- #830 (priority-aware receive-pump shedding now drops Normal-topic control frames under pressure, which could slow GRAFT/PRUNE/IHAVE recovery), or
- the existing cooling machinery (#611 / sg#62-63) after mass restarts.

## Asks
- On the next run, capture the shed counters (#830) and the pubsub cooling and claim stats from `/diagnostics/gossip` on the anchor, before and after the fixture restarts.
- Determine why `claim_skipped` covers every candidate, and how long eager fan-out takes to recover after peer restarts.
- Harness (separate PR): discovery sends the announcement as a direct message to each runner's known agent id, with pubsub as a fallback, so fixture validity doesn't depend on pubsub recovery.

issues.title: Encrypted-store joiner convergence relies on slow repair (55–119 s on R12, >120 s on R14); silent drop paths + misleading checkpoint-subsumed WARN
issues.body:
## Summary
A freshly joined member of an encrypted (GSS) group converges a store value only through slow repair, not the live publish. On R12 the GSS fixture passed with little margin: sfo got owner-page after 54.6 s and nyc got member-page after **119.0 s**, against a 120 s deadline. On R14 (a9265758) it went over: sfo never saw owner-page in 120 s.

The R14 diagnosis found no rejection at sfo; every reject path WARNs and none fired. So the record was either never delivered live or dropped silently before merge. Candidates: the retained-image `Ok(None)` return (~src/kv/sync.rs:1489), or 30 s PubSub handler timeouts under load.

## Asks
1. Joiner cold-sync: after an encrypted store opens, the joiner's state-sync request and response should converge well under 120 s.
2. Log the sender and the specific reason for every Rejected (store.rs:2257, sync.rs:1572). Downgrade the checkpoint-subsumed Rejected, an echo of the owner's own checkpoint, back to debug as an idempotent no-op. Since #847 it shows up as a misleading WARN "encrypted delta rejected by content admission".
3. Rerun the GSS fixture with sfo at `RUST_LOG=warn,x0x::kv=debug`, to separate "never delivered" from "silently dropped".

Related: #811 (late-joiner history), #656 (load).

issues.title: SelfKeyed per-agent quota silently evicts the writer's highest-sorting key instead of refusing the 65th put (0.45.0)
issues.body:
## Summary

On x0x 0.45.0 the per-agent, per-store `SelfKeyed` quota (`MAX_SELFKEYED_KEYS_PER_AGENT = 64`) does not refuse a writer's 65th key. It admits the lexicographically lowest 64 of the writer's live keys and silently evicts the rest, so the `put` that causes an eviction returns success with no signal that an older key of the same writer just disappeared.

Source: `src/kv/store.rs` ~1700–1765 (`self_keyed_candidates` / `self_keyed_admitted`, `enforce_self_keyed_live_set`, `evict_outside_admitted`). A `403 AgentQuotaExceeded` is returned only when the NEW key itself sorts into the dropped tail.

The lowest-N rule is deterministic (every replica converges on the same admitted subset), which is a sound design property. The gap is observability: the writer learns of the eviction only later, via a `404` on `get_value` or the key's absence from `list_keys`.

## Reproduction (two embedded daemons, 0.45.0)

1. On a fresh `SelfKeyed` store, one agent writes 64 keys with segments `"0"` … `"63"` (unpadded decimal strings).
2. The same agent writes a 65th key, segment `"64"`. The `put` succeeds.
3. `list_keys` for that agent now returns 64 keys: `"64"` is present and `"9"` (the lexicographically highest of the original set, since `"7"`, `"8"`, `"9"` sort after every `"6…"` segment) is gone. No error, no event.

## Impact for clients

A client that keys a paged directory as `<agent>/catalog/p<ix>` + `<agent>/catalog/index` gets string ordering (`"p10" < "p2"`, `"index" < "p0"`), an

issues.title: SECURITY: TreeKEM catch-up adopts intervening commits without checking the pending owner attestation (forking responder)
issues.body:
`handle_treekem_catchup_response` (`src/server/routes/named_groups.rs` ~9514-9570) checks only that the responder is an active member of the joiner's current (stub) view. It then applies the intervening commits through the normal path **without checking them against the pending owner v2 attestation**. So a forking responder's intermediates could be adopted before the queued terminal fails to link. This is pre-existing on main, and was found in the #839 security review.

Fix: check that the served intervening chain leads to the attested head, i.e. the owner v2 attestation binds the terminal and its parent before anything is adopted; or hold the intervening commits until the terminal links. Add a test where a forking responder serves divergent intermediates and nothing is adopted.

issues.title: Owner sync: every session between mutually-enrolled owner devices fails 'stream reset by peer 0xA17C0244' (R12); initiator errors hidden at debug
issues.body:
## Summary
In the R12 synthetic Home run (the first run with mutually enrolled owner devices, from #826), **every** owner-sync session failed in both directions: 21 on nyc and 19 on sfo, all `Tier-1 sync session failed (fail closed) … sync io error: stream reset by peer: error 2709258820` (0xA17C0244, the peer drops the stream before finishing). Initiator-side failures log only at debug level (`src/owner_sync.rs:2403`), so the cause isn't visible. The wait-for-sync from #826 fell back to the group advertisement, so Home still resolved, but owner sync (and therefore the canonical pointer via sync) is non-functional between these devices.

## Ask
- Raise initiator failure logging to WARN, with the error class.
- Root-cause the peer-side stream reset (0xA17C0244): the responder refusing because of enrollment mismatch, a protocol/version check, or a session-limit or quiesce interaction?
- Add a two-device owner-sync session test that completes successfully.

issues.title: Home join rejected 'no agent certificate resolved' when the joiner's cert announce didn't propagate — join should carry the verifiable AgentCertificate (#447 class)
issues.body:
## Summary
The owner rejects a certified same-owner device's Home join with `rejecting uncertified joiner (ADR-0038 OwnerCertified) … reason=no agent certificate resolved`. It retries about every 2 s for the whole 120 s window. The owner resolves joiner certs only from its discovery cache and announce-blob cache (`src/server/routes/named_groups.rs:20788-20890`, failing at `src/groups/owner_cert.rs:291`). If the joiner's certificate announce didn't propagate, nothing re-sends it until the next identity heartbeat (600 s). This is the #447 class of bug, on R12 (#802 71cb9544).

## Evidence (R12 synthetic Home, 2026-09-24)
- sfo announced at ~14:31:25 (200) and joined at 14:36:59, over both gossip and a raw-QUIC acked DM.
- nyc refused it 100 times until 14:38:59.
- nyc's `announce-blob-cache.bin` contains helsinki/nuremberg/singapore's `agent.cert` but not sfo's.
- The fixture's readiness check asks sfo itself for `/agent/user-id` (`tests/e2e_vps_private_kv.py:68`), not the owner's view, so it can't catch this.

## Fix
- **Preferred:** the join event carries the joiner's AgentCertificate. It's self-verifiable against the policy owner (`verify_cert_against_owner`), so no extra trust is added. The owner verifies it inline.
- **Alternatives:** on a `NoCertificate` refusal, the owner pulls the joiner's announce blob directly; or the joiner re-announces with its cert when it starts a join.
- **Fixture:** gate seat minting on the owner's view of each device's cert.
- **Test:** the own

issues.title: TreeKEM Welcome: joiner discards an already-received Welcome when its FetchRequest ACK times out (joiner-side twin of #825)
issues.body:
## Summary
This is the joiner-side twin of #825. When the joiner's own Welcome **FetchRequest** delivery ACK times out (24 s, over the gossip inbox, which runs 19-24 s under load), the fetch attempt gives up: `cleanup_welcome_fetch_state` plus an early return at `src/server/routes/named_groups.rs:33911`. That happens **before it reads the result channel**, so it throws away a Welcome that had already been fully received, and it deletes the receive state. Chunks that arrive during the retry sleep are then silently dropped (`chunk_recv_no_pending`, debug level only). A repeated FetchRequest is ignored while the old owner stream is still waiting for final ACKs (~:34079), so the join ends up stuck in `pending_authority_commit`.

## Evidence (R12 private fixture, singapore, welcome_id 6b02910d…, 14:18-14:20Z)
- The owner accepted the join and committed MemberAdded at 14:18:04.
- Stream A delivered both chunks over raw QUIC plus a Complete-sized frame by 14:18:44.
- Attempt 1 then logged `fetch_retry_failed … timed out` at 14:18:57 and discarded it.
- Stream B, with #828 in effect ("streaming chunks anyway"), arrived while no receive state existed.
- Result: timeout. #828 works on the owner side; this is the remaining joiner-side half.

## Fix
1. Joiner: a FetchRequest ACK timeout logs a warning and **keeps waiting** on the result channel for the attempt's full window. No cleanup, no return.
2. Owner: a repeated FetchRequest restarts or re-sends the stream instead of being ignored

issues.title: GSS encrypted KV merge: writer authorization checked before store lock (same TOCTOU as #806)
issues.body:
## Summary
The same check-then-merge TOCTOU as #806 exists on the GSS encrypted path. `merge_encrypted_record` checks `is_authorized_writer` at `src/groups/sync.rs:1467`, awaits `store.write()` at :1496, and merges at :1508. A writer revoked between the check and the merge can still land a record. #834 fixes only the signed-public path. The TreeKEM production path already does this correctly: `stores.rs:1078-1089` takes the membership lock, re-checks, then takes the store lock.

## Ask
Re-validate authorization under the store lock, mirroring #834's `kv_context` final check (versioned generation, state read guard held through apply). Add a regression test for revocation between check and merge on the GSS path.

Found in Claude's review of #834.

issues.title: TreeKEM Welcome-blob stream aborts on a single Offer ACK timeout → joiner stuck pending (private join fails under load)
issues.body:
## Summary
In the TreeKEM Welcome-blob transfer, when the Offer's DM receipt times out, `stream_welcome_blob` removes the ACK slot and **returns without sending any chunks** (`src/server/routes/named_groups.rs:34073-34076`). The joiner may have received the Offer anyway. Its fetch retries then time out (`fetch_retry_failed … timed out waiting for TreeKEM Welcome blob`), and the join sticks at `pending_authority_commit` even though the owner accepted it and committed MemberAdded.

The Welcome control messages (FetchRequest, Offer, ChunkAck, Complete) are forced onto the gossip-inbox path with `prefer_raw_quic_if_connected: false` (~33751-33764). Under load, those round trips go over the ~12 s per-attempt ACK window, while the raw-QUIC commit is delivered fine.

## Evidence
R11 private-KV testnet fixture, 2 of 2 runs, joiner singapore:
- nyc logs `failed to send Welcome blob offer: timed out after 1 retries over 24.0s`, then `failed to send Welcome blob complete`;
- singapore logs `welcome.trace stage="fetch_retry_failed"`;
- the owner roster includes singapore, but the joiner never seats.
Receipts: `omp-reports/takeover-20260921/802-r11-private-a{1,2}-*`.

## Fix direction
- Don't abort the stream on an Offer receipt timeout: keep streaming the chunks, or let the joiner's FetchRequest retry restart the stream idempotently.
- Consider sending Welcome control frames raw-QUIC-preferred when a connection is already cached as connected, since the commit uses that path successfully.

issues.title: Home: owner-key-copied admin device auto-provisions a duplicate Home; ~ then mints invites into the wrong Home (200 ok)
issues.body:
## Summary
A same-owner device that gets the copied owner key and restarts creates its **own** Home, because its canonical Home pointer hasn't synced yet. Later it joins the owner's Home and ends up seated in two Home groups. `POST ~` on that device then returns **200 ok with an invite into the duplicate Home**, not the owner's canonical Home.

## Evidence (R11 synthetic Home e2e, reproduced 2/2: a1, a2)
- The owner (nyc) promotes singapore to Admin. singapore mints the seat for the late device helsinki.
- The response is 200, ok true, owner_user_id and intended_joiner correct, seated false, **but group_id ≠ the canonical Home**.
- singapore's `GET /home` reports state `local` with the duplicate's group_id.
- Receipts: `omp-reports/takeover-20260921/802-r11-home-seat-diag-a2.json`, `802-r11-home-diag-report-a{1,2}.json`.

## Mechanism
1. `provision_home` (src/server/routes/home.rs:780) runs on the post-certification restart. Its duplicate guard `effective_canonical_home` sees no pointer yet, so step 4 (~944-955) creates a new Home.
2. `seat_home` → `resolve_home` (:320) prefers the canonical Home only if the pointer is known and the device is seated in it. Otherwise `find_home` picks the smallest stable id, which can be the duplicate.
3. It mints at :1576, and `seated` is hard-coded to false at :1636.

## Fix direction
- `seat_home` refuses with 409 (`ambiguous` / `adoption_pending`) when duplicates exist and the canonical pointer is unknown or doesn't match. It must

issues.title: Intermittent: public_pubsub_key_cache_full_ref_restart_recovery receives pre-restart payload (~15%, pre-existing)
issues.body:
## Summary
`public_pubsub_key_cache_full_ref_restart_recovery` (CI job "Gossip key-cache transport proof", Integration & Soak Tests workflow) fails intermittently, about 4 of 25 recent runs. The failure is `tests/gossip_key_cache_transport.rs:185` with `application payload mismatch`: the receiver gets the **pre-restart** payload (`initial-0`) where it expects `after-restart-0`. One older run failed at :234.

## Evidence
It failed on these #802 lineage heads:
- 1fb7f4cd (:234)
- d02f5867
- aa3d4c67
- ee090829 (#816 branch)

It passed on dc34264b, b2b2a746, 259ebb55, 9b7ba64b and others. The failures predate the #807/#812/#816 changes, so it is pre-existing.

## Why it matters
Receiving an older message where the post-restart one is expected could be a real stale-replay or dedup defect in key-cache full-ref recovery (sg `handle_key_cache_control`, retained or ref'd messages across a restart), not just test timing. It needs a mechanism before it can be labelled a flake.

issues.title: Authz review: GET /groups/:id exposes invite_lineage + roster to any session bearer without per-group membership check (LOW)
issues.body:
`GET /groups/:id` returns the full `invite_lineage` (now including `anchored_gap_refusal`) and the roster to any API/session bearer, with no per-group membership check. It isn't exposed to arbitrary peers, since a bearer or session is required and riders are excluded. Under the single-operator model this is LOW, but it should get an authz review of which fields a session token may read per group.

Found in OMP's security re-review of #816.

issues.title: SECURITY: non-TreeKEM owner-group across-gap adoption accepts parent-only (v1) join attestation — sibling-terminal replay
issues.body:
## Summary
The owner join-head attestation v1 (`x0x.join-head-attest.v1`) signs the **parent** head, not the terminal. #816 adds a v2 terminal-bound signature (`x0x.join-terminal-attest.v2`: v1 fields plus terminal `state_hash`, `committed_by` and TreeKEM epoch) and requires it on the new TreeKEM stale-base anchor.

The **existing across-gap adoption path for non-TreeKEM owner groups still accepts v1 alone.** So the same attack OMP found on #816 may apply there:
- an active admin builds a divergent sibling terminal on the same parent;
- they serve it together with the owner's genuine v1 attestation;
- the adoption accepts the sibling.

## Ask
- Confirm the threat on that path, with a test: sibling-terminal plus genuine-attestation replay on a non-TreeKEM owner group.
- Require v2 there as well, falling back to the pre-adoption behaviour when v2 is absent. Decide the mixed-fleet policy.

Found during OMP's security review of #816. Related: #816, #818.

issues.title: Typed-payload routes are bypassed on the raw-QUIC inbound path (0.45.0) — ADR 0028 predecessor offer silently dropped, request/approve admission wedges
issues.body:
## Summary

On x0x 0.45.0, typed-payload routes (including `GROUP_PREDECESSOR_RELAY_DM_PREFIX`) are registered and dispatched only on the gossip DM-inbox receive path (`DmInboxService::route_typed_payload`, `dm_inbox.rs:1631-1684`). The raw-QUIC inbound loop (`lib.rs:12884-12945`) calls `dm.handle_incoming(...)` and unconditionally publishes the payload as a plain broadcast; it never calls `route_typed_payload`.

`send_direct_with_config` chooses raw QUIC whenever the sender's `capability_store` has no usable entry for the recipient (`capability_lookup … hit=false gossip_ok=false source="none" capability_store_entries=0`), and `prefer_raw_quic_if_connected = false` is only consulted after that lookup, so it does not prevent the fallback (`lib.rs:6126-6167`). The send returns `Ok` (path `raw_quic_acked`), so the sender sees no error.

Consequence for GSS `MlsEncrypted` (`public_request_secure`) named groups: `create_join_request` (`named_groups.rs:21085-21110`) sends the requester→authority predecessor offer exactly once with this config. If the capability store has not converged at that moment, no `PredecessorRelayObligation` is stored on the authority, and `approve_join_request`'s B8 precondition (`named_groups.rs:21157-21344`) refuses with 412 `"predecessor obligation not found — JoinRequestCreated not yet received"` indefinitely. A second `POST /groups/:id/requests` returns 409 `"pending request already exists"` (`named_groups.rs:20990-20996`), so the requester cannot re-s

issues.title: Private KV: late joiner never receives a store's history from a plain member when owner+admin are offline (testnet, R9 and R10)
issues.body:
## Summary
In the private-KV testnet fixture, a late joiner (helsinki) never receives the **web** store's owner value within 120 s once the owner (nyc) and the admin (nuremberg) are offline. The only online member holding the history is sfo, a plain member. This reproduced on R9 (#802 90662c6) and on R10 (b2b2a746). The testnet daemons are Full, so this is not #807. - Helsinki rejected history pages with `too many retained images are awaiting pages` at 01:15:21, 01:16:44, 01:16:52 and 01:16:59. The cap is 4 in-flight images per store for 120 s, and they can't be evicted across sender or epoch. The line doesn't name the store, so it can't be attributed.
- Journals are at WARN level, so there are no lines about `7933833b` on helsinki or sfo.

2. Decide whether the late-joiner catch-up SLO is below 120 s. If so, fix the backoff or the retained-image cap interaction; if not, document it and change the fixture deadline, with justification.
3. Rerun with debug logging of sto

issues.title: Receive pump sheds Critical IHAVE above 90% PubSub-queue occupancy, undermining #807 lazy repair under saturation
issues.body:
## Summary
x0x's receive pump drops **all** control-kind frames, IHAVE included, when PubSub-queue occupancy is above 90%. It does this *before* any priority-aware processing (`src/network.rs:868-873`, `1511-1529`). Under #656-class saturation, an IHAVE a sender recorded as handed off can therefore be discarded at the receiver, even for **Critical** topics such as `x0x/dm/v1/*`. Sender-side `ShedNormal` structurally protects Critical IHAVE; this receive-side path does not.

## Why it matters now
#808 (the #807 fix) makes lazy IHAVE/IWANT repair the recovery path for Leaf peers beyond the eager degree, including a directly connected DM or join recipient that isn't in the eager set. A saturated receiver can still lose that repair, so #807's black-hole could come back in a narrower form under load.

Normal and Bulk lazy repair also depend on deferrable IHAVE with bounded retries (a 1024 pending-ID cap).

## Ask
- Make the receive-pump shed priority-aware: never discard Critical control frames (IHAVE/IWANT for Critical topics) before classification.
- Test: lazy repair of a Critical-topic publish succeeds with the receive queue above 90% occupancy. No current test covers this.

Found in OMP's cross-model review of #808 (2026-09-24). Related: #807, #808, #504, #656.

issues.title: Leaf eager-set truncation by PeerId byte order black-holes DM-inbox/join envelopes to directly-connected recipients
issues.body:
## Summary
On a **Leaf** node, x0x fills each topic's PlumTree eager set from `connected_peer_ids()` through `ordered_topic_peers` → `ordered_leaf_peers`. That function sorts by **PeerId bytes**, optionally puts one Full/bootstrap peer first, and then **truncates to `leaf_max_eager_degree` (default 2)**. saorsa-gossip `set_topic_peers` keeps only that list, so truncated peers are neither eager nor lazy and never receive an IHAVE. A local publish then goes only to those ≤2 peers. If they are Leaf nodes not subscribed to the topic, they refuse the frame (#380 C0 participation gate), so the message is **black-holed with no error**. In an all-Leaf neighbourhood, whether a DM-inbox envelope or join request reaches its recipient depends on how the machine-key bytes sort.

Present since 0.41.4 (#544, #504 leaf ceiling). Production v0.45.0 is affected (`src/gossip/pubsub.rs:1924-1959`, `src/gossip/config.rs:107`).

## Evidence (R9 candidate #802, synthetic Home e2e, 2026-09-23)
- sfo (Leaf) sent a 33 KB Home join envelope on nyc's DM-inbox topic. sfo and nyc were **directly connected**, and 58 small raw-QUIC DMs sfo→nyc were all acknowledged.
- Byte-order sort of sfo's connected peers: sgp 3133…, nue 7084…, hel 7aaf…, nyc c9f2…. The top 2 were sgp and nue; nyc was excluded. nyc's own list (for nyc→sfo) excluded sfo the same way.

issues.title: KV: retained-image merge validates writer authorization before the store lock (pre-existing TOCTOU window, P3)
issues.body:
Pre-existing, narrow authorization window found during the #804/#805 shared-KV recovery work (adjudication: `omp-reports/takeover-20260921/805-preexisting-auth-race-adjudication-sol6.md`, Sol GPT-6).

**Where:** `src/kv/sync.rs` `merge_group_signed_record` (~1264–1299 on `codex/804-public-revision-recovery`). Ordinary deltas re-check writer authorization **under the store lock**; retained images refresh the shared public context and verify signature, exact revision and roster **before** the await that takes the lock. A writer revoked (public group revision change) during that suspension can still have a retained image applied.

**Severity:** P3 — narrow window, retained images only; not introduced by #802/#805.

**Suggested fix:** after acquiring the store lock, compare the `PublicAuthorizationVersion` (a generation counter, not just `authorization_binding()`, which misses an A→B→A cycle) against the one captured at validation, and re-validate or reject if it changed. Add a regression test that revokes the writer between validation and apply.

Not a blocker for the #802 release; track for follow-up.

**Defect.** `KvStoreHandle::retire` only cancels. Most production callers cannot drain because they hold `kv_stores`/membership locks while the listener's lifecycle section may be waiting on those same locks (deadlock): `server/routes/stores.rs` — `create_kv_store`, `join_kv_store`, `join_self_keyed_store`, `create_group_kv_store` (registration rollback), `retire_group_kv_stores` (leave/withdraw/delete), `public_kv_refresh`, `gss_kv_refresh`. Old and new syncs have independent lifecycle/persist gates, so one persist admitted by the OLD sync before cancel can land after the new sync/import wrote — stale overwrite of newer state.

**Fix shape (Codex).** Retain retirement state (tombstone/reservation keyed by snapshot path), release membership/registry locks, drain the old sync, and only then permit a re-open of that path. Merely releasing locks before draining introduces a different reuse race.

**Also:** `KvStoreSync::stop` unsubscribes without draining; an OwnerAnnounce waiting behind persistence blocks subsequent responder requests (throughput nit).

issues.title: Happy Eyeballs cancellation leaves spawned dial attempts running
issues.body:
When an outer timeout or caller cancellation drops `happy_eyeballs::race_connect`, its pending dial tasks continue running. The race owns a `Vec<JoinHandle<()>>`, and only the success paths call `abort_all`; dropping the handles detaches their tasks. The direct-connect path wraps this race in an outer timeout, so returning from that timeout does not cancel the spawned attempts.

Observed in source at commit `4264c345cffe29ad04463fa9c2ee8a2492a38fc2`: [race ownership and exit paths](https://github.com/saorsa-labs/ant-quic/blob/4264c345cffe29ad04463fa9c2ee8a2492a38fc2/src/happy_eyeballs.rs#L299). This predates and is separate from PR #293.

Expected: every spawned attempt remains owned by the race and is aborted when the race exits or is dropped. Preserve winner selection and all-attempts-failed behavior.

A repair and two inert regression tests are prepared locally. Validation is pending: each test waits until a pending mock dial has entered, cancels or times out the race, then requires its drop witness within a bounded interval. A separate baseline fixture will verify these tests fail on the original implementation. No sockets are needed for this reproduction.

- If subset-resilience runs remain useful, make them an explicit option consistent with Phase B and label the result as partial, unsuitable for fleet-release acceptance.
- Preserve `--nodes` support for deliberately selected complete smaller inventories.

issues.title: Direct-dial budget (rtt*4+750ms, 1s floor) is ~2.08s by default against measured 5.9s dials under CPU contention
issues.body:
## Summary

The direct-connection budget in `connection_strategy.rs:222-240` is computed as `rtt * 4 + 750 ms`, clamped to a **1 s** floor. With the default RTT estimate of 333 ms that yields a budget of roughly **2.08 s** — against a **measured 5.9 s loopback dial** under 5x CPU contention. The dial is aborted with a terminal `ConnectionFailed` well before it could have succeeded.

The arithmetic is **identical in 0.27.48 and 0.27.52**, so nothing in the recent lifecycle work (#278/#280/#283/#286/#288) changes it.

## Why this is not a CI-only curiosity

It surfaced through x0x #623 as a Happy-Eyeballs abort under CPU contention, which reads like a test-environment artefact. It is not: on the x0x production bootstrap fleet, **each host runs three `x0xd` daemons on two vCPUs and sits at 1.6–4.6% idle**, with the primary daemon spending 63 s running against 94 s waiting for CPU per 90 s window (`schedstat`, wait/run 1.49). CPU contention is the *steady state* on those hosts, not an anomaly — so a budget tuned for an idle machine is being applied to a permanently contended one.

A dial that needs 5.9 s on a contended host and is given 2.08 s fails deterministically, and the failure is terminal rather than retried.

## What would settle it

Measure actual dial completion time across a contention range (1x, 2x, 5x oversubscription) and compare against the computed budget at each point. That answers whether the floor is simply too low, or whether the `rtt * 4` scaling is the wrong

issues.title: #501 meter: the in-test oracle counts eager+IHAVE, derive-legacy-bus-attempts.py still counts eager bytes only — a pure-IHAVE run passes the test and is reported as an oracle failure
issues.body:
Found while investigating #613 (see PR #706, side finding 2). Filing separately so it is not lost in that thread.

## The divergence

#674 moved the in-test D5/O5 oracle from "eager bytes" to **active dissemination = eager + IHAVE**, because eager re-publish is no longer the only bus forwarding mechanism: a relay whose `RelayFanout` verdict goes `LazyForward` (C2 unconsumed topic, or C3 budget exhausted) withholds the eager send and announces via IHAVE instead, and peers pull by IWANT.

`src/legacy_bus_interop_tests.rs` (the in-test oracle):

```rust
if delta(&a, &b, &["eager", "ihave"])? == 0 {
    return Err("FAIL: D5 recorded no bus dissemination (eager or IHAVE)".into());
}
```

`scripts/ci/derive-legacy-bus-attempts.py:239` (the CI derivation tool, unchanged):

```python
delta = deltas.get(BUS, {}).get("eager", {}).get("bytes", 0)
if (arm == "D5" and delta == 0) or (arm == "O5" and delta != 0):
    oracle_failures.append(arm + "_EAGER_ORACLE")
```

## Why it matters

The two now disagree in both directions on the same record:

- **False alarm.** A run where D5 disseminates purely via IHAVE under a `LazyForward` verdict passes the test and is reported by the derivation tool as `D5_EAGER_ORACLE`. The tool exits 1 on `derivation == "FAIL"`, so this is a red CI signal for a run that is correct by the current oracle.

issues.title: Run Benchmarks gate produces false regressions by construction (mock benches, head-of-master baseline, cross-runner comparison, no CI)
issues.body:
## Summary

The `Run Benchmarks` job can fail a PR with a large, confident-looking "performance regression" that does not exist. This was found while investigating PR #275, whose red check reported `event_processing/process_events` at +166% to +226% across four sizes. There was no regression. Filing separately from #275 so the design problem is tracked whatever happens to that PR.

## Four defects, in descending order of severity

**1. It gates merges on benchmarks that cannot observe this crate.** `benches/connection_management.rs` is a self-contained mock: it defines its own `enum ConnectionEvent { _Connected(()), _Disconnected(()), … }` — every payload `()` — and pushes/pops them on a bench-local `Arc<RwLock<VecDeque>>`. Its only ant-quic import is `use ant_quic::PeerId;`, a `[u8; 32]` newtype. It measures `std` `VecDeque`/`Vec`/`RwLock`. No commit to this repository can move these numbers, so any movement they show is by definition not about our code.

**2. It baselines against head-of-master rather than the PR's merge-base.** In the #275 run the baseline resolved to master @ `be19c822` (v0.27.52) while "current" was the PR head branched from `f2f1934f` (0.27.49), **29 commits behind**. Older code was graded against newer, so the reported regression was the intervening fixes read upside down. Under this design, *any* branch that falls behind master is failed for being behind master.

**3. The two sides are built in different jobs on different runners, with no same-commit

issues.title: test_slow_subscriber_isolated_at_100k_messages consumes the full 600s terminate-after ceiling and is killed
issues.body:
## Observation

In a full `--lib --run-ignored all` suite run on 2026-09-13, `gossip::pubsub::tests::test_slow_subscriber_isolated_at_100k_messages` hit the nextest `terminate-after` ceiling and was killed, making the suite exit 100.

The ceiling is 600 s: `.config/nextest.toml` `[profile.default]` sets `slow-timeout = { period = "60s", terminate-after = 10 }`. So this single test consumes ten minutes of every full-suite run and is then terminated, against a total suite wall time of 608 s.

## Why this may not be merely a slow test

The test (`src/gossip/pubsub.rs:2879`) publishes 100,000 messages to a deliberately slow subscriber and asserts that the slow subscriber is **isolated** rather than allowed to stall the manager. If it never completes, the most economical explanation is that the isolation under test is not happening — which would be a product defect in exactly the area that matters for fleet memory and CPU, not a test-harness inconvenience.

It is also possible it is simply an expensive test that has quietly exceeded its budget. Both are worth knowing; neither is currently tracked.

## What is known and what is not

- **Known:** observed once, terminated at the ceiling, in a run against **ant-quic 0.27.50** (a deliberate control pin), from a worktree whose only source edit was confined to `src/server/routes/named_groups/tests/hs_f2_membership_cluster.rs`. So it is not caused by that edit, and it is not caused by anything in ant-quic 0.27.51/0.27.52.
- **Not known:*

issues.title: The ambient-suite-load attribution behind the .config/nextest.toml #316/#510 overrides is unverified — one direct measurement points the other way
issues.body:
The `.config/nextest.toml` overrides for #316, #510 and ADR-0030 slice 3 all rest on one causal claim: that these tests fail because of **ambient suite load starving their timing windows**. The file states it twice:

- line 57: "the trigger is ambient suite load starving their timing windows, not group-internal contention"
- line 71: "the trigger here is ambient load from the ~2600 ungrouped tests starving the dial's timing window"

That attribution is the justification for the `threads-required = 4` scheduler reservations and for the `membership-cluster` / `quic-localhost` `max-threads` caps. As far as I can tell it has never been measured directly — it was inferred from "green in isolation, red under a full run", which is consistent with ambient load but also with several other explanations (port/address reuse collisions, shared `/tmp` state, ordering effects, or simply more total opportunities for a low-rate race to fire).

## Evidence from #692 that points the other way

While establishing the negative control for #692 (retiring the #684 settle-barrier workaround), I ran the hs_f2 restart tests with the workaround **removed** and ant-quic pinned to **=0.27.50** — i.e. the pre-ant-quic#283-fix control, the configuration in which the defect demonstrably reproduces.

In that configuration, one full `cargo nextest run --all-features --lib --run-ignored all` pass (3071 tests, all the ambient load the suite has to offer):

| test | under full suite | isolated single-test run |

issues.title: dedupe concurrency test: assert verify.count >= 2 to pin the overlap it depends on
issues.body:
Non-blocking nit from the PR #67 round-2 review.

`concurrent_same_msg_id_frames_admit_exactly_once` now genuinely discriminates the post-verify double-check (breaking it fails the test 5/5). But it asserts only `verify.count >= 1`, which does not pin the *overlap* the test depends on: if pre-signing were ever removed or the racers otherwise serialised, verify would collapse to 1 and the test would still pass while exercising nothing — exactly the failure mode round 1 had.

Measured profile over 10 instrumented runs is stable at 32 probes / 24 hits / 8 verify / 1 admission, so `verify.count >= 2` pins the overlap with a large margin. One-line change. Refs #58.

issues.title: shutdown: the canonical connections drain sits outside the lifecycle sweep's lock
issues.body:
Moderate follow-up from the PR #288 round-2 review; **pre-existing on master**, not introduced by #288.

The canonical `connections` drain happens outside the lock the lifecycle sweep holds, so a registration that holds the lifecycle lock across the drain can leave one already-closed connection in the winner map. It cannot produce the stale `is_connected` symptom that x0x#692 cares about (that path is now gated), but it is a genuine ordering gap.

Fix: move the canonical drain inside the sweep's critical section so both maps are cleared under one lock.

Two minor notes from the same review, worth folding in: the shutdown gate is a process-global that an early assert can leave armed, and two comments in `shutdown()` overstate what the join guarantees. Refs #286, #283.

issues.title: cooling floor: the #32-before-replacement ordering is unguarded by any test
issues.body:
Non-blocking finding from the PR #64 round-2 review.

PR #64 round 1 ran the new graft-eligible replacement gate *before* the #32 last-peer check, which silently reduced the zero-fan-out protection from two layers to one. Round 2 reordered it correctly (`cooling_floor_blocks_at`: #32 last-peer arm first and unexempted at `lib.rs:3739`, then the replacement gate at `:3746`, then the widening at `:3752`).

**But nothing pins that ordering.** Re-introducing the exact round-1 ordering in a scratch tree passes the whole suite, 249/249 — the new Dead test exercises `cooling_floor_last_peer_blocks_at`, a separate single-arm function with no ordering to get wrong, and neither #62 leg reaches the ordering either. So the invariant that was the round-1 blocker can regress silently.

One short test closes it: with the **last eligible eager peer** and a **graft-eligible lazy peer present**, assert the floor blocks the demotion. That fails under the round-1 ordering and passes under the shipped one. Refs #62, #32.

issues.title: relay fan-out: per-topic validator/bucket state grows monotonically on relays; nothing clears it
issues.body:
Non-blocking finding from the PR #695 review (#674 C2/C3).

On a relay, `registered`, `buckets` and saorsa-gossip's `topic_validators` now gain an entry per topic and never lose one: sg's idle-topic reaper (pubsub `lib.rs:8377`) does not touch validators, and x0x never calls `clear_topic_validator`. A bootstrap sees a large and open-ended set of topics (tag shards alone are 65,536 possible PlumTree topics), so this is unbounded in principle.

Not a merge blocker — each entry is small and the monitor already ships as `relay_fanout.topics` on `GET /diagnostics/gossip`. But it must be watched: **sample `relay_fanout.topics` alongside RSS after the 0.43.x fleet rollout**, and if the topic count climbs without bound, wire an eviction (drop the composite and its bucket when sg reaps the topic, or an LRU keyed on last-use) and have sg clear the validator in its reaper.

Refs #674, #656, saorsa-gossip#59.

issues.title: Bulk-priority topics can never self-recover from cooling: post-expiry suppression state is fed into admit_bulk's drop, so the recovery probe is unreachable
issues.body:
Found while root-causing x0x#611 (pubsub 0.5.78). Separate defect from the cooling floor issue filed alongside this one.

**Mechanism.** `filter_peers_through_admission_in_state` (`lib.rs:2124`) feeds post-expiry suppression state into `admit_bulk`, which drops the send (`admission.rs:461`). No send is attempted ⇒ no recovery probe is claimed ⇒ `is_suppressed_at` never clears. On Critical-priority topics admission still admits a cooled peer, the probe fires and the peer recovers after the cooldown; on **Bulk** topics there is no self-driven escape at all. The only ways out are the remote peer initiating traffic to us, or a transport disconnect.

**Blast radius (x0x).** Every announce/discovery lane is Bulk: `x0x.machine.announce.v2`, `x0x.user.announce.v2`, `x0x.discovery.groups`, `x0x/release`, `x0x/caps/v1`. A peer cooled once on any of those stays cooled indefinitely from our side. This is a plausible contributor to saorsa-labs/x0x#288 (fleet degrades after ~21 h) and to the advert/capability convergence lag behind x0x#442.

**Fix direction.** Either (a) exempt a bounded recovery probe from the Bulk drop — allow exactly one probe send per peer per cooldown expiry, the same allowance Critical already gets implicitly, or (b) clear suppression on expiry for peers with no outstanding failures instead of requiring a successful probe. (a) preserves the fail-closed intent; (b) is simpler but weaker. Either way the test is: suppress a peer on a Bulk topic, advance past the cooldow

issues.title: pubsub cooling: demotion removes an eager peer with no graft-eligible replacement, locking the topic at degree 1 for >=120 s (x0x#611)
issues.body:
Root-caused from x0x#611 (analysis by Claude Opus against pubsub 0.5.78).

**Mechanism.** A *local* CPU stall blows the 2500 ms per-peer send budget and is booked as peer slowness. Five such timeouts in 30 s suppress the peer for 120 s and demote it eager → lazy (`lib.rs:3994` via `prune_peer` at `:4037`; timeout state machine at `:3855`; constants at `:146,:156,:159,:162`). The issue-#32 cooling floor (`cooling_floor_blocks_at`, `:3546`, bypass arm at `:3950`) then guarantees exactly **one** surviving eager peer. With a consumer that sets a max eager degree of 2 (x0x Leaf), the healthy degree is also 2, so the observed collapse is precisely 2 → 1.

**Why it does not recover promptly.** `set_topic_peers` re-adds peers as *lazy* (`:8604`) and `maintain_degree_at` (`:4082`) wants to promote at `:4102`, but its candidates come from `scored_lazy_peers_at` (`:3665`) which filters on `can_graft_peer_at` (`:3640`); the cooled peer fails it. Expiry alone is not enough: `can_graft_at` (`:2877`) defers to `is_suppressed_at` (`:2867`), which stays true after expiry until a recovery probe succeeds. On a Critical-priority topic the probe does fire, so recovery happens — but only after the 120 s cooldown. (x0x#611 called the degrade "permanent"; the evidence there covered only ~3–12 s of wall time after the degrade, so it never tested recovery. The defect is real; the label was wrong.)

issues.title: Retire the #684 settle-barrier workaround and the #277/#510 flake allowances once ant-quic 0.27.52 is pinned
issues.body:
Follow-up to #691 (ant-quic 0.27.51 pin).

Two workarounds exist only because the fixes were not yet upstream:

issues.title: ADR-0061 §3 remaining halves: versioned launchd/systemd templates and systemd loaded-policy readback
issues.body:
Follow-up tracker split out of #671 (which covers the #668 round-3 review's immediate items). #671's item 2 recorded that ADR-0061 §3 requires **versioned launchd/systemd templates *and* loaded-policy readback**, and that only the macOS launchd readback shipped (#668). This issue keeps the remaining halves visible; per the ADR's dated status note, §3 stays **NOT MET** until they land.

Remaining work:

1. **Versioned templates (launchd and systemd).** §3: "Versioned templates and loaded-policy readback establish support, not a marker in isolation." `x0x autostart` currently generates an unversioned plist; a supported deployment must identify the template version it was created from so drift can be detected at upgrade time.
2. **Systemd loaded-policy readback.** Before an in-place replace on Linux, the upgrade path should read back the loaded unit policy (`systemctl show -p Restart -p ExecStart` on the unit named by `INVOCATION_ID`/the systemd-parent signal) and refuse the apply unless the loaded `Restart=` policy actually guarantees a respawn after exit 0 — the systemd-side twin of the macOS `launchctl print` readback #615 shipped.
3. **"Supported launchd jobs must actually restart after 0" remains unobserved** (platform acceptance observation, per ADR-0061's Validation section).

Refs #668, #671, #615, #616. Source: ADR-0061 §3 and its "Implementation status updates after acceptance" note; #668 merge record round 3.

issues.title: pubsub: add ValidationAction::LazyForward — deliver + cache + IHAVE-announce (incl. withheld eager peers) without eager re-publish (x0x#674 C2)
issues.body:
Needed by x0x#674 C2/C3 (fleet CPU, saorsa-labs/x0x#656): x0x must forward *relayed* (non-owned) traffic lazily instead of eager-republishing it to the full eager set, while preserving delivery. The only validator seam (`apply_topic_validator`, called once in `handle_eager_admitted`) has no lazy verdict: `ForwardAndDeliver` eager-forwards, `DeliverOnly` withholds the IHAVE too (subscriber behind a relay learns nothing), `Drop` suppresses IWANT serve. Fabricating IHAVE at the x0x transport shim is not viable (IHAVE headers are signed by sg's constructor-owned key; mesh bookkeeping lives in sg).

Exact spec (API, semantics in `handle_eager_admitted`, meters, and the sg-side tests) below, from the x0x analysis (omp-reports/x0x-3f-674-c23-report.md §2). Target: 0.5.79, no wire-format change, compatible with 0.41.x/0.42.x peers.

## 2. Required saorsa-gossip change (exact)

**Crate:** `saorsa-gossip-pubsub`, target release **0.5.79**. No wire-format change (IHAVE/IWANT/EAGER frames unchanged; only which peer gets which kind changes). Compatible with 0.41.x/0.42.x peers — they process IHAVE/IWANT today.

    /// lazy set as usual AND to every peer whose eager send was withheld.
    LazyForward,
}
```

issues.title: shutdown() never joins the accept worker; a handshake completing after the lifecycle sweep escapes into both maps
issues.body: Follow-up from the PR #285 review (pre-existing; not introduced by #285). The accept worker is spawned at `src/nat_traversal_api.rs` ~L2094 with its join handle dropped, so `shutdown()` never waits for it, and the registration path (~L6758) has no shutdown check. A handshake that completes after the #285 lifecycle sweep lands in both `connections` and `connection_lifecycle`; since `connections` is drained only once it is not even implicitly closed at `clear()`. Fix: keep the accept worker's JoinHandle, set a shutting-down flag before the sweep, make the registration path refuse (and close) when the flag is set, and abort/join the worker before `release_socket_for_shutdown`. Test: start shutdown while an inbound handshake is mid-flight and assert no entry survives. Refs #283, #285; Greptile P1 on #285.

issues.title: spawn_reader_task: per-stable_id reader guard is checked after tokio::spawn, leaving a brief duplicate-reader window
issues.body: Follow-up from the PR #282 round-2 review (LOW, non-blocking). `spawn_reader_task` now guards on `conn_stable_id` (p2p_endpoint.rs ~L9607-9626, #166 cross-generation semantics preserved), but the guard is evaluated after `tokio::spawn` (spawn ~L9270, check ~L9611), so a duplicate reader can be live across the lock await and steal one stream before the abort lands. Fix: take the guard (or reserve the stable_id slot) before spawning, and abort/skip without ever polling accept. Add a test that races two spawn_reader_task calls for one connection and asserts a single accept consumer. Refs #280, #282.

issues.title: shutdown() closes only canonical connections; superseded lifecycle survivors keep is_connected() true on the remote until idle timeout
issues.body:
Found while root-causing x0x#510 (restart-class CI failures that survived x0x#679).

**Mechanism.** `NatTraversalEndpoint::shutdown` (`nat_traversal_api.rs` ~L8424) closes only the canonical `self.connections` entries (~L8434-8440); the `connection_lifecycle` map is never pruned on shutdown (its own comment at ~L8455 says so). Superseded-but-alive entries are closed only implicitly via `ConnectionRef::drop` (`high_level/connection.rs` ~L1351) when `clear()` runs at ~L8457, immediately before `release_socket_for_shutdown` (~L8460) yanks the socket, so the CONNECTION_CLOSE frequently never transmits.

On the **remote** side that survivor keeps the peer "connected": `Node::is_connected` requires both maps true (`p2p_endpoint.rs` ~L8694); `is_peer_connected` (`nat_traversal_api.rs` ~L7777) falls through to `repromote_surviving_connection` (~L7359), which promotes any Superseded lifecycle entry still alive with no close_reason; `remove_connected_peer_if_unroutable` (`p2p_endpoint.rs` ~L2642) then refuses to drop the `connected_peers` entry. The remote's view stays stale until the idle timeout. A second connection family exists whenever a reverse dial or simultaneous open happened earlier, which is why the x0x test passes on rerun.

**Evidence.** x0x CI jobs 103561131939 and 103569350890 fail the new 5 s "joiner must observe the old owner connection as gone" barrier (`tests/hs_f2_membership_cluster.rs:2612`) after a full 5 s; an earlier capture (job 103483947641) showed the joiner

issues.title: tests/e2e_deploy.sh: binary upload to the APAC nodes stalls (Singapore/Sydney) even with ssh keepalives — needs a resumable/retried transfer
issues.body: Observed 2026-09-11 (Nuremberg, Singapore) and 2026-09-12 (Sydney): the 58 MB `gzip -1 | ssh … gunzip` upload from the Mac to the APAC bootstraps stalls indefinitely; the #657 keepalives (`ServerAliveInterval=15`, `CountMax=4`) did not fail the session fast either — the script sat in the upload until the outer `timeout` (40 min) killed it, leaving the last node on the old binary. Manual redeploys of the same node with the same gzip stream succeeded on the next attempt in 6–10 min. Ask: (1) upload with retries and a per-node transfer timeout (e.g. `rsync -z --partial --timeout=60 -e "ssh …"` with 3 attempts, or split the upload into a bounded `timeout 900` per node and retry), (2) verify the byte count on the remote before restarting (`stat -c %s` vs local), (3) after the loop, re-check every node runs the new version and re-upload stragglers instead of only reporting them. The rolling-restart order and the mesh verification are fine as they are.

issues.title: hs_f2 treekem restart e2e: one-shot 5 s announce-blob fetch (no retry) before the #447 verified-certificate assertion fails under heavy load
issues.body: Found during the #679 review (1 failure in 19 loaded runs, 45 s timeout at the downstream #447 verified-certificate assertion after the #510 gossip-plane barrier had passed). Suspect: the test performs a single 5 s announce-blob fetch with no retry; under load the blob response can arrive after the window. Add a bounded retry (or wait on the blob-arrival event) with a mechanism-based justification, or make the product path retry. Also note from the same review: the #677 accept-loop `continue` has no consecutive-`None` cap (safe on ant-quic 0.27.47+), and the #510 bootstrap-cache fallback widens the send-path liveness repair at `src/network.rs:2531` from instant-fail to a full dial — both to keep in mind if either path changes.

issues.title: pubsub: dedupe fast path takes the per-topic write lock on a miss (72% of frames); per-topic dedupe_lock_acquire measured at 4.1 s wait per wall-second on an x0x bootstrap
issues.body: From the x0x#674 review of #56 and a live x0x testnet sample (NYC bootstrap, 27 peers, 0.5.77): `pubsub_stages.dedupe_lock_acquire.total_ns` accumulates 4.12 s of wait per wall second and `republish.total_ns` 3.98 s/s, versus 0.19 s/s in `verify` — the per-topic lock is the hot spot, not signature verification. #56 (0.5.78) adds a pre-verify dedup fast path that takes the per-topic WRITE lock even when the msg_id is absent (the common, 72% case), doubling write acquisitions on the new-message path. Ask: probe with a read lock and upgrade to write only on a hit (or use a lock-free/sharded seen-set for the dedupe check), and add a counter split for read vs write acquisitions so the effect is measurable on the fleet. Expected: `dedupe_lock_acquire` and `republish` elapsed drop materially on relay nodes.

issues.title: One connect_addr yields two accepted generations at the acceptor; after supersession a dialer-opened stream never surfaces (release builds, loopback)
issues.body:
Found while reviewing #279 (report in the x0x session artifacts). The two-node loopback fixture used by `p2p_endpoint::tests::reader_recovers_from_prefix_starvation` (`src/p2p_endpoint.rs:~14509`, currently `#[ignore]`d as "timing-sensitive across CI configs") and copied by #279's new `churn_disconnect_reconnect_delivers_over_new_connection` fails deterministically in **release** builds: 6 of 7 standalone runs on a quiet machine, always at exactly the 10 s stream-accept deadline (the one pass took 4.2 s — bimodal, never slow-but-passing). Instrumenting the accept loop shows a single `connect_addr` producing **two** accepted generations at the receiving node; after the second supersedes the first, the application stream the dialer opened with `open_bi` (8-byte magic prefix written correctly) never reaches the receiver's stream queue. The reader's 2 s prefix-read guard is not involved (zero occurrences across four instrumented runs); a 300 ms settle between connect and stream open does not help (5/5 still fail). The failure happens before any `disconnect()`, so #278's sweep is not on the path.

This is the same "write succeeds but never arrives" family as #277 / x0x#277 shape B and is worth fixing rather than quarantining: an acceptor that accepts two generations for one dial should either reject the second at the handshake or migrate/queue streams from the superseded generation. Reproduce: `cargo test --release --lib -- --ignored reader_recovers_from_prefix_starvation`.

issues.title: Accept loop exits permanently when ant-quic accept() returns None on the re-keyed Rejected path
issues.body: Found during the #510 investigation. In `src/network.rs:4548-4550` the inbound accept loop `break`s when `Node::accept()` yields `None`. ant-quic returns `None` (without `register_connected_peer`) on the re-keyed path in `p2p_endpoint::accept` (`~:6748`, `actual_peer_id != peer_id`, Rejected outcome — a simultaneous-open tiebreaker loser on a connection whose peer id was re-keyed). After that the daemon never accepts another inbound connection until restart. Fix: treat `None` as "this connection was rejected, continue accepting", and only exit the loop on endpoint shutdown. Needs a hermetic test that drives a Rejected accept and asserts a subsequent inbound is still accepted.

issues.title: disconnect(): nat_traversal connections map still returns the closing connection to open_bi() (close_reason unset during async teardown) — streams silently opened on a dying connection
issues.body:
Found via x0x#277 (`connection_churn_falls_back_to_reliable`, reproduced locally in both shapes; ant-quic 0.27.50).

After `disconnect()` followed by `connect_addr()` to the same peer:
- `p2p_endpoint::connected_peers` is updated to the NEW connection — `is_connected()` (`src/p2p_endpoint.rs:8694`) returns true.
- `nat_traversal_api::connections` (DashMap) still holds the OLD `InnerConnection` whose `close_reason()` is still `None` while the async teardown runs — `get_connection()` (`src/nat_traversal_api.rs:7798`) returns it, and `open_bi()` (`src/p2p_endpoint.rs:7983`) opens a stream on it.

Consequences for the caller: writes either fail with `sending stopped by peer: error 0` (peer already processed CONNECTION_CLOSE) or **succeed into the old send buffer and are discarded** when the close completes — no error surfaces at all, so application-level replay buffers never trigger.

Ask: in `disconnect` (`src/p2p_endpoint.rs:6947`) set the connection's close reason synchronously (or remove/mark the entry in the nat_traversal map) before initiating the async teardown, so `get_connection()` never returns a closing connection and `open_bi()` returns `ConnectionClosed` immediately. A regression test: disconnect → immediately `open_bi()` must fail, and after `connect_addr()` the new connection must be the one `open_bi()` uses. Possibly related to ant-quic#277-adjacent report x0x#510 / ant-quic#277 (fresh handshake state disagreeing between the two maps after a restart).

issues.title: #656 inbound side: drop-before-verify for non-owned blob traffic and a signature-verify cache (CPU is inbound-dominated)
issues.body:
Follow-up from #656. The publish-side fixes (#663/#664/#665) shipped in the 0.42.2 candidate but cannot reduce bootstrap CPU, because 99.4% of a bootstrap's traffic is relayed and CPU is ML-DSA-65 verification of INBOUND messages generated by peers still on older code (`outbound_publish_origin`: local 0.47 msg/s vs relay 78.6 msg/s; testnet after 5 h on 0.42.2: CPU unchanged at 46–67%).

Design work needed (each with a hermetic count/CPU test):
1. **Drop-before-verify for `announce/v3/blob` responses a node cannot serve or does not need**: either partition blob topics so a non-owner is not subscribed to other certs' partitions, or add a cheap header check (digest ∉ {own digest} ∪ {digests with an in-flight `ensure_blob`}) that discards the frame before the signature verify. Must not break the fetch path (`ensure_blob` → IWANT) or wire compat with 0.41.x/0.42.x peers.
2. **Signature-verify cache** keyed on `(msg_id, signer key hash)` with a bounded LRU, so a message arriving via several gossip paths (EAGER + IWANT repair) is verified once. Likely belongs in saorsa-gossip-pubsub; check where PlumTree dedups by msg_id relative to the verify.
3. Measure the split: how much inbound verify cost is blob vs caps vs bus vs SWIM on a bootstrap, from `/diagnostics/gossip` inbound-by-topic counters, to rank 1 vs 2.
4. Rollout reality: the fix only shows in CPU once most of the mesh is upgraded; plan the fleet/user upgrade cadence accordingly (prod: 12 bootstrap daemons of ~27 peers).

issues.title: Immediate reconnect after peer restart: fresh handshake dropped while the previous connection's CONNECTION_CLOSE is still being processed
issues.body:
Observed from x0x (saorsa-labs/x0x#510, e2e `integration_treekem_home_rename_restart_single_announce_end_to_end`, ant-quic 0.27.50, loopback, 2-node):

1. Node A (owner) shuts down its ant-quic `Node` and immediately builds a new one on the same address.
2. A calls `connect_addr(B)`; it returns `Ok` (handshake completes).
3. Within ~100 ms, B has no connection to A (`connected_peers()` empty on A's side too) and nothing re-dials; A stays disconnected for the whole 20 s test window.

Interpretation from the investigation: B is still unwinding the previous connection's `CONNECTION_CLOSE` when the new handshake arrives and treats the new connection as a stale/duplicate generation, dropping it after accept. The failure is timing-dependent: it shows only on loaded 2-vCPU CI runners (≈6 of 14 job runs on 2026-09-11/12), never locally on an M-series Mac (local reconnect 123–155 ms). Inserting a 300 ms pause before the rebuild avoids it (x0x#666).

Ask: on the accepting side, a new handshake from an address/peer whose previous connection is in the closing/draining state should either be accepted as a new generation or be retried by the dialer once the drain completes, rather than completing the handshake and then dropping silently. Relevant x0x-side helpers: `connect_addr`, `connected_peers()`; the earlier "never durable" diagnosis in x0x#278/#510 has the same signature.

issues.title: Gossip announce/identity adverts push every interface address even when the listener is bound to a specific IP (card fixed in #649; announce paths still inconsistent)
issues.body:
Split from the review of PR #649 (#638). `card_addresses` (src/server/routes/identity.rs) now suppresses interface hints that are not dialable for an explicitly bound listener, because ant-quic 0.27.50 honours explicit binds (PR #274). The gossip announce paths still push every interface address unconditionally: `announce()` src/lib.rs:~2979, `announce_identity()` ~7567, `announcement_addresses()` ~9299. A loopback- or LAN-bound daemon's card and its gossip advert therefore disagree, and peers dialing from the advert burn the 3 s + 3 s per-hint probe budget (`local_direct_probe_priority` excludes loopback from fast probes, src/lib.rs:~857; ladder ~4619-4821) before reaching a dialable address.

Fix: share one "dialable hints for this bind" helper between the card and the announce producers; consider letting the dial ladder try loopback early when the advert is loopback-only (defence in depth), and document the 3+3+8 s ladder budget in docs/trust-and-connectivity.md. Production bootstraps bind `[::]` and are unaffected.

issues.title: Local shell e2e suites (dogfood_groups, local_mesh) depend on mDNS to mesh their loopback daemons; a foreign mDNS x0x node makes them fail deterministically (#417 class)
issues.body:
Observed 2026-09-11 on the release engineer's macOS host while proving the 0.42.0 tip. `tests/e2e_dogfood_groups.sh` and `tests/e2e_local_mesh.sh` had passed 29/29 and 6/6 in the morning; from ~12:40Z both fail deterministically on the SAME binaries (tip `dd23c4e` and RC `af4f8d0` alike, idle machine), at the first command DM: `POST /direct/send` → 404 `recipient_key_unavailable` (alice never receives bob's announce/key material); mesh reports "need at least 2 runners; found ['alice']".

Cause: the scripts write configs with only `instance_name`, `data_dir`, `api_address`, `log_level` and start `x0xd --no-hard-coded-bootstrap` — no `bootstrap_peers`, no `mdns_enabled = false` — so the three loopback daemons can only find each other through mDNS. bob's daemon log during the failures shows 23× `saorsa_gossip_pubsub: Invalid signature, dropping peer_id=peer_b5e5ba38` plus traffic from `peer_aecf222f`; neither is a test daemon nor the local production daemon (`07bf47fc…`), i.e. foreign x0x nodes reachable over mDNS on this LAN. alice marks bob's peer dead via SWIM suspect timeout. `e2e_dogfood_local.sh` (2 daemons) keeps passing.

Fix (same shape as #608 for the Rust harness): generate `mdns_enabled = false` and explicit `bootstrap_peers = ["127.0.0.1:<alice quic port>"]` (with fixed QUIC ports per node) in every local shell suite, so they are hermetic regardless of the LAN. Both failures are the same rule:

issues.title: e2e_full_audit.sh: stale owner.json beside /tmp/x0x-fulltest-user.key makes 'x0x user-id create' refuse (ADR-0036), breaking the local audit on reruns
issues.body:
Found 2026-09-11 while running the local e2e suites against the 0.41.4 RC (origin/main af4f8d0).

`tests/e2e_full_audit.sh` sets `USER_KEY_PATH=/tmp/x0x-fulltest-user.key`, deletes only that file on cleanup (line ~34), then runs `x0x user-id create "$USER_KEY_PATH"` (line ~43). Since ADR-0036 (PR #430) `user-id create` also writes `owner.json` beside the key and refuses to install a different UserId over an existing owner. A stale owner file from an earlier run therefore makes every later run fail before the daemons start:

```
error: refusing to replace owner cec5087ffa47fef73089403c07a53c2f469ae9d5a57a5b3c8ad570dd76dda4cd with 3d8854ce5e4a6956f7ea0d813f80b702e44288e6455f7c2e5baed13475c98287: one owner per install (ADR-0036)
```

The operator's real `~/.x0x/owner.json` is not involved (different UserId, mtimes untouched) — the daemons use a config-scoped `data_dir`. Fix: give the run its own `mktemp -d` for the user key (so the sibling `owner.json` lives and dies with it), or remove the sibling in the cleanup trap. Likely the same pattern in `e2e_comprehensive.sh` (exit 2 under `set -euo pipefail` in the same run).

issues.title: ADR-0061 §6: write and platform-test the manual recovery procedure for a failed supervised upgrade
issues.body:
The one ADR-0061 clause left without a tracking issue after PR #612. Arguably more urgent than the §3 gap in #615.

## What exists

PR #612 honours the *prohibition* half of §6: recovery on the supervised path is explicitly labelled manual, the supervised-exit log line carries `automatic_rollback = false` and states that readiness is observed by the supervisor rather than by x0xd, and `docs/upgrade-system.md` says the same in prose. **Nothing advertises automatic supervised rollback.** That is the safety-critical half and it is done.

## What is missing

§6 permits the first ownership correction to use "a documented, platform-tested operator recovery procedure; it must label recovery manual." We have the labelling, not the procedure.

**No step-by-step recovery procedure has been written, and none has been tested on macOS.**

The concrete scenario it must cover: a migrated launchd job takes the supervised path, x0xd exits 0 as a restart request, and **the replacement fails to start**. The daemon is now down and, by design, nothing automatic will bring it back.

The materials to recover with already exist:
- the backup binary at `<target>.backup`
- the handoff intent file at `<data_dir>/upgrade-handoff.json`

What is undocumented is the *sequence*: how an operator determines what stage failed, whether to restore the backup binary, how to reconcile the intent file, and how to bring the job back under launchd without leaving two restart owners — the very condition ADR-0061 exist

issues.title: ADR-0061 §3 follow-up: verify launchd loaded policy at upgrade time, not just at repair time
issues.body:
Deferred deliberately from PR #612 (ADR-0061 implementation), with David's explicit ruling on 2026-09-09 to ship the first stage and record §3 as **NOT MET** rather than delay the duplicate-daemon fix.

## The gap

ADR-0061 §3 states that a supported managed install must identify its actual service/job, supervisor version, executable/arguments, root resolution, supervision signal, exit status, restart policy and recovery owner — and explicitly that:

> Versioned templates and loaded-policy readback establish support, **not a marker in isolation**.

PR #612 recognises supervision by `X0X_SUPERVISED=1` (or `INVOCATION_ID` / parent `systemd`) **alone**. That is the marker in isolation §3 rules out.

## The concrete residual failure

`x0x autostart --repair` checks `KeepAlive: true` **at repair time**. The daemon does not re-check the loaded job policy **at upgrade time**.

So: a launchd job that carries the marker and later has `KeepAlive` removed or made conditional will still classify as `SupervisedExit`, exit 0 on upgrade, and **nothing restarts it**. The daemon goes down and stays down.

This requires an operator to alter `KeepAlive` after running `--repair`, which is why it was judged acceptable to defer — but it is a silent-service-disappearance failure, so it should not stay open indefinitely.

- At upgrade time, read back the **loaded** launchd job policy for the running instance (not the on-disk plist alone — a loaded job can differ from

issues.title: Test fixture leaks into the real user identity dir: profile_api round-trip returns the operator's actual profile
issues.body:
Found while implementing the #417 mDNS knob (PR #608). This is a **second, independent #417-class fixture leak** — same category of defect, different vector: identity-dir rather than mDNS.

## The defect

`profile_api::daemon_api_profile_round_trip` fails on an **unmodified tree** and, in doing so, returns the machine operator's real profile — the observed response contained `"human_name":"<person>"`.

That means the test is not reading a fixture-owned identity directory. It is reaching the developer's actual `~/.x0x/` state.

## Why this matters more than a failing test

1. **It is a correctness hazard in both directions.** A test that can *read* the real identity dir can generally also *write* to it. Identity material (`machine.key`, `agent.key`, `user.key`), `contacts.json`, the bootstrap cache and revocation state all live there. A test run should never be able to mutate an operator's real identity.
2. **It makes results non-reproducible and environment-dependent** — the test outcome depends on whose machine it runs on and what that person's profile says. On a clean CI runner it may pass for the wrong reason.
3. **It is a privacy leak into test output and CI logs.** A real human name appeared in a test failure. On a shared CI log that is an accidental disclosure of operator data.

#417 (canonical, with #337 closed as its duplicate) is "test/CI daemons join the prod network — hermetic-by-default". This is the same *class*: tests are not hermeti

`cli_request_parity` fails because `--agent` is not serialized for `GET /diagnostics/dm` in `src/cli/commands/`. The CLI accepts the flag but it does not reach the request, so the endpoint is queried without the agent selector.

issues.body:
Found while root-causing #600. Verified against `main` @ 8440014. This is independent of both #493 and #600 and is filed separately because it is a data-integrity defect in its own right.

## The defect

**There is no single-instance guard in `x0xd`.** No pidfile, no `flock`, no exclusive port bind, no launchd job-label check anywhere in `src/`. The only related code is `src/cli/commands/daemon.rs:14-19`, a courtesy HTTP probe in the CLI — not a guard in the daemon.

What actually prevents two daemons today is a side effect of SQLite:

  if let Err(e) = conn.execute_batch("BEGIN IMMEDIATE; COMMIT;") { return Err(HistoryError::Locked(..)) }
  ```
  with the comment *"Acquire the exclusive lock NOW so a second process fails at open, not at first write."*

That is a poor guard for two reasons:

1. **It is implicit.** The second process dies with `history initialization failed … failed to create agent` — which reads as a history subsystem problem, not "another daemon owns this data dir". #493 shows this happening 3,492 times.
2. **It only covers `history.db`.** These are left entirely unprotected: `machine.key`, `agent.key`, `contacts.json`, the bootstrap cache, and `revocations-v2.bin`.

## The hole

**With `history.enabled = false` there is no guard at all**, and two daemons will coexist fully on one data directory, both reading and writin

issues.title: Terminate announce-blob responder when subscription inputs close
issues.body:
The announce-blob responder keeps selecting a drained subscription after it closes. With one closed input and a quiet surviving input it repeatedly receives `None`; with both drained inputs it never terminates (`src/announce_blob.rs:665–669` on main `aba0a671`).

The retained `Arc<PubSubManager>` does not retain each subscription forwarder sender. Queue-full forwarder exit is a concrete closure path; established-topic unsubscribe also drops the upstream sender in locked saorsa-gossip-pubsub 0.5.76, then its x0x forwarder exits. Ordinary Agent shutdown alone does not establish closure. No evidence ties this defect to the recorded certificate-resolution failure or proves CPU starvation.

Proposed bounded fix: share a generic two-receiver helper with the production Subscription wrapper, disable closed branches while waiting for a surviving input, and terminate the responder when both are drained. Keep verification, publish behavior, digest selection and task ownership unchanged. Constructor-free tests should directly poll closed/live receivers, drain buffered values, prove closure wakes a pending future and preserve cancellation safety. Complete Agent shutdown custody remains separate.
