issues.title: Concurrent announce-blob fetches terminate on another request’s response
issues.body:
At current main `aba0a671ca07b56c758cac6d77f7caa0fab05e48`, `src/announce_blob.rs:430–432` documents that concurrent fetchers share the response topic and select their own digest. The receive loop instead returns `verify_fetched_blob` for the first decodable response (line489). A valid response for another pending digest fails the digest comparison (lines534–540) and terminates this fetch before its own response arrives.

This is a P2 availability defect with a concrete interleaving: fetch A and fetch B both subscribe; B’s response arrives first; A terminates with digest mismatch, although A’s valid response may follow within the existing deadline. Certificate validation remains fail-closed.

The new PR578 coverage failure reached readiness in484ms but had digest present/certificate absent and one failed fetch. Its log does not record the fetch failure reason, so it does not prove this interleaving caused that run. This issue tracks the source defect separately from #447’s original topology diagnosis and broad acceptance.

Repair scope: ignore responses whose actual bytes hash to another digest; retain the complete existing verifier for matching candidates, the same request carriers and fetch deadline. Required inert controls: interleaved distinct valid responses reach their own matches; unrelated-only has no terminal selection; matching malformed, mixed, wrong-agent and forged certificate candidates still reject. A local one-file candidate exists under review; no merged repa

issues.body:
Wiki and Web currently create ordinary Signed stores from a Space-ID-prefixed topic. Those stores are not bound to group membership: the generic PUT direct-delivery path selects eligible contacts without a group filter. For confidential Spaces this is a P1 confidentiality boundary defect. Readers on other members also lack a shared anchored store opener. GUI saves ignore failed create/PUT responses and announce success; page keys are not encoded as single URL segments; failed loads masquerade as empty or stale content.

- Use real group-bound shared storage for confidential GSS and Home/TreeKEM, with no fallback to generic readable stores. Existing encrypted group-store route is GSS-only; a URL substitution alone is incomplete.
- Preserve intentionally public readability for SignedPublic while defining and enforcing the intended collaborative writer policy against current membership.
- Share one deterministic application store across authorized members; preserve epoch/revocation and persistence guarantees. Do not silently migrate or republish legacy pages.

Concurrent fixtures using the same name can also destroy each other's data. TCP connection matches can include more than the intended listening daemon; querying TCP for the configured UDP port is not an ownership check. This is source-confirmed destructive behavior, not a report that a production process was killed during the campaign.

## Problem

A transport can distinguish a concurrent-session/acceptor conflict internally, but the `LinkTransport::start` trait cannot expose that distinction through `LinkTransportError`. This blocks typed handling in saorsa-labs/x0x#460.

Verified both published saorsa-webrtc-core0.5.0 and current upstream main0c09a6156687e580f15730f3750e5739341bb721: [LinkTransportError](https://github.com/saorsa-labs/saorsa-webrtc/blob/0c09a6156687e580f15730f3750e5739341bb721/saorsa-webrtc-core/src/link_transport.rs#L55) offers NotConnected, PeerNotFound, SendError, ReceiveError, InvalidStreamType and IoError, with no typed busy/session-conflict case.

In x0x main e16ba97a9d65022251e67ecc17f6e23d4b75699e, start_lane maps the real StreamAcceptorConflict to VoiceLaneError::SessionConflict, then the trait implementation at src/voice/link_transport.rs:957–962 converts it to IoError(text). The first session remains valid, so mapping contention to NotConnected would misstate the failure.

## Requested API design

Provide a stable typed resource/session contention result through the trait, retaining genuine setup failures as their appropriate error class. Decide the public compatibility policy before implementation: this enum is currently exhaustive, so adding a variant can break downstream exhaustive matches. Do not assume a patch release is compatible or silently substitute an unrelated existing variant.

issues.title: Data: handshake flights >1500 B rely on IP fragmentation — breaks on fragment-filtering networks (OCI), 16,260/16,260 reassembly failures
issues.body:
Data point from deploying v0.41.2 (linux-arm64) on an Oracle Cloud instance. RFC 9000 §14 says an endpoint MUST NOT rely on IP fragmentation for QUIC packets — observed behavior suggests the PQ handshake flights do exactly that, which fails hard on networks that drop non-initial fragments.

**Setup:** OCI aarch64 instance, public IP, VNIC MTU 9000. Daemon dials the embedded bootstraps (142.93.199.50 etc. on :443/:5483). Bootstrap replies visible at the NIC via tcpdump: 48 B ACK-only Initials and **4096 B ServerHello flights** arriving as first-fragments.

**The failure:** the non-initial fragments never arrive — kernel counters: `IpReasmReqds 16260 == IpReasmFails 16260` (100% reassembly failure, sustained). Result: the client only ever processes ACK-only Initials, retransmits ClientHello CRYPTO forever, and the connection times out after 15 s — "Connection to … timed out", 24/24 bootstrap peers unreachable, daemon healthy but isolated at peers: 0. Trace shows the classic signature: server Handshake packets (1152/1200 B) arriving later and being discarded as "unexpected" because the Initial CRYPTO flight never reassembled.

**Control:** the same v0.41.2 binary on a residential network (fragment-tolerant path) connects to the same bootstraps immediately — same binary, same fleet, only the path differs. A standard QUIC/H3 handshake (aioquic → cloudflare-quic.com) succeeds from the OCI box, so it is not a general UDP/QUIC egress problem.

issues.title: Flaky CI: test_crdt_merge_performance asserts wall-clock < 10ms on shared runners
issues.body:
`tests/comprehensive_integration.rs:557` asserts a wall-clock budget:

```rust
assert!(elapsed.as_millis() < 10, "Merge should be < 10ms");
```

This failed the **Test Suite** job on PR #502 (run 33932778145), a GUI/docs-only change that touches no runtime code. The same test passes locally in **1.15 ms** — roughly an 8x margin — so the budget is not the problem; the shared GitHub runner stalling under load is.

A wall-clock assertion on a shared runner is not a property of the code under test, so it will keep producing red builds on unrelated PRs and training people to re-run CI without reading it.

Options, roughly in order of preference:

1. Drop the timing assertion and keep the correctness assertion (`tasks_ordered().len()`), which is the part that encodes intent.
2. Keep timing as an observation only — print the duration, do not assert.
3. If a regression guard is genuinely wanted, move it to the weekly timing suite (`Integration Timing Suites`) where it does not gate PRs, and give it a budget with real headroom.

Per CLAUDE.md Rule 9, a test should encode why behaviour matters. This one currently encodes runner scheduling luck.

issues.title: leaf nodes still sit on the whole-network compat DM bus; opt-in skip_legacy_dm_bus ready on a fork branch
issues.body:
every node, leaf included, sits on x0x/dm/v1/bus, the whole-network compat
dm topic. every subscriber re-broadcasts it, so a phone carries every
gossip dm in the network, not just its own. on mobile data that is the
dominant idle cost. modern senders use per-recipient inbox topics and only
touch the bus as a fallback.

a node joins the bus in three places today:

1. the inbox service subscribes to it unconditionally
2. the reverse-ack pre-warm joins it on every contact connect and receipt
3. durable acks publish on the bus route as well as the targeted inbox route

(3) matters because publish on an unsubscribed topic is not a no-op here,
it initializes the topic peers and grafts an eager set, so every ack would
rejoin the bus even if (1) and (2) were fixed alone.

prs here are collaborator-only, so the fix is on a fork branch, based on
current main, ready to pull:

https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/compare/main...josh-clsn:x0x:dm-inbox/skip-legacy-bus

it adds one setting, skip_legacy_dm_bus, default false. unset, nothing
changes. set, the node stays off the bus at all three places. trade-off,
stated in the docs: a node with this set no longer hears from senders that
publish only on the bus, and its acks have one fewer gossip route.
per-recipient delivery is unchanged and sends still fall back to the bus.

not tied to participation mode on purpose. leaf is the default, so that
binding would change behaviour for everyone and is your call to make.

Same defect class as #415 (Windows Service), on macOS under launchd. `is_supervised()` (`src/upgrade/restart.rs:144`) only recognises `INVOCATION_ID`, parent comm `systemd`, or `X0X_SUPERVISED=1`. issues.title: WP-C code-review residue: mixed-version roster-clock convergence for non-self-leave events (#482) and pre-verification queue authorization in catch-up fan-out
issues.body:
Two architectural residues from the WP-C code review of PR #489 (hs-codex-pr489-r1-verdict.md items 3 and 7) not addressable within the minimum-fix scope:

1. **Non-self-leave roster-clock gap (item 3)**: the self-leave-scoped waiver in treekem_state_frontier_gap_reason only waives the roster-gap for MemberRemoved where actor == agent_id. A surviving legacy/high-clock member (e.g. a joiner later promoted to admin) emitting an adjacent, hash-linked NON-self commit with revision 10 against a peer at revision 3 still queues forever — catch-up cannot manufacture absent roster-only revisions. Needs either: a generalized clock-reconciliation rule for adjacent hash-linked commits regardless of event kind, or a catch-up mechanism that fills roster-only gaps. Filed separately from the shipped self-leave fix because changing the general admission rule has broader wire-compat implications.

2. **Pre-verification queue authorization (item 7)**: the queue's authorized_treekem_membership_event_for_queue treats sender == actor == target as self-leave without requiring ACTIVE membership, and queues before signed-commit action validation — a FORMER member can enqueue far-frontier commits, displace lower pending entries through the capped sorted queue, and trigger sequential catch-up sends. Fix: require active membership for the self-leave queue authorization arm and validate the commit's action before queue admission.

issues.body:

issues.title: release.yml: 'Require green CI on tagged commit' times out at 20 min while Coverage Gate is still running (v0.41.0 needed a manual rerun)
issues.body:
On the v0.41.0 tag (0522c42) the release workflow (run 33709009755) failed at `Require green CI on tagged commit` with:

```
CI did not reach a terminal state within 20 minutes for 0522c42… (status=in_progress). Refusing to release on unknown CI.
```

CI on the tagged commit was not red — the Coverage Gate job (llvm-cov instrumented full suite) simply runs longer than the gate's 20-minute ceiling now that the suite is ~3,250 tests. Every release will need a manual `gh run rerun` until the ceiling exceeds the Coverage Gate's typical duration.

issues.title: ADR follow-up: owner mandate on MemberAdded, alternate-chain authority validation, and route-complete quarantine for invite-derived seatings (the full fix for #468/#469)
issues.body:
Deferred from the v0.41.0 follow-up wave by design decision (2026-09-02). The codex design reviews of `omp-reports/hs-followups-design-2026-09-02{,-v2}.md` established that fully closing #468/#469 needs a protocol change, not a hardening patch:

1. **Pre-commit owner mandate.** A new field on `MemberAdded` (and the join flow) carrying an owner-user-key signature bound to (stable group id, parent revision/hash, joiner, invite-secret hash, policy hash), produced BEFORE the authority mutates TreeKEM/persists (today `stage_join_result` runs after mutation, named_groups.rs ~9239/~9366), and validated by every enforcing member, not only the joiner. Rollout matrix: owner-keyless v0.41 admins, existing members, old joiners, stripped-policy invites, authority upgrade ordering.
2. **Alternate-chain authority validation.** Fork/eviction decisions must validate the complete alternate chain from the common ancestor (authority proven at each step), not the signer against the retained base roster (which lets a canonically-removed admin force eviction and rejects an admin promoted after the base). Canonical branch selection still needs an independent owner/head anchor; without one, name the behaviour "quarantine on authenticated fork evidence" and document the old-key availability attack.
3. **Persistent, route-complete quarantine.** One centralized operational-state gate (by map id and stable id) consulted by every data-plane route and background worker (public send/cache, secure ratchet/op

issues.title: Home persistence writes the sidecar before named_groups.json: a failed second write leaves sidecar new / named old (split outcome outside the journaled paths)
issues.body:
Found by the codex design review of the #468/#469/#470 follow-ups (2026-09-02). Pre-existing.

`save_named_groups_checked_unlocked` writes the authoritative Home-Suite sidecar first and `named_groups.json` second (named_groups.rs ~23967-24008 at e683e2d). If the second write fails, the in-memory rollback (#470 compare-and-restore) restores memory while the sidecar keeps the NEW Home record — a split outcome on the non-journaled save path. The journaled TreeKEM seal/rebind paths handle this via the paired journals (#467), but ordinary saves do not.

Options: (a) make the ordinary save path journal-first like the seal path; (b) on second-write failure, restore the sidecar from the pre-write bytes (as the #467 rebind rollback already does for its own transaction); (c) write named first then sidecar and treat a missing/old sidecar record as "sidecar behind" on load. Add a regression: sidecar write succeeds, named write fault-injected ⇒ on-disk pair consistent after rollback (or after restart replay).

Refs: #470, #467.

issues.title: persist_named_groups_mutation whole-map rollback can clobber concurrent cross-group writes made outside the persistence mutex
issues.body:
Found by the round-11 independent review of #467. Pre-existing on main (the #467 round-10 `persist_named_groups_mutation_unlocked` body is byte-identical to the previous locked body); not introduced by #467.

`persist_named_groups_mutation` snapshots the whole `named_groups` map, mutates, saves, and on `NotReplaced`/error restores the full snapshot — but the restore happens after the map write guard was released, and some map writers (e.g. owner-cert evaluation, `named_groups.rs` ~14524 / `groups/mod.rs` ~905) do not participate in `named_groups_persistence_lock`. A failed mutation (e.g. a failed DELETE save) can therefore restore an old whole-map image over another group's concurrent in-memory mutation.

Options: retain the map guard through the transaction; generation/CAS-aware rollback (restore only the entries the transaction touched, or only if the map generation is unchanged); or require every map writer to take the persistence mutex. Add a cross-group interleaving regression.

Refs: #467 (round-11 codex verdict), #457.

issues.title: groups: residual invite-derived trust-root and fork authority after InviteV4 (#472)
issues.body:
Found by the round-7 independent review of #467. Pre-existing design, not introduced by #467.

`src/groups/invite.rs` documents that the invite `signature` field is vestigial and not validated by the join flow; admission is authenticated by the invite secret + join handshake only. The joiner copies `invite.policy` and the supplied base hash/roster into its local stub unauthenticated. Consequences:

- **Admission tier is attacker-selected.** #467 introduces two-tier across-gap adoption: an owner-signed head attestation is REQUIRED when the joiner's local policy has an `OwnerCertified` axis (Home groups), and round-4 reconstruction otherwise. A malicious or stale admin inviter can strip the owner axis from the invite policy, keep its admin seat in the supplied base roster, and sign an internally consistent invite-only chain, routing a Home group into the weaker tier from the joiner's point of view.
- **Trust root is invite-derived generally.** The same inviter already controls the joiner's base roster and policy hash, so this is the existing invite trust model rather than a new capability; it is the same class as #468 (stale-base fork).

Follow-up options: enforce the invite signature under the inviter's agent key AND bind the invite policy to the group's canonical policy hash (e.g. cross-check against the discovery-cache GroupCard / announce for the stable group id when one is present, refusing a policy that lacks an owner axis the card advertises); or require the admission ow

issues.title: Invite-base stub adopts a removed admin's fork when the joiner never saw the canonical removal (ADR-0016 equal-revision fork choice)
issues.body:
Found during the independent round-4 review of #467 (certified-membership cluster, #458 reconstruction fix). Both reviewers (Codex + Fable) confirmed it is a **pre-existing** property of the invite-base join stub, not introduced by #467, and equally true of the gapless direct apply path.

**Scenario.** Admin A is an active admin at invite revision N. The authority removes A at canonical revision N+1. A joiner whose local view is still at N (offline / never received the canonical N+1 commit) receives from A an internally consistent alternate N+1 commit that retains A, followed by an N+2 `MemberAdded` for the joiner signed by A. Every check passes: A is an active admin in the joiner's (reconstructed) predecessor roster, linkage is consecutive from N, roster roots and the full state hash re-derive. The joiner adopts A's fork. The next canonical commit then `PrevHashMismatch`es.

**Why it is not fixed in #467.** With the joiner at N, A's fork is indistinguishable from a legitimate N+1 commit A could have issued at that moment; it is the equal-revision fork-choice limitation already documented in `docs/adr/0016-role-based-group-authority-flat-admin.md` (~line 109). #467 does reject the fork whenever the joiner's view has advanced over the canonical removal (round-5 regression test).

**Follow-up options.** (a) Have the joiner fetch/verify the authority's current head (or a quorum of members' heads) before adopting any chain that starts at its own stale revision; (b) require the in

issues.title: test: adapter_insert_advert_enriches_cache is non-hermetic (binds 0.0.0.0, races live-mesh inbound peers) — fails deterministically on mesh-connected dev hosts
issues.body:
Reproduced on a macOS dev host that sits on networks with live x0x daemons (prod mesh + always-on local instances), at pristine `origin/main` `9ba917c` AND identically on a docs-only branch — **not a regression from any current PR**; CI (isolated runners) passes it.

```
---- adapter_insert_advert_enriches_cache stdout ----
thread panicked at tests/gossip_cache_adapter_integration.rs:75:9:
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: 1
 right: 0
```

**Cause.** `agent_with_network_in` (`tests/gossip_cache_adapter_integration.rs:14-26`) builds the agent with `bind_addr: Some("0.0.0.0:0")` and `bootstrap_nodes: vec![]`. Binding all interfaces with a real socket lets INBOUND traffic from the live mesh (mDNS/lan peers dialing the host) land a peer in the gossip cache before the very first assertion (`assert_eq!(adapter.peer_count().await, 0)` at `:75`). On an isolated CI runner nothing dials in, so the count is 0 and the test passes — on any mesh-connected host it is a startup race that usually loses.

Same disease class as #417 (test daemons join the prod network) and #456 (tests writing real state).

**Ask.** Bind the test agent to `127.0.0.1:0` (or assert on the inserted peer only, tolerating pre-existing cache entries) so the test is hermetic on connected hosts.

issues.title: dm: /direct/send response `path` reports gossip_inbox even when the receipt was hedged home over the direct/raw-QUIC path
issues.body:
Found by HS-E1 e2e (2026-08-31, D11) and confirmed by source read on `9ba917c`: a durable DM delivered/hedged over the direct typed path answered with `"path":"gossip_inbox"` while `/diagnostics/dm` showed the real per-peer path.

**Cause.** The durable-ack send path builds its receipts with a hardcoded `path: DmPath::GossipInbox` — the send *strategy*, not the transport that actually carried the ACK:

- `src/dm_send.rs:579-584` (`ack_outcome_to_receipt` → `Accepted`)
- `src/dm_send.rs:600-607` (`gossip_publish_receipt`)
- also `src/server/routes/public_group_bootstrap_outbox.rs:1133-1135`

When the gossip-inbox publish is slow/lost and the durable ACK is hedged home over the direct typed/raw-QUIC path (`durable_ack_is_hedged_on_direct_typed_after_history_commit`, `src/dm_inbox.rs:3389+`), the response still says `gossip_inbox`.

**Impact.** Minor/diagnostics-only: delivery correctness is unaffected; callers using `path` for transport telemetry get the wrong value.

**Ask.** Thread the actual final transport into the receipt instead of the constant (or report both, e.g. `strategy` + `path`).

**Interim.** SKILL.md §4.2 now documents the caveat and points at `/diagnostics/dm` for real per-peer path state.

issues.title: voice: second concurrent call surfaces IoError-wrapped SessionConflict through the LinkTransport trait (typed variant flattened)
issues.body:
Found by HS-E1 e2e (2026-08-31, step 9 evidence `hs-E1-evidence/step09/session-conflict.txt`) and confirmed by source read on `9ba917c`:

```
second lane error: IoError("WebRtcV1 stream acceptor already held by a concurrent call session on this agent")
```

**What happens.** The typed single-acceptor conflict exists and is correct on the lane surface: `X0xLinkTransport::start_lane()` maps `NetworkError::StreamAcceptorConflict` → `VoiceLaneError::SessionConflict` (`src/voice/link_transport.rs:316-318`; variant message at `:87-88` is exactly the string above). But the `LinkTransport` trait impl flattens it:

```rust
// src/voice/link_transport.rs:957-963
async fn start(&mut self) -> Result<(), LinkTransportError> {
    self.start_lane().await
        .map_err(|e| LinkTransportError::IoError(e.to_string()))   // ← typed → stringly
}
```

So every library consumer using the trait (incl. `--example voice_call` shape code) sees `IoError(...)` for a session conflict and cannot branch on the typed variant — callers must string-match.

**Ask.** Carry the typed conflict through the trait surface: either add a `SessionConflict` (or `Busy`) variant to `LinkTransportError`, or map `VoiceLaneError::SessionConflict` to a distinguishable variant instead of `IoError(e.to_string())`.

**Interim.** Docs (SKILL.md §6) now document the actual IoError surface and point typed-error consumers at `start_lane()`; this issue tracks the API gap.

issues.title: Rollback trap: v0.40.4 crash-loops on a data dir that holds a Home (owner_certified) — self-update auto-rollback would brick owned installs
issues.body:
Observed live 2026-08-30 while restoring the testnet plane from b769b79 back to v0.40.4 (`omp-reports/x0x-hs-B-vps-20260830-report.md` §7.1, and independently on a Mac in `hs-B-studio-evidence/s5-restart-crash.txt`):

```
failed to parse named groups file .../named_groups.json
Caused by: unknown variant `owner_certified`, expected one of `invite_only`, `request_access`, `open_join`
```
exit 1 → systemd restart counter reached 44 within minutes until `home.json`, the Home entry in `named_groups.json`, its TreeKEM snapshot and member key-package entry were hand-removed.

Why it matters beyond a manual downgrade: the upgrade helper respawns the PREVIOUS binary when the new one fails `/health` within 30 s (`docs/upgrade-system.md` §5–7). On an owned install (user.key present) the new binary auto-provisions a Home on first start (#435) and persists `GroupAdmission::OwnerCertified`; if that start then misses the health deadline for any reason, the rollback binary crash-loops on the state the new one just wrote → daemon down, `UPGRADE_FAILED`. Old decoders failing closed on the new variant is intentional (`src/groups/policy.rs:275-285` test), but there is no migration/sanitizer and no downgrade guard.

Options: persist Home-suite state in a separate file that old binaries ignore; or write the new variant only after the first successful health-checked start; or ship a documented downgrade sanitizer and make the release notes explicit that v0.40.x cannot start on post-Home state.

issues.title: Mixed-fleet: AgentCard signatures from #445 daemons fail verification on v0.40.4 peers (digest_support inside bincode(dm_capabilities) signable bytes)
issues.body:
Source-confirmed on b769b79 (independent review + Codex adversarial pass, `omp-reports/hs-codex-verdict-20260830.md`); not yet reproduced live.

- `AgentCard::signable_bytes` embeds `bincode::serialize(&self.dm_capabilities)` length-prefixed (`src/groups/card.rs:237-238`).
- Card endpoints copy the live capabilities into the card before signing (`src/server/routes/identity.rs:417-428`); on a daemon with durable gossip ready that is `DmCapabilities::v2_durable_gossip_ready` → `digest_support: true` (`src/dm.rs:160,178`).
- Cards travel as JSON (`identity.rs:760`, `named_groups.rs:1858`, `:16575`). A v0.40.4 receiver's `DmCapabilities` has no `digest_support` field and no `deny_unknown_fields`, so serde drops the field, the receiver rebuilds the bincode caps WITHOUT it, the signable bytes differ, and the card signature verification fails → the old peer rejects every card from a new-binary agent until it upgrades.
- The existing pin `false_digest_support_encodes_byte_identical_to_v1_caps` only covers the `false` case; nothing pins a `true`-advertising card against an old-decoder fixture.

Same class as the #430 round-1 "fleet-breaking card signatures" blocker and the #448 advert drop. Fix options: exclude `digest_support` from the card's signable caps encoding (freeze the v1 caps shape in `signable_bytes`), or carry the caps in the card as opaque bytes that are signed verbatim. Add an old-decoder fixture test.

Related: #448, #445.

issues.title: ADR-0038: a second owner device auto-provisions a SECOND Home instead of joining the owner's Home (per-machine dedup marker)
issues.body:
Observed on b769b79 during the Home Suite proof run (`omp-reports/hs-f1-repro-20260830.md`, side note): three daemons sharing the same owner `user.key` (A = owner, B and C = additional owner devices with self-issued owner-chained agent certs) each auto-provisioned their **own** Home group on first start (A `a629fb86…`-class, B `59dd2e3f…`, C `7339c429…`), because the #435 dedup marker is per machine, not per owner.

Consequence: an owner with N devices has N competing "Home" groups; the ADR-0038 promise of a single owner space is only true per install. ADR-0041 Tier-1 sync carries no reconciliation for this, so the duplicates persist. A second device should discover/join the owner's existing Home (or auto-provisioning should be suppressed when an owner-device enrollment / SyncV1 peer already advertises a Home), and `GET /home` on a device should be able to report "Home lives on another device, not yet joined".

Related: #447 (certified join needs a second announce), #448.

issues.title: Mixed-fleet: digest_support=true capability advert is undecodable by v0.40.4 peers — old→new strict DMs 409 until the OLD peer upgrades ("self-healing" only heals at upgrade)
issues.body:
Found during the 2026-08-30 independent Home-Suite review (hs-A), source-verified on origin/main @ b769b79.

## Summary

Every new-binary daemon advertises `DmCapabilities.digest_support=true` (`src/dm.rs:160,178` — `v1_gossip_ready`/`v2_durable_gossip_ready`, used by the capability service). The true bit appends one byte to the positional postcard advert, so a v0.40.4 peer cannot decode/verify it and DROPS it (documented at `src/dm.rs:104-110`; proven reciprocally by the old-decoder tests `src/dm_capability.rs:736-785`). The old peer therefore never learns the new peer's KEM key / gossip_inbox.

## What the v0.40.4 peer loses while mixed (all old→new)

1. **Gossip-DM lane**: no recipient KEM ⇒ `gossip_ok=false`; strict/product sends (`require_durable_app_ack`, the product default per `src/lib.rs:5818-5820`) fail at the strict gate with `AckSemanticsUnavailable` (`src/lib.rs:5776-5836`) — the contact-card fallback is explicitly insufficient for strict semantics (`src/lib.rs:5716-5725`). A 409-class failure for every product DM old→new until upgrade.
2. **Relay fallback**: the relay seed requires `cap.kem_public_key` (`src/lib.rs:5850-5857`) ⇒ no relayed envelope can be built old→new.

issues.title: peer relay: digest transition policy and per-peer capability observability
issues.body:
Follow-up to #437 (fix/437-relay-inner-binding).

#437 added `RelayHeader.inner_digest` (blake3 over the inner DmEnvelope's canonical postcard bytes, signed under the `x0x-relay-hdr-v2` domain). Receivers hard-drop present-but-mismatched digests, but a digest-less (legacy pre-#437) header is still **fail-open**: it keeps exactly the pre-fix relay-hop guarantees (contact-gate/forward-accounting attribution can still be bypassed by such senders).

This issue tracks the transition end-state, mirroring ADR-0021's attestation transition:

- Add a digest-support flag to `DmCapabilities` (signed capability advert / AgentCard path, src/dm.rs).
- Once a peer's confirmed advert shows support, `PeerRelay::disposition_for` must treat a missing `inner_digest` as rejectable (new `RelayRefusal` variant or reuse `BadSignature`), closing the residual.
- Until then, absence stays fail-open by design — documented in docs/design/adr-0051-mechanics.md.

Scope note: #437's fix targets the RELAY HOP (contact gating + forward accounting attribution). Final-recipient integrity never depended on the header — the inner envelope's own ML-DSA-65 signature attributes a substituted envelope to its real author. No recipient-side header↔inner check is planned (the forward arm delivers only the inner envelope; the header never travels past the relay hop).

Also relevant: the two-stage v1/v2 postcard decode (`RelayedDm::from_postcard`) added for wire compat — old→new frames decode; new→old frames fail to parse

issues.title: peer relay: RelayHeader does not bind RelayedDm.inner — relay can substitute a different valid DmEnvelope
issues.body:
Found during ADR-0051 backfill review (codex + Claude, 2026-08-29): `RelayHeader::signing_bytes()` (src/peer_relay.rs:152-172) signs no digest of `RelayedDm.inner`; `verify()` validates only the header; the listener contact-gates the header sender (src/lib.rs:14113-14133) but reads the inner origin separately (14135-14147) without binding the two. A relay (or on-path holder of a valid header) can carry a DIFFERENT valid `DmEnvelope` under an unrelated outer header. Inner envelope crypto still gates final acceptance, but header-level sender gating and accounting are bypassable. Fix: include `blake3(inner)` in the header signing bytes (additive, capability-gated for old peers). ADR-0051 (in flight, docs/adr-trim-backfill) records the limitation until fixed.

issues.title: Self-update transactional handoff leaves x0xd Stopped for hours-to-days under a Windows Service wrapper (supervision not detected)
issues.body:
## Summary

On Windows, `x0xd` running as a Windows Service (WinSW-style wrapper) intermittently gets stuck in the `Stopped` state after a self-update's transactional handoff — sometimes for hours, once for ~2 days — because `x0xd`'s supervision-detection does not recognize a Windows Service as a supervisor, so it takes the "unsupervised, detached-helper" handoff path even though something is watching it (the service wrapper). The wrapper sees a clean `exit(0)` and its `onfailure` restart is not reliably re-arming afterward.

## Mechanism

Per `CHANGELOG.md` (issue #261, "Unsupervised self-update restart is now transactional"):

> `SupervisedExit` (exit 0 / 100 for the supervisor) only when `stop_on_upgrade = true` and a real supervision signal exists (`INVOCATION_ID` set, parent comm `systemd`, or `X0X_SUPERVISED=1`); not-a-TTY and launchd ancestry are explicitly NOT supervision.

None of those three signals exist under a Windows Service:
- `INVOCATION_ID` is systemd-specific (Linux only).
- Parent `comm == systemd` is Linux-specific.
- `X0X_SUPERVISED=1` is opt-in and not set by any Windows service-wrapper convention I am aware of (not set in our WinSW-style `<service>` XML — see below).

So on Windows, every self-update takes the transactional handoff path: the running daemon exits `0`, writes `upgrade-handoff.json`, and spawns a detached `x0xd --upgrade-handoff` helper to swap the binary and relaunch. That is correct behavior for an unsupervised `nohup`/background run — b

issues.title: test: addr_is_free_probes_loopback_for_unspecified_bind fails deterministically on macOS
issues.body:
`upgrade::restart::tests::addr_is_free_probes_loopback_for_unspecified_bind` fails on macOS (passes on Linux CI). Verified on pristine main (b09d610).

Cause: `addr_is_free` probes an unspecified bind by **binding** `127.0.0.1:port`. Rust std sets `SO_REUSEADDR` on Unix; BSD/macOS then allows a specific-IP bind alongside an existing wildcard (`0.0.0.0:port`) bind, so the probe succeeds and `addr_is_free` wrongly reports free. Linux refuses the overlapping bind, so CI stays green.

Impact beyond the test: on macOS, the upgrade-restart port-free check can report a port free while the old daemon still holds the wildcard bind. Fix options: probe by `TcpStream::connect` to loopback (connection refused ⇒ free) instead of bind, or bind without REUSEADDR via socket2.

Found during system-topic cadence work 2026-08-26.

issues.title: Infra: David's ISP drops inbound UDP from Hetzner ranges (Helsinki/Nuremberg unreachable directly from home network) — evidence + relay implications
issues.body:
Evidence (2026-08-24, public IP [home IP redacted] behind CGNAT hop [CGNAT hop redacted]):
- ICMP to 65.21.157.229 / 116.203.101.172: fine (60-97 ms).
- QUIC/UDP probes: both Hetzner nodes TIMEOUT on 5483+443; both DO nodes answer version-negotiation in <0.35 s.
- tcpdump on Helsinki: our 1200 B probes ARRIVE (`In … [home IP redacted] > .5483`), Helsinki SENDS 34-35 B replies (`Out … > [home IP redacted]`), the Mac receives nothing → the drop is on the return path into the ISP, specific to Hetzner source ranges (likely ISP-side anti-DDoS filtering).

Implications:
- Direct AND hole-punched paths Mac↔Hetzner are impossible from this network (punch needs bidirectional UDP); only MASQUE relay via a DO node works — exactly the #398 fix-5 ladder. Bootstrap seed dials to Helsinki/Nuremberg from this network will always burn timeouts; the eternal-retry noise is bounded by dial gating but nonzero.
- Options: ISP ticket (evidence above suffices); or note in ops docs that Hetzner nodes are relay-only from Hetzner-filtered ISPs. No code change filed.

issues.title: NAT traversal is unreachable from x0x's dial shapes: hot paths dial by address, discarding known PeerIds — desktops never punch, never relay (100%-connectable directive)
issues.body:
Joint verdict of a dual independent deep dive (Claude + omp, 2026-08-24). Full reports: `.scratch/claude-report-antquic-throughput.md` precursor + `.scratch/omp-report-nat-traversal.md` (stage-by-stage file:line table).

Live desktops show `nat_traversal_attempts: 0`, `relayed_connections: 0`. The ant-quic ladder (Direct → HolePunch → MASQUE Relay, per ADR-005/006/008) is CODE-LIVE but **unreachable from x0x's dial shapes**:

issues.title: reader throughput: unread Assembler chunks on live connections drain on a ~30-min time constant under churn (residual after #368)
issues.body:
Residual observed during the #368 proof run (x0xd on ant-quic 0.27.44, ttt sidecar, MallocStackLogging, LAN churn 22 min then off):

- 1.25 KB class = single stack `Bytes::copy_from_slice ← ant_quic::connection::assembler::Assembler::insert ← StreamsState::received ← Connection::process_payload` — unread inbound stream chunks on **live** connections (no sg frames, no 48 B pairing — not the fixed #368 mechanism).
- Peaked **28 min after churn ended** (49.5k blocks, `recv_streams_with_unread` 3,546 across ~35 open connections), then drained 39 % in 5 min (30.3k / 1,073). Long-period sawtooth, not monotonic.
- Bounded per connection by the 16 MiB receive window, but 35 connections × up to 16 MiB is still ~0.5 GB of transient residency, and the drain constant means a degraded host (cf. the original studio1 state) may never catch up.

Angles: x0x's reader task does `read_to_end` **sequentially per connection** (one stream at a time) feeding a bounded `data_tx`; under gossip bursts unread streams queue in the assembler. Options: concurrent stream reads per connection with a per-connection budget; recv-pump back-pressure visibility; ant-quic #255 assembler reaping / smaller windows as the durable bound. Measure with `/diagnostics/transport` (`recv_streams_with_unread`, `recv_buffered`) before changing anything.

issues.title: pubsub: spawn_ihave_flusher has no shutdown handle — livelocks all workers after transport shutdown (x0xd SIGTERM hang)
issues.body:
Found while fixing saorsa-labs/x0x#368 / #371 (x0xd on saorsa-gossip 0.5.71).

After the transport shuts down, `spawn_ihave_flusher` keeps looping: every flush attempt fails with "node not initialized", the failure is logged at WARN and the loop immediately retries, saturating all 16 runtime workers (~10 Hz per LAN peer, +700 MB RSS during shutdown, ~10 MB of WARN logs in seconds). There is no cancellation/shutdown handle the embedding daemon can signal, so the process never exits on SIGTERM — x0x has shipped a 5 s force-exit watchdog as an interim.

Ask: give the flusher (and any sibling long-lived pubsub tasks) a shutdown token it `select!`s on, and treat a transport 'not initialized'/closed error as terminal for the task rather than retry-forever. Expose the token (or a `shutdown()` on PubSubManager/runtime) so embedders can drive a clean stop. Related: x0x#371, saorsa-gossip#41.

issues.title: named groups: concurrent self-leave of the last two members leaves a live zero-member group with no withdrawal tombstone
issues.body:
Pre-existing race surfaced while reviewing PR #370 (#369 sole-member delete).

`leave_disposition` is evaluated once per daemon on its own roster snapshot. Two-admin (or admin+member) group, both `DELETE /groups/:id` inside the same window: each sees a 2-member roster → `Proceed` → emits `MemberRemoved(self)`, does `groups.remove(&id)`, stops its listener. The peer's MemberRemoved is rejected on arrival (group absent, named_groups.rs ~:6149); third parties see a PrevHashMismatch on one of the two. Nobody ever seals a withdrawn commit, so the public discovery card and relay caches keep advertising a live zero-member group with no anti-resurrection record.

Options: (a) the second-to-last leaver's MemberRemoved apply on a daemon that just left should still be able to seal a withdrawal for a now-empty roster; (b) a third party (relay/any member applying the commit log) that observes the roster reach zero seals the tombstone; (c) document as accepted and let discovery cards age out. ADR-0016's #369 amendment must describe the real behaviour, not a convergence guarantee the code doesn't provide.

issues.title: ~4 MB residue survives every connection Close (x0x#368): locate what a Closed generation retains
issues.body:
Heap profile from x0x (saorsa-labs/x0x#368, MallocStackLogging, bare x0xd 0.39.0 on ant-quic 0.27.41, 57 min): ~400 MB live in `SendStream::write` buffers and ~390 MB in `Assembler::insert` copies, on connections to peers that stalled (NAT'd half-open paths, slow consumers). The caller opens a uni stream per gossip message; when the send times out the caller currently neither resets the stream nor closes the connection, so both ends pin the per-stream state indefinitely. The caller-side fix is landing in x0x, but ant-quic has no defence of its own:

1. **No per-connection cap on aggregate buffered outbound stream bytes.** A caller can open N uni streams against a connection whose peer never reads; each stream buffers independently and the sum is unbounded (flow control bounds each stream/connection window, but the caller-side `write_all` futures keep the data queued before it even reaches the window).
2. **No reaping of assembler state for streams that make no progress.** A stream whose sender stops mid-message (peer cooled it) keeps its partial `Assembler` buffers until the connection closes, which on a half-open path may be never (see #235/#238 idle-gate behaviour).

Proposed: (a) a `TransportConfig` knob bounding total buffered-but-unsent bytes per connection, after which new `write` awaits or fails fast; (b) reap receive-side stream state with no progress for > T (connection-level idle timeout is too coarse when keep-alives keep the path 'alive'). Related: #244 (drop ⇒ fi

issues.title: macOS: x0xd ignores SIGTERM (no exit after 13s+, needs SIGKILL) — reproduced on v0.39.0 bare daemon
issues.body:
Long-observed ("OPEN: macOS SIGTERM hang" in session notes since v0.32) but never filed. Reproduced today on two bare `x0xd 0.39.0` official-binary instances on macOS 26.6 (M-series):

- `x0xd --name leakctl --api-port 12798 --skip-update-check` (prod bootstrap, ~3h uptime, 3.1 GB RSS)
- `x0xd --name leakctl2 --api-port 12797 --no-hard-coded-bootstrap --skip-update-check` (~1h uptime, 770 MB)

`kill <pid>` (SIGTERM) → both still running after 13 s with no log output indicating shutdown began; `kill -9` required. Earlier today the tic-tac-toe sidecar on studio1 (0.37.4, 142 GB RSS) behaved the same (SIGTERM, 6 s, then -9).

Impact: the #261/#363 transactional upgrade handoff "cancels gracefully within a 5 s bound" and test harnesses' DaemonFixture teardown both assume SIGTERM works — on macOS they fall through to the hard path and lose the clean-shutdown guarantees (dhat dumps, WAL flush, GroupDeleted/withdraw fan-out). Possibly related to the large-RSS state (#368) if shutdown is blocked on a stalled task, but the 770 MB instance hung identically.

Repro: start a bare daemon, wait for peers > 0, `kill -TERM`, watch `kill -0` for 30 s.

issues.title: named groups: sole-member group is undeletable — last-admin precheck fires with misleading guidance when no other member exists
issues.body:
Observed live on v0.37.4 (ttt e2e, 2026-08-20), and the HEAD precheck appears to behave the same.

Repro: A creates `public_open` group, B joins, B leaves. Roster on A now shows exactly `[(A, admin)]`. `DELETE /groups/:id` from A returns:

```
409 {"error":"a group must always have at least one admin; make another member an admin before leaving"}
```

…but there is no other member to promote. The creator can never dispose of their own empty group via the leave path.

`last_admin_self_leave_precheck_error` (src/groups/mod.rs:288) removes the leaver from a proposed roster and enforces the last-admin invariant on the remainder — an empty remainder fails the invariant, so a sole member is permanently blocked. If the intended disband path for an empty group is `POST /groups/:id/state/withdraw`, the 409 should say so; better, a sole-member self-leave should disband (or auto-withdraw) the group.

Found during the two-machine tic-tac-toe e2e (Gate 8 cleanup): the `cutest-e2e-154538` group is now orphaned on the creator.

issues.title: CRDT task deltas: non-checkbox operations merged without authorship verification (apply path ignores envelope-verified sender)
issues.body:
Found during the ADR-012 gossip-signature audit (hardening item 3). This is an **application-layer** integrity gap, independent of the transport signature.

## The gap

The task-list CRDT apply path decodes `(peer_id, delta)` from the payload and merges using that **self-declared** `peer_id`, never the envelope-verified `msg.sender`:

- `src/crdt/sync.rs:359` — `decode_delta::<TaskListDelta>(&msg.payload)` → `(peer_id, delta)`
- `src/crdt/sync.rs:362` — `list.merge_delta(&delta, peer_id)` — uses the payload peer_id; `msg.sender` (the V2-envelope-verified author) is never consulted here.

Checkbox **claim/complete** operations DO carry a verified inner `OpAttestation` (`src/crdt/task_item.rs:288,387`; verified in `purge_unattested_elements` → `verify_attestation`, `src/crdt/provenance.rs:274-283`). But `added_tasks` (creation), `task_updates` (title/description/assignee/priority), `name_update`, and `ordering_update` are LWW-merged with **no authorship check** — vector-clock only.

## Impact

Any participant on the group's task topic (membership-gated, so not an open-internet attacker) can inject, rename, reassign, or reorder tasks attributed to another member, and it is applied. The V2 gossip envelope *does* authenticate the true sender end-to-end (`src/gossip/pubsub.rs:1225` signs the full payload; unverified dropped at `:830`) — the apply path simply doesn't use that identity for task-content authorization.

issues.title: MemberBanned fan-out shares the one-shot delivery gap fixed for MemberRemoved/GroupDeleted (#333 family)
issues.body:
Found during the #333 slice C/D build: `ban_treekem_group_member` (named_groups.rs ~:13167) emits `MemberBanned` through a byte-identical fan-out block to the one `MemberRemoved` used — one gossip publish + best-effort DMs, no repair. Slice C/D added a bounded two-channel resend schedule (`spawn_group_control_event_redelivery`) to the MemberRemoved and GroupDeleted sites; the ban site was deliberately left out of that PR to keep scope exact.

A lost `MemberBanned` means the banned peer retains group state until some later event triggers reactive catch-up — same shape as the #333 hops. Fix is mechanical: wire the same redelivery helper at the ban fan-out and add a fault-injection test mirroring the MemberRemoved one (the drop-hook plumbing already generalizes by event kind).

Deliberately NOT in scope: self-leave `MemberRemoved` (leave_treekem_group/leave_group) — the leaver already knows; there is no notice to lose.

issues.title: relay_server: distinguish clean read-direction end from mid-frame cancellation so intact teardowns can finish (follow-up to #248)
issues.body:
From omp's #248 review (approved; adjudicated follow-up, not blocker) and Greptile's finding on the same site:

`run_stream_forwarding_loop`'s read-direction exit currently classifies EVERY teardown as compromised (`send_stream_intact = false`), because `select!` cancels the write direction at an arbitrary await point. Consequence: a client that gracefully half-closes while still reading loses complete-but-unacked reverse frames to the reset.

Today that's unreachable by in-repo clients — `MasqueRelaySocket::finish()` fires only at full socket teardown, when the client's recv half is being dropped simultaneously — and the conservative classification sits on the safe side of #248's thesis (a misparsed frame is worse than a lost tail). But the precise version is clean:

1. A frame-boundary flag around the length/data write pair (set dirty before writing the length prefix, clean after the data write completes).
2. Distinguish a clean framed-read end from a read error on the recv direction.
3. On clean-read-end + frame-boundary-clean: finish instead of drop-reset.

The site comment in relay_server.rs already half-documents the trade-off; this issue exists so the next reader doesn't rediscover it.

issues.title: no-default-features build cannot accept loopback connections (fallback create_dual_stack_sockets doesn't share the v6-assigned port)
issues.body:
## Defect

With `--no-default-features` (i.e. without `network-discovery`), a `P2pEndpoint` cannot accept connections at all — a loopback `connect_addr()` to another endpoint's advertised `local_addr()` hangs until timeout.

Repro (fails on current master):

```rust
let a = P2pEndpoint::new(cfg(127.0.0.1:0)).await?;
let b = P2pEndpoint::new(cfg(127.0.0.1:0)).await?;
let addr = normalize(b.local_addr()?); // 127.0.0.1:port
timeout(5s, a.connect_addr(addr)).await // Elapsed(())
```

`cargo test --no-default-features --test <repro>` → `Err(Elapsed(()))`.

## Root cause

The fallback `create_dual_stack_sockets` in `src/high_level/runtime/dual_stack.rs` (the `#[cfg(not(feature = "network-discovery"))]` version) binds `[::]:{port}` and `0.0.0.0:{port}` with `port = 0` — the two sockets get **independent OS-assigned ports**, and the v6-assigned port is never propagated to the v4 bind. The network-discovery version does this correctly (`actual_port` propagation). The advertised `local_addr()` therefore points at a port the v4 listener never bound.

## Impact

Any downstream crate building ant-quic with `default-features = false` gets a transport that can dial but never accept. Exposed by PR #229's repromotion tests (temporarily gated on the feature in that PR).

## Fix direction

Mirror the port propagation from the feature-gated version, or bind v4 first and reuse its port for v6. Found while validating #229/#209 for release v0.27.38.

issues.title: Proposal: per-key write authority (AccessPolicy variant) for open directory stores
issues.body:
Every current access policy routes write authority through a single store
owner (`is_authorized`, `src/kv/store.rs:768`). That fits app stores, team
workspaces and tamper-evident logs. It does not fit the "open directory"
shape: one topic, many mutually-unknown agents, each writing only their own
key, discoverable by a newcomer who knows none of them in advance.

Today that shape has to be encoded either as a single blessed owner writing
on everyone's behalf (a server), or as one store per publisher that readers
join individually (which needs the `expected_owner` you don't have yet — it
defeats discovery). We took a third path and re-implemented request/response
anti-entropy over raw gossip in our app, ~700 lines duplicating `src/kv/sync.rs`
without its hardening. That's the smell that prompted this.

**Shape being asked about.** A policy where authorization is a predicate over
`(writer, key)` rather than `(writer, owner)` — the simplest binding being
that a key is writable only by the agent it names, e.g. the key must be
prefixed with the writer's `AgentId`. The predicate, whatever a variant for
it would end up called:

```rust
<variant> => key_agent_prefix(key) == Some(writer),
```

One constraint from your code rather than from me: such a variant has to be
appended LAST — bincode encodes variants positionally, and the comment at
`store.rs:79` is explicit that inserting mid-enum corrupts existing stores.

issues.title: cold-start latency: first durable DM to a new peer costs ~17.5s (gossip cold success path)
issues.body:
Found during PR #334 (ADR 0030 slice 4, product durable-by-default). Measured on two-daemon loopback:

- first durable send to a peer: 17,476 ms
- second: 439 ms
- third: 191 ms

Why hidden until now: product sends previously took the raw-QUIC fast path (prefer_raw_quic_if_connected: true). Durable sends correctly skip raw QUIC (a transport receipt is not a commit), so the first POST to a new peer pays gossip publish + reverse ACK cold. The daemon budget is already 8s x 2 attempts + 8s backoff ~= 24s; ttt already uses DIRECT_SEND_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 30s.

Required before any fix claim: a stage breakdown of the 17.5s (strict-gate/forced-refresh vs publish vs reverse-ACK). Note: advert warm-on-connect does NOT obviously fix this - in the #334 investigation the capability-store wait had already returned before the slow send. Do not claim warm-on-connect is the fix until the split is measured.

Candidate directions after the breakdown: advert warm-on-connect (may only shave the ~3s forced refresh), pre-establishing the gossip mesh path on first contact, reverse-ACK route warmup.

Release-note fact for 0.38.0 (per cross-review ruling): first durable DM to a new peer will succeed (clients calibrated to 30s) but feels ~17s until this is fixed. Deliberately NOT an api-reference SLA - that would freeze a limitation as a contract.

Refs: PR #334, channel ruling 2026-08-15T18:39Z. Sibling 0.38.x follow-up: #335.

Do NOT take the later 6a58d81 AckRoute refactor (entangled with raw-frame transport).

**Why it matters:** the ttt desktop's `require_bounded_agent_delegation` path looks up the delegation root on the *owner* daemon and requires an Outbound `LocalSend` row matching the canonical root id — when the dedupe id is exposed instead, the lookup is a silent `None` and cold child wake fails. **Evidence:** `record_group_public_history` (named_groups.rs:9355) is correct by construction (artifact = `serde_json::to_vec(msg)`, payload = body bytes, scope = `msg.group_id`), so rows from it must project canonically. The nondeterminism implies a racing recorder writes the sender-side row first with a payload/artifact shape that fails `group_history_message` recovery, and the store's dedupe then keeps that row. Root-causing which recorder wins the race is the first task.

issues.title: Address validation rejects all candidates with port < 1024 as Suspicious — silently defeats ADR-0011 dual-port :443 reachability fleet-wide
issues.body:
Found during the x0x asymmetric-delivery investigation (2026-08-08 candidate-validation trace).

`perform_address_validation` (src/connection/nat_traversal.rs:858) marks any advertised candidate with `addr.port() < 1024` as `Suspicious` → rejected as `SecurityValidationFailed`. The verdict is cached per exact SocketAddr with **no TTL** (cleanup only above 1000 entries, dropping an arbitrary half), so the rejection is permanent for the connection's life.

Fleet impact: the x0x bootstrap fleet runs a second daemon on UDP 443 per host (ADR-0011) precisely to traverse full-tunnel VPN / CGNAT / DPI networks. Every ADD_ADDRESS carrying a `:443` candidate is silently rejected — no PATH_CHALLENGE probe, no candidate pair (so never a migration target), no port prediction, and no `PeerAddressAdvertised` → bootstrap-cache/peer-hint learning. The exact reachability :443 exists to provide is unavailable to NAT-traversal candidate exchange.

(Since 0.27.36 / #221 the rejection is logged at debug! only; on ≤0.27.35 it produced the recurring "Failed to add remote candidate: security validation failed" WARNs.)

Suggested fix: drop or scope the privileged-port heuristic (e.g. allowlist 443, or only flag ports < 1024 when combined with another suspicion signal), and give the validation cache a TTL so transient verdicts aren't permanent.

issues.title: upsert_discovered_machine: unbounded address accumulation + 5s-per-dead-candidate reconnect cost
issues.body:
## Context

PR #307 fixed the immediate issue (issue #304): inbound peers from  now have their observed address recorded in `machine_discovery_cache` via `upsert_discovered_machine`. A reviewer noted two residual caveats in the implementation that are worth tracking separately.

## Residual Issues

### 1. Unbounded address accumulation

`upsert_discovered_machine` deduplicates addresses but never evicts stale ones. Every new inbound connection for the same peer adds an address to the list if it is not already present. For peers behind mobile or symmetric NAT, the source port changes on every reconnect, so the address list grows unboundedly over the daemon's lifetime. This is a memory leak proportional to reconnect frequency.

**Affected code:** `src/lib.rs` — `upsert_discovered_machine` function.

**Suggested fix:** cap the address list per peer to a sensible maximum (e.g. 8 most-recently-seen addresses) and/or apply a TTL at the same point as `last_seen`.

### 2. 5s-per-dead-candidate reconnect cost

The proactive-reconnect candidate loop tries each address in `m.addresses` sequentially. If stale addresses accumulate from mobile/symmetric-NAT sessions, every reconnect attempt incurs a 5-second dial timeout per dead address before reaching a working one. For a peer that has cycled through many NAT-assigned ports, this significantly delays connection recovery.

**Affected code:** `src/lib.rs` — reconnect candidate loop that iterates `candidate_addrs`.

**Suggested fix:** eithe

## Problem

When peer B dials peer A (inbound connection from A's perspective) and that connection later dies, A holds `candidate_addrs=0` for B in `machine_discovery_cache`. The proactive-reconnect loop at `src/lib.rs:9722` only dials addresses from `machine_discovery_cache`, so it finds an empty candidate set and the LAN dial that would succeed is never attempted.

**Root cause:** The `PeerConnected` handler in `lib.rs` only called `dm.mark_connected()` and cancelled pending reconnect tasks. It never wrote the peer's observed `address` into `machine_discovery_cache`. **Consequence:** After the inbound connection drops:
- `GET /peers` returns `[]` for B (no candidates)  
- A's 10 proactive LAN redials all time out  
- `B→A` continues delivering over the old (stale) connection while A reports 0 peers  
- A's sends return HTTP 200 + msg_id but never arrive (silent black-hole)

This was confirmed as the blocking issue in the stage-1 acceptance test for the bidirectional delivery investigation (results-stage1-acceptance-20260808-151336.txt, section P2).

## Fix

In the `PeerConnected` event handler, call `upsert_discovered_machine` with the peer's observed remote `address` so the reconnect loop can find it. Skip the `0.0.0.0:0` placeholder the accept loop substitutes when `remote_addr` is unavailable.

## Summary

Running the pre-commit hook on a **clean, unmodified checkout of `main`** (confirmed at `b9971f9`) causes `cargo hakari verify` to exit with a non-zero status. This means the hook fails with no user changes in place.

## Impact

Both the PR #33 author's commits and the reviewer's commits used `--no-verify` as a direct result of this breakage. Bypassing the hook with `--no-verify` silently disables:

- `-D warnings` enforcement
- Forbidden-pattern checks (e.g., `unwrap()`, `panic!()` guards)
- Any other hook steps that run after hakari verify

This trains contributors to habitually skip the hook rather than fix the underlying drift, and means the guard rails are effectively absent on every commit made while the hook is broken.

## Root cause

The `workspace-hack` crate managed by `cargo-hakari` has drifted from the state `hakari verify` expects, but the drift exists in the committed `main` tree — not in any local modification. Either:

1. A previous commit updated `Cargo.toml` / `Cargo.lock` without regenerating `workspace-hack`, or
2. The `cargo-hakari` version installed locally differs from the version that generated the current `workspace-hack`.

## Suggested fix

One of:

- Run `cargo hakari generate` and commit the updated `workspace-hack`, resolving the drift.
- Pin `cargo-hakari` in a `rust-toolchain.toml` or `Makefile` so all contributors use the same version.

issues.body:
## Summary

Calling `connect_cached_peer(victim_peer)` against a poisoned or stale cache entry that now points at a different node ("Carol") leaves the caller **connected to Carol** with Carol added to the bootstrap cache via `add_from_connection` + `record_success`, while the call returns `Err`. `ant-quic::connect_peer_with_addrs` does not enforce the requested `PeerId` on the resulting connection. When the identity check finds a mismatch it warns and returns `Err`, but:

- The mismatched connection to Carol remains open (leaked).
- Carol has been added to the bootstrap cache with a `record_success` entry.
- The victim peer gets a `record_failure`.

- **Not an auth bypass**: identity is correctly identified; plane + connect-ACL gates still apply. The caller cannot send authenticated traffic to the wrong peer.
- **Cache poisoning**: a single mismatched dial permanently inverts the quality s

issues.title: Per-topic transport mutex map is never pruned
issues.body:
The transport keeps a per-topic in-flight lock map that only ever grows — one entry per distinct topic ever ensured, never removed. Under topic churn (many short-lived channels) this is an unbounded-growth / slow memory leak.

Code:
- `src/transport.rs:141` — `inflight: dashmap::DashMap<String, Arc<tokio::sync::Mutex<()>>>` ("One entry per topic ever ensured").
- `src/transport.rs:267` — `ensure_topic` does `inflight.entry(topic).or_insert_with(...)` and never removes entries.
- The sibling `topics` map (`src/transport.rs:137`) has the same lifetime property but is the source of truth for active subscriptions; the `inflight` lock map has no reason to persist past a successful ensure.

Fix: drop the per-topic `inflight` entry once `ensure_topic` completes (topic is now in `topics`), or bound the map. Guard against the ensure race while removing.

Scheduled to land in bridge-v2 M1a.

issues.title: NIP-42 relay-tag check skipped — AUTH replayable across bridges within the window
issues.body:
NIP-42 auth verification validates the challenge and time window but does **not** check the `relay` tag of the auth event. An AUTH event signed for one bridge is therefore replayable against any other bridge whose challenge it happens to match within the asymmetric validity window — the relay tag is what binds an AUTH to a specific relay URL.

Code:
- `src/proto.rs:89` — doc comment: "`relay` tag is NOT checked (loopback bridge has no stable URL; documented ...)".
- `src/proto.rs:91` — `verify_auth_event()` checks only the `challenge` tag and timestamp window; no `relay` tag assertion.
- `src/main.rs:42` — on a non-loopback bind this is only a `warn!`, not enforcement.

Fix: give the bridge a stable relay URL (from `BRIDGE_BIND` / config), pass it into `verify_auth_event`, and require the auth event `relay` tag to match it. Keep the loopback allowance behind explicit config if needed, but validate by default on non-loopback binds.

Safe under the default loopback bind; must be closed before any non-loopback deployment. Scheduled to land in bridge-v2 M1a.

issues.title: No cap on concurrent WebSocket connections
issues.body:
The relay accepts unbounded concurrent WebSocket connections. On a non-loopback bind this is a resource-exhaustion vector — the non-loopback warning (`src/main.rs:42`) documents the exposure but nothing bounds it.

Code:
- `src/relay.rs:205` — `.on_upgrade(move |socket| handle_connection(state, socket))` spawns a per-connection task with no admission control.
- `src/relay.rs:242` — `handle_connection`; each connection holds a send queue + subscription registrations with no global ceiling.

Fix: add a global connection cap (e.g. a `Semaphore` / atomic counter in `AppState`) and reject/close new upgrades past the limit; make the limit configurable.

Safe under the default loopback bind; must be closed before any non-loopback deployment. Scheduled to land in bridge-v2 M1a.

issues.title: NIP-11 info document has no active unit test
issues.body:
The NIP-11 relay-information endpoint is served but no non-ignored test exercises it, so the advertised `supported_nips` / document shape can regress silently.

Code:
- `src/relay.rs:207` — `router` returns `nip11_response()` when the request is a NIP-11 doc request rather than a WS upgrade.
- `src/relay.rs:214` — `is_nip11()` (Accept: `application/nostr+json`).
- `src/relay.rs:225` — `nip11_response()`; `src/relay.rs:229` declares `"supported_nips": [1, 11, 16, 42, 50]`.

The only coverage today is the `#[ignore]`-gated e2e readiness probe (`tests/e2e_convergence.rs:170`, `accept: application/nostr+json`), which does not run under `cargo nextest run` / CI.

Fix: add a hermetic unit test that drives `router(state)` with a NIP-11 Accept header and asserts status 200, `content-type: application/nostr+json`, and the `supported_nips` set.

Scheduled to land in bridge-v2 M1a.

issues.title: [docs] api-reference.md missing the ADR-0023 history endpoints (/history, /history/search, /diagnostics/history)
issues.body:
The v0.34.3 endpoint registry (src/api/mod.rs, "History (ADR-0023 durable local history)" section) registers GET /history (keyset-paginated per scope), GET /history/search (scoped FTS), and GET /diagnostics/history — but docs/api-reference.md documents none of them (grep for \`/history\` returns nothing on main).

Found during bridge-v2 M1a recon: an agent auditing against api-reference.md concluded the history API "does not exist in 0.34.3", which is false — the docs gap actively misleads integrators (and agents). tic-tac-toe Stage 1+ integrates against these routes, so the reference needs to be authoritative.

Related: #275 (scope-less search + GET /history/scopes) should update the same section when it lands.

issues.title: [config] misplaced data_dir under [gossip] silently falls back to default — multi-daemon boxes collide on history.db
issues.body:
Found during the v0.34.3 prod rollout (2026-07-23): the fleet x0xd-443.toml files had data_dir nested under [gossip] instead of top level. The daemon silently ignored it and used the default data dir (/root/.local/share/x0x), so x0xd and x0xd-443 on the same box BOTH resolved history.db to the same path; the exclusive-open design (ADR-0023) then failed the second daemon in a restart loop (\"history initialization failed: pragma setup failed\"). Pre-0.34.3 this was invisible because there was no exclusive-locked DB.

Two hardening asks:
1. History init errors should include the RESOLVED db path in the message (\"pragma setup failed\" alone sent debugging down a lock-contention path when the real cause was path resolution).
2. Config validation: warn loudly (or refuse to start) on known keys found in the wrong section (data_dir under [gossip] being the observed case). Silent fallback to defaults is what made this invisible for months.

Fleet configs fixed in place on 5/6 boxes during the rollout (saorsa-7 pending a console reset).

issues.title: [testnet] Pre-existing x0xd RSS growth (120-245 MB/h) is killing 4 GB fleet nodes
issues.body:
Elevated from the ADR-0023 soak (2026-07-22): the pre-existing RSS growth pattern (21-195 MB/h measured during the soak; <phone> MB/h envelope documented 2026-07-18) is no longer just a watch item — it is the prime suspect for two fleet node losses on 2026-07-23.

Evidence:
- saorsa-2 and saorsa-7 both wedged with kernel-alive/userland-dead (sshd accepts TCP, sends zero banner bytes); saorsa-2 recovered fully from a bare power-cycle with memory back to 758/3915 MB.
- saorsa-6 (healthy) is at 329 MB available of 3.8 GB, load 3.81, following the same trajectory.
- Soak doc: history layer adds NO new leak signal; this predates ADR-0023. SFO daemon self-restarted mid-soak with RSS 1.2 GB pre-restart.

Per the soak, this item owns the 12-24h soak sign-off. Needs: a tracked RSS profile (dhat or heaptrack on a long-running daemon), identification of the growth source, and a documented mitigation (leak fix or scheduled rolling restarts as a stopgap).

Refs: .testnet-logs/adr0023-soak-20260722/SUMMARY.md; #271 comment trail.

issues.title: [history] Salt MLS epoch-derived msg_id with group scope (cross-group dedupe collision)
issues.body:
From the #268 review (Greptile finding 2, verified real-but-narrow 2026-07-23):

src/history/record.rs compute_epoch_msg_id derives msg_id = blake3(domain | epoch | payload), and Store::insert dedupes GLOBALLY on msg_id (src/history/store.rs:166-176). Two identical plaintexts sent to two DIFFERENT groups whose MLS epochs happen to coincide produce the same msg_id — the second insert is silently dropped as Duplicate.

Fix: mix the group scope (stable_id) into the epoch hash. Signed-envelope rows are unaffected (artifact includes recipient/signature); local sends already nonce-salted.

Severity: low — requires identical payload + same epoch across groups — but the drop is silent.

issues.title: [flake] named_group admin-delete propagation integration coverage intermittent
issues.body:
Named follow-up from 2026-07-22: the delete-propagation integration coverage (tests/named_group_integration.rs — named_group_admin_delete_propagates_to_peer_after_creator_delete_409 family, currently #[ignore]d integration tier) flakes intermittently.

Filing to track: needs a captured failure log, a rerun count to quantify the rate, and either a fix or a documented quarantine reason. The harness already enforces peering before propagation-dependent assertions (tests/harness/src/cluster.rs:398-402), so the residual flake is elsewhere — candidate areas: withdrawn-tombstone retention timing, TreeKEM roster advance vs GroupDeleted ordering.

issues.title: [voice] voice_call demo: honor connection deadline; harden e2e pacing and restricted-network gating
issues.body:
Greptile findings on #270 (merged), confirmed valid:

1. examples/voice_call.rs:160-168 — when the 10s connection deadline expires the loop falls through and signaling proceeds into unbounded receive_message() waits; the demo can hang instead of reporting the failed connection. Fix: break with connected=false and assert (suggestion in the PR review comment).
2. tests/voice_e2e.rs can pass on restricted networks without exercising the pipeline — require an explicit lane-open / frames-delivered marker so a no-op environment fails loudly.
3. The e2e sender bursts rather than pacing 20ms frames like the demo, so jitter behavior is untested — pace the sender.

issues.title: [voice] Expose unreliable datagram lane through the x0x adapter seam (V1.3 gap)
issues.body:
The #270 demo runs on a Reliable ordered ADR-0022 stream lane. saorsa-webrtc-core 0.5.0 ships the datagram audio lane + mandatory jitter buffer (WP-V1.3), but the x0x voice adapter seam (src/voice/, X0xSignaling + WebRtcV1) does not expose an unreliable lane yet. This is the one gap between the merged demo and full V1.3 voice.

Work: extend the WebRtcV1 adapter to negotiate and open an unreliable datagram lane via the capability exchange; route AudioDatagram wire frames over it; extend tests/voice_e2e.rs to assert jitter counters (reordered/late/duplicate) under an actually-unreliable lane.

Refs: PR #270 body (lane mode note), saorsa-webrtc 7077017 (datagram lane).

issues.title: [testnet] saorsa-7 (Nuremberg) SSH unrecoverable post-fail2ban; move fleet monitoring off SSH loops
issues.body:
From the ADR-0023 soak (2026-07-22, .testnet-logs/adr0023-soak-20260722/SUMMARY.md findings 2-3):

Frequent SSH sampling (sgp-sampler.sh) tripped DO-host rate-limits/fail2ban across the fleet. NYC and SFO recovered after bans aged out (~hours); saorsa-7 (Nuremberg, 116.203.101.172) never recovered and needs the provider web console (check sshd/fail2ban, restart).

Systemic fix: fleet monitoring should ride the mesh/API (per-node /health is already open; /presence behind token) instead of SSH polling loops; add fail2ban whitelist entries for the monitoring source IPs as a stopgap.

issues.title: testnet runner: reload API token after rotation (ordinary restarts reuse token)
issues.body:
Observed in the ADR-0023 4h soak (2026-07-22, .testnet-logs/adr0023-soak-20260722/SUMMARY.md finding 1):

A daemon-only restart orphans the co-located test runner — x0xd regenerates its API token at startup; the runner holds the stale token and 401s until manually restarted. Masked on deploys because both units restart together; SFO self-restarted mid-soak and exposed it.

Fix options: runner re-reads the token file on 401 and retries once, or a watchdog restarts both units together. The token re-read is the smaller change and also covers watchdog lag.

issues.title: [history] Scope-less search and GET /history/scopes enumeration
issues.body:
ADR-0023 phase 3 shipped scoped reads only: scope is a REQUIRED query param on GET /history and GET /history/search (src/server/routes/history.rs:25). Two deferred gaps:

1. Scope-less search: clients cannot run an FTS query across all scopes (e.g. find a phrase without knowing which DM/group it was in). The store HistoryQuery already accepts scope: None — the REST surface does not.
2. No GET /history/scopes: clients cannot discover which scopes have rows without knowing them a priori. Add an enumeration endpoint (scope_kind, scope_id, row count, newest seen_at_ms) so UIs can list conversations.

Deferred follow-ups from the ADR-0023 M0 merge (#268).

issues.title: P2pLinkTransport: dial_addr hangs on loopback between bare endpoints; accept() ignores ProtocolId
issues.body:
Found during saorsa-webrtc V1.3 datagram-lane work (2026-07-22), on ant-quic 0.27.34:

1. **`P2pLinkTransport::dial_addr` hangs indefinitely on loopback** between two bare `P2pConfig::builder()` endpoints — a 15 s dial timeout fires inside `connect_orchestrated` and the dial never completes, while the `Node`-mediated connect path on the same machines connects sub-second. Reproduced while building saorsa-webrtc's two-real-nodes datagram e2e (the test switched to the Node path as a workaround: `Node::inner_endpoint().get_quic_connection(&peer)` → `P2pLinkConn`).
2. **`P2pLinkTransport::accept` ignores its `ProtocolId` argument** — matches the in-code TODO; all acceptors currently receive all protocols.

Neither blocks downstream work (the Node path + LinkConn's public `send_datagram`/`recv_datagrams` cover the use case), but both make the standalone link-transport surface a trap for new consumers.

issues.title: rustls floor under-constrained: MLKEM1024 requires rustls ≥0.23.40, Cargo.toml declares 0.23.35
issues.body:
Found during the saorsa-webrtc ant-quic 0.27.34 upgrade (2026-07-22).

`src/crypto/pqc/pqc_crypto_provider.rs:128` uses `rustls::crypto::aws_lc_rs::kx_group::MLKEM1024`, which only exists from **rustls 0.23.40**. `Cargo.toml:111` declares `rustls = { version = "0.23.35", ... }`.

Any downstream whose lockfile resolves rustls in the 0.23.35–0.23.39 window fails to compile ant-quic with a missing-item error (reproduced in the saorsa-webrtc workspace, whose lock pinned 0.23.36). Fresh resolutions pick ≥0.23.40 and hide the bug.

One-line fix: bump the rustls floor to `0.23.40`.

issues.title: Synthetic peer_id_from_socket_addr placeholders (10-byte hash+port, 22 zero bytes) can leak into sessions/hole-punch targets
issues.body:
`peer_id_from_socket_addr` (p2p_endpoint.rs:703) builds a synthetic placeholder PeerId — DefaultHasher(addr) in bytes 0-7, port in 8-9, zeros elsewhere — documented as "must not be persisted or compared across builds". Production logs show these phantom ids reaching NAT-traversal sessions (`is not synchronized` warn floods for exactly these ids at hundreds/sec on startup) and hole-punch targets (`await_hole_punch_outcome polled event for target PeerId([...0,0,0])`). Sessions keyed on phantom peers can never authenticate and generate warn spam proportional to activity (37-40k/6h observed on healthy prod nodes).

Asks: (1) assert/guard that synthetic ids never reach bootstrap-cache persistence or `add_bootstrap_node`; (2) rate-limit or demote the `is not synchronized` warn (it is activity-proportional noise at WARN level — 50k+/6h on healthy nodes drowns real signals); (3) same for `add_remote_candidate: security validation failed` (23-52k/6h on healthy nodes).

issues.title: Defense-in-depth: supervise/respawn the endpoint driver instead of terminal driver_lost

issues.title: Transport wedge: daemon reports healthy with peers:0 while its QUIC socket is completely silent (prod NYC, 6+ hours)
issues.body:
Observed on prod bootstrap saorsa-2 (142.93.199.50), v0.33.1, 2026-07-18.

Symptoms:
- `/health` returned `{"ok":true,"status":"healthy","peers":0}` for the entire 6.4 h process uptime.
- 10 s packet captures showed ZERO packets in or out of the prod daemon's UDP 5483 socket — while the co-located :443 and testnet daemons on the same host were exchanging traffic with remote peers normally (host network fine, ufw inactive).
- The daemon was not even dialing its sibling bootstraps despite peers:0 (no outbound from :5483 at all), yet logged periodic `WARN ant_quic::connection: Failed to add remote candidate: security validation failed` and `send failed ... Peer not found` bursts — so internal tasks were alive against a dead transport.
- Clock NTP-synced (not skew). The same log pattern existed under the PREVIOUS pid too (before an 06:52 restart), so one restart did not clear it; the 13:19 restart did (came back with 14 peers in ~90 s and self-updated to 0.34.0).

Two asks:
1. Root-cause the wedge (ant-quic endpoint driver task death? socket wedge after some error path?) — diagnostics captured pre-restart in /root/x0x-wedge-1784380717/ on saorsa-2 (journal tail; API captures failed auth so mostly journal).
2. `/health` must not report healthy with a silent transport: a bootstrap node with peers:0 and no socket I/O for N minutes should degrade its health status so fleet monitoring catches it — this sat invisible for 6+ hours.

issues.title: Self-update swaps the binary but the restart can fail silently (macOS, terminal-launched daemon) — daemon left DOWN
issues.body:
Observed live during the v0.33.1 → v0.34.0 rollout (2026-07-18, macOS).

The local prod daemon (launched manually as `./target/release/x0xd --skip-update-check` from the repo dir) self-updated after the release published: at 14:16 local the updater sidelined the old binary (`x0xd.backup`) and wrote the new 0.34.0 binary in place — but the process never came back. No x0xd was running until manually relaunched (~8 min gap); the relaunched binary is fine (v0.34.0, healthy, 16 peers), so the swap itself succeeded and only the respawn failed.

Likely related to the known macOS SIGTERM shutdown hang (the shutdown half of restart), and/or a respawn path that assumes argv[0]/cwd or a service manager that isn't there for terminal-launched daemons.

Expected: replace_via_sideline must be transactional through the RESTART, not just the file swap — if the new process fails to come up, roll back to the sidelined binary and keep the old process alive (or at minimum leave a loud artifact + nonzero exit rather than a silent death).

Repro shape: run x0xd from a terminal on macOS with updates enabled, publish a release, wait for the periodic check.
