pulls.title: fix(security): N19 part A — file/welcome consumers require verified sender ids
pulls.body:
## Problem and change

File-transfer and TreeKEM Welcome-blob listeners attributed every decoded frame to `DirectMessage.sender`, even when the transport reported `verified = false`. A peer could therefore claim another agent's identity at these consumers.

Part A requires the DM layer's verified sender binding before decoding or dispatching any file-transfer or Welcome-blob frame. Verified frames retain their existing handling; unverified frames are ignored. The checked sender travels with the decoded payload into the consumer.

## Scope still outstanding

**N19 part B is not implemented in this PR.** Fork-quarantine clearing still needs a durable-gated transition, including post-rename `ReplacedNotDurable`, concurrent readers/writers, restart behavior, and each owner-anchored clear path. The current shared mutation helper publishes the candidate before saving and retains it after a non-durable replacement; a return-status check alone does not protect the quarantine. No part-B regression is claimed here.

## Test-first evidence

Base: `4f49274dbc09be54e502686be332f0c32ea9a44e`.

The first commit extracts the existing decoding operations into behavior-preserving receive-boundary helpers and adds regressions. The next commit adds the verification checks. Tests cover all six file frame variants and all five Welcome-blob variants, plus verified positive controls and malformed input.

pulls.title: fix(cli): N2 — x0x upgrade --apply refuses; install via authenticated POST /upgrade/apply
pulls.body:
The standalone `x0x upgrade` installer could replace `x0xd` after an unauthenticated shutdown attempt and restart it with self-update disabled. Installation now refuses before any I/O and directs the caller to authenticated `POST /upgrade/apply`. `x0x upgrade --check` retains its read-only, verified GitHub manifest check, including `--check --force`.

Refs N2

The refusal option is the smaller safe implementation: it removes the duplicate download/swap/shutdown/restart flow rather than adding another authenticated installation client. The refusal is unconditional for installation, including default invocation and `--force`. This deliberately also disables offline standalone installation: discovering only a default instance cannot establish that no named, custom-data-dir, or concurrently starting daemon uses the binary. The daemon remains responsible for its authenticated upgrade transaction and restart ownership. No routes, authentication rules, or daemon update settings change.

CLI help, the descriptions in `src/api/mod.rs`, and `SKILL.md` describe the same behavior. The obsolete standalone `api.token` reader is removed; corrected `api-token` tests now exercise the shared daemon-client reader (extracted without changing its behavior). Socket-based tests belonging to the deleted standalone download path are removed.

pulls.body:
**N7 (charter I13, W2): plane-isolation config validation.** Reviewer: Codex.

## Defect
- **A misplaced plane key is silently ignored.** `network_id` (or `mdns_enabled`) under a section such as `[gossip]` is dropped by serde. An unset `network_id` resolves to `x0x.prod`, so the daemon joins prod. That is how the testnet ran on the prod plane.

| `network_id` / `mdns_enabled` below the top level, at any depth, including under an unknown section | **refuse to start** | **fail** |
| any other ignored or misplaced key | WARN (now actually emitted) | **fail**, with `FINDING` lines |

## Summary

Product fix for the #1036 P1 syslog flood (~16 GB/day): ant-quic logged a `WARN` for every send to a peer with no connection, and x0x kept sending to such peers indefinitely. pulls.title: fix(groups): #1023 follow-up — recover trimmed roster certificates after MemberAdded
pulls.body:
A joiner seated by a trimmed `MemberAdded` can stop fetching its JoinResult while other roster seats remain digest-only. After a verified, accepted seat event is applied and its sidecar hydrated, the receiver schedules bounded certificate recovery through the existing #946 group-scoped protocol. Recovery runs only for the seated local joiner or a demonstrably trimmed sidecar, and only against a roster matching that event's signed roster root. This moves recovery ahead of the promoted admin's first seal, while a holder is still likely online.

Refs #1023, #1025, #946 and #802. Target: main. No issue-closing keyword until testnet row 3b passes.

- Handles legacy events with an absent/empty sidecar, including the pre-#1025 authority shape.
- Uses the existing request TTL, at most 16 distinct requests per apply, and 25–250 ms send jitter. The 4,096-entry request cache evicts its oldest entry at capacity, so one group cannot block admission of another group's requests. Duplicate drops, cap drops, and evictions are logged at debug level. Adds no wire fields or state maps; rejected/unverified events cannot initiate recovery.
- Tests a 17-seat owner-certified roster (reduced from 22 in round 2 to fit the intentional recovery cap), actual sidecar trimming, event-only seating, signed promotion, #946 handler recovery, and sealing after the last other holder shuts down. A separate negative case preserves `OwnerCertMemberPending` and the retry/deadline distinction when nobody answers.

**ADR 0084 revocation race: a v0.46.0 W2 must-land.**

The accept loop checks machine revocation, then releases the lock before it hands the stream off. This ADR records #1044 (merged into the candidate at e803709 before any ADR existed). #1044 admits an inbound `SyncV1` owner-sync stream from a machine that: - has **no known agent**, and - holds a **verified, current, unrevoked owner enrollment**. Fixes a latent production panic introduced by #1044 (issue #1040). v0.46 DoD blocker under the no-panic rule.

## Bug
#1044 added an enrollment-only admission path for inbound SyncV1 owner-sync streams (`start_stream_accept_loop` → `dispatch_enrolled_owner_sync_stream`). Those streams carry an EMPTY agent list. `PeerStream::agent()` did `self.agents[0]` and would panic if any caller used it on such a stream.

The SyncV1 owner-sync acceptor never called `agent()` and is unchanged.

## What

Fixes #1041: the #985 direct-delivery fallback's `encode_kv_store_delta_direct_payload` serialized `KvStoreDirectDelta` as **serde_json**, which cannot serialize the delta's non-string-keyed maps — the OR-Set's `HashSet<UniqueTag>` (UniqueTag = (PeerId, u64)) and the name LWW register's `HashMap<PeerId, u64>` vector clock. On the legacy-SOURCE signed stores (seed puts + DELETE tombstones + renamed stores) the encode failed 80× with `key must be a string`, so **the fallback never delivered at all**.

## The fix

**bincode** under the same `KV_STORE_DELTA_DM_PREFIX`. bincode has no map-key restriction and is already the envelope encoding for the sealed KV path.

**Wire compatibility**: the receiver's decode, `valid_kv_store_delta_typed_dm`, and the DM-history classifier each accept bincode **first** with the legacy r1 JSON shape as a fallback — an in-flight JSON payload from an un-upgraded sender still decodes (it serialized only when it carried no non-string keys, which is exactly when both encodings agree on the content). No new prefix, no new route.

## Rule 9

New test `kv_delta_direct_payload_serializes_legacy_source_shapes` builds the exact failing shape (a seed put with its UniqueTag, a DELETE tombstone tag set, a `name_update` LWW register with a PeerId-keyed vector clock):

pulls.title: fix(kv): v0.46 must load v0.45 snapshots (versioned snapshot magic) — release blocker
pulls.body:
## Release blocker

v0.46 could not load **any** KV store snapshot written by v0.45.0. The file layout is `X0XKVS1 || bincode(KvStore) || u64 seq_counter`. `KvStore.last_history_endorser` (97813fa, 8bd7c64) was added after the v0.45.0 tag and sits before `seq_counter`, so it consumed the head of the counter. Every 0.45 snapshot then failed with `UnexpectedEof` (`de_tolerant` swallows the field error, but the bytes are gone). Each store was skipped at startup, and opening it through the API failed with "refusing to start with amnesia". Background: `.planning/mixed-version-matrix-0.46.md` §C1.

## Fix

- **v1 read (`X0XKVS1`).** The body is decoded through `KvStoreV1SnapshotShape`, a frozen copy of the exact v0.45.0 `KvStore` serde shape (same field order and attributes, from `git show v0.45.0:src/kv/store.rs`). It is converted with `KvStore::from_v1_snapshot_shape`, which uses an exhaustive struct literal, and new fields take their defaults. Trailing bytes are rejected. One exact-length fallback accepts the v1 magic in front of the current shape, which only unreleased candidate builds wrote. At most one of the two layouts can consume a given body exactly, so the choice is unambiguous.
- **v2 write (`X0XKVS2`).** The body is `{ seq_counter, store }`. The counter comes first so the store runs to the true end of the stream, where trailing `de_tolerant` fields can default. Trailing bytes are rejected.
- **Unknown magic** still fails closed (the amnesia guard is kept).
- A v1 file

Closes #1040
Refs #843, #824

## Problem
A restarted owner device has an empty discovery cache. Until one of its enrolled owner machine's identity announcements arrived (more than 120 s on loaded hosts in R20), two things happened:
- It denied that machine's transport-authenticated `SyncV1` stream as `deny_not_verified`.
- It could not dial that machine (`machine not in discovery cache`).

  - The loop reads the prefix, re-verifies the enrollment, and admits `SyncV1` only. The stream goes to the **registered** SyncV1 acceptor only (`StreamAccept::registered_sender`), never to the default channel.

pulls.title: fix(groups): seat events carry owner-certified roster certificates (#1023)
pulls.body:
Closes #1023

## Root cause

#970 attached the roster-certificate sidecar **only to the JoinResult**. The authority builds it in `join_result_payload_with_roster_certificates` and serves it only in answer to the joiner's `FetchRequest`. The joiner, though, is normally seated first by the **direct or gossip copy of the authority's `MemberAdded`**. That copy carried only the joiner's own `certificate_b64`. Once seated, `poll_join_result_until_membership_confirmed` breaks out (`confirmed` / finalized), so the JoinResult, and its sidecar with it, is never fetched.

The joiner's stub comes from the invite's `base_roster`, which is `roster_projection`: digests only. The creator's seat therefore stays digest-only for good. After promotion, every seal hits `OwnerCertMemberPending [creator]`, and while the creator is offline the #946 fetch has nobody to answer it.

Evidence in the R19k `singapore.log`:
- Singapore's own seat arrived as `x0x_control_blob_witness … kind=member_added byte_len=55000`, 1.6 s after its MemberJoined.
- Singapore never logged a `kind=join_result` blob or an `R19: roster certificate sidecar hydrated` line.
- The fixture report's "oversized join_result reassembled…" check has `receipt_count 0`.

## Fix (gate unchanged)

- `MemberAdded` gains `roster_certificates_b64`, declared with `serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")`.
- **Serve:** all three authoritative seat-event builders call `seat_cert_fetch::attach_roster_certificates_to_member_added`,

pulls.title: docs(adr): propose ADR 0082 - notes accept records under their roster epoch
pulls.body:
Needs David's acceptance.

Proposes ADR 0082 (serves R9). It amends only ADR 0081's "current writer" rule, using the epoch-bound rule David chose on 2026-09-27. ADR 0081 itself is not edited.

- **Epoch:** each record signs the `(state_revision, state_hash)` of the ADR-0016 state-commit chain it was written under (`NoteUpdateRecordV2`).
- **Acceptance:** a replica accepts the record if the author was `Active` in the retained roster at that exact epoch (`GroupInfo.commit_log`, #111). Future, unknown or forked epochs are held until known, and provable non-writers are refused.
- **Backdating (for David):** the ADR bounds it rather than preventing it (§4). Causal epoch monotonicity refuses any record that depends on ops from a later epoch. A removed member also needs a current writer to relay its records. Within those limits, a removed member can still insert text positioned against pre-removal content.
- **Follow-ups:** store-carried roster evidence for late joiners, retaining the policy per commit, and persisted (sticky) verdicts.

The implementation is on `feat/965-notes-store` (no PR; main is scope-locked for R19).

pulls.body:
## What

Proposed **ADR 0080: Grant Revocation Is Also Pushed Directly to the Grantee; Gossip Remains the Backstop** (#1003, from the #994 Root decision; serves **R5**), plus its README index entry. **Docs only — no code, no behaviour change.** Acceptance is <person> only.

## Why a NEW ADR, not an amendment of ADR-0077

1. ADR-0077 is **Accepted**, and Accepted ADRs are immutable (0077's own closing rule) — the repo's amendment pattern is a new ADR whose header RECORDS the relationship; this one carries `Extends: ADR-0077 … does not edit it`.
2. The decision class is exactly what 0077 deferred to its own ADR: a new typed-DM wire carrier with old-peer compatibility obligations (0077's core win was "no wire change").
3. Propagation ≠ delivery — separate lifecycles.

Numbering checked live: 0076 reserved by parked #967, 0077 Accepted on main, 0078 Proposed on `omp/945-adr-0074`, 0079 Accepted on its branch → **0080** next free.

## The decision in one paragraph

On `DELETE /grants/:id`, AFTER ADR-0077's durable ordering completes, the owner best-effort pushes the signed `x0x.revocation.v3` record **bytes** over a new plain typed-DM prefix (`x0x-revocation-push-v1`) to the grantee's known agents, the shared agents, and every `deliver_to` daemon. Old receivers have no route for the prefix — the payload falls through to the generic-DM path and is ignored safely; the route is NOT durable-registered, so the sender never depends on an ACK. pulls.title: docs(adr): propose ADR 0079 — grant-carried owner_name and machine names (ADR-0074 §1 defaults)
pulls.body:
Proposed ADR-0079 (docs only). It makes the ADR-0074 §1 name defaults computable, and serves **R4** and **R5**. Following David's decision of 2026-09-27, the design is **grant-only**: both `owner_name` and machine names travel inside the grant.

## Decisions
- **Why a versioned carrier:** `ShareGrant` is strict positional bincode (`reject_trailing_bytes` plus a canonical re-encode check), and its signature covers a fixed layout. Appending an optional field would break every old verifier, so the names need a versioned carrier.
- **Carrier:** a new `x0x-sharegrant-v2\0` typed DM. It carries:
  - the **unchanged v1 grant**;
  - a names section with `owner_name` (from `human_name`: 1–128 bytes of UTF-8, no control characters) and `{machine_id, machine_name}` for each machine hosting the granted agents (at most 64);
  - an owner **user**-key signature over `SHA-256(grant.signed_bytes()) ‖ names`.
- **Storage:** the stored grant is byte-identical to a v1 delivery, so a v1 and a v2 copy of the same grant are an idempotent `Duplicate`.
- **Who gets v2:** only grantees that advertise a signed `share_grant_names` capability extension (modelled on #448). Everyone else gets v1. This is needed because an old peer drops an unknown prefix into its generic DM inbox and ACKs it.
- **Wire cost:** two new wire elements, the v2 prefix and the capability extension. The ADR-0072 freeze justification is in the ADR.
- **Rejected option:** an `X0U3` network-wide `owner_name` announcement. David rejec

pulls.title: fix(1004): ShareGrant outbox P3s — prune expired entries on disk; nudge includes due entries
pulls.body:
Closes #1004

Two P3 follow-ups from the #983/#994 audit, both in `src/share_grant/outbox.rs`.

1. **Expired entries are now removed from the file on load.** `load()` used to drop entries that expired while the daemon was down from memory only. They stayed in `share-grant-outbox.bin` until some later write. `validate_loaded` now also returns the expired count. When it is non-zero, `load` rewrites the file under `write_lock`.
   - Only a fully validated file reaches this path. Unreadable, malformed, over-bound, forged or foreign files still load fail-closed (`load_error`) and are never rewritten.
   - If the rewrite fails, `persist()` leaves the outbox dirty, and the worker's existing pass-0 dirty rewrite retries it.
2. **The reconnect nudge now includes already-due entries.** `nudge()` used to count only entries whose schedule it moved earlier. For a delivery that was already due, it returned `false` and did not wake the worker, so the retry waited for the next poll. Every queued delivery to the given recipients now counts: its schedule becomes `min(schedule, now)` (an overdue entry keeps its earlier slot) and the worker is woken.

Contract, lock order and send gate are unchanged. The load rewrite takes only `write_lock` (step 4 of the lock order), on a fresh outbox that nothing else can reach yet. `nudge` touches only the entry map. Revocation checks are untouched: `step` still drops revoked entries and re-checks each one before sending.

pulls.title: fix(983): a revoke during POST's initial DM can never be undone
pulls.body:
Fixes the #983 post-merge P1 (Greptile, confirmed by Codex in codex-983-post-merge-greptile.md), its P2, and Codex r1 of this PR (codex-994-r1-review.md).

## The races

**Late enqueue** (#983 post-merge P1):
1. POST stored the grant and took its enqueue timestamp, then awaited the initial DM.
2. A DELETE completed meanwhile. It removed nothing, because nothing was queued yet.
3. The DM failed, and POST queued the revoked grant with no revocation check and no gate.
4. The worker checked revocation on one snapshot but selected due entries from a second, so it sent the grant after DELETE succeeded.
5. The receiver stored it without a revocation check.

**Successful initial DM** (r1 P1): the initial DM ran outside the gate. A DELETE could complete while the DM was in flight, and a receiver that had no gossip yet would then store and ACK the grant after DELETE returned.

## The contract (Codex r2 / Root's ruling)
Over a network nobody can promise that nothing lands after `DELETE` returns: a send cut off by the 30 s deadline may already be on the wire. The contract is exactly this:
1. **Owner side:** after `DELETE /grants/:id` returns, this install makes **no new send and no new enqueue** of the grant.
2. **In flight:** a DM already on the wire is handled by the receiver. The revocation reaches it on the `x0x.revocation.v3` gossip carrier; **there is no direct push** (see below). A receiver that already knows the revocation refuses the grant. A receiver that stored the grant first

pulls.title: fix(tasks): gate encrypted task-list publication on the current group epoch (#975)
pulls.body:
**Stacked on #973 (merge); merges right after #973.** Branched from `codex/969-stale-seal-epoch` at `adde676` and will pick up #973's deadlock fix by merge, never rebase. The diff against the base therefore includes #973's commit until #973 lands.

## Root cause
Encrypted group task lists (#914/#895) went from seal straight to publish. `publish_delta` and the `/state-sync` full-state serve both called `seal_for_wire`, which snapshots the group key through `GroupTaskDeltaProtector::seal` (GSS `secret_epoch` or the live TreeKEM ratchet), and then called `pubsub.publish` with nothing in between. A member removal that commits between the two (GSS rotation, or a TreeKEM removal commit) let a record sealed under the **pre-removal** epoch go out after the removal. The removed member still holds that epoch's key and can read it. This is the #969 class, on the task-list path.

## Fix
- `TaskDeltaProtector::confirm_publication(body)` (in `src/crdt/sealed.rs`) runs after the seal and immediately before publication. It returns `Current(permit)` or `Stale`. The permit holds the group's epoch fixed until it is dropped.
- `seal_and_publish` (in `src/crdt/sync.rs`) replaces `seal_for_wire` in both `publish_delta` and the state-sync responder. The loop is: seal, confirm, then publish while holding the permit. If the result is `Stale`, the stale record is discarded and the payload is re-sealed, up to 3 attempts, after which the publish is refused. Never plaintext. Confirm plus publish is bound

pulls.title: fix(kv): serialize GSS encrypted publication with roster commits (#969)
pulls.body:
An encrypted group KV publisher could refresh at epoch E, pause while a removal durably commits E+1, then seal or enqueue a frame under E. Retirement does not drain every responder/requester publication. This change serializes authoritative roster commits with every GSS encrypted KV publication from refresh through the initial pubsub publish call, including already-sealed retained, control, full-state, and delta frames.

The daemon shares one publication gate across group-store syncs and roster persistence. Writers hold it through live-map installation, durable save, or rollback; publishers hold a read permit through seal and initial publish. A single 30-second absolute deadline covers each guarded async refresh, seal, and publish section so a stalled pubsub call cannot hold a roster writer indefinitely. Encrypted syncs with authoritative refresh fail closed if the gate was not installed before startup.

The encrypted transport proof now records phase, sender, topic, and frame epoch on failure. It authenticates delayed old-epoch frames with the saved pre-removal secret and rejects any that carry the unique post-removal or restart key; required current-epoch frames must authenticate and have the expected mutation kind and key. This distinguishes a legitimate gossip retry of precommit bytes from a new stale-epoch publication.

## Root cause (R18 Home fixture, analysis `802-r18-home-ANALYSIS.md`)

Owner-certified roster seats hold only certificate **digests**. Certificate bytes travel only on each device's own identity announce (every 600 s), and only the cert's owner serves the announce blob (#656).

In R18, the owner device (nyc) announced once at 10:09:21, before any other daemon had started, and shut down at 10:15:03, before its next heartbeat. No surviving node ever held nyc's certificate. When the admin (singapore) sealed the next joiner, it refused forever with `members pending certificate resolution: [nyc]`.

The #946 group-scoped fetch was correctly designed but had no supplier: its responder consulted only the announce-blob cache (`seat_cert_fetch.rs:299`).

## Design

1. **The JoinResult carries certificates (root fix).**
   - `JoinResultMessage::Result` gains `roster_certificates_b64`. The local seat goes first, then entries are sorted by agent hex; the sidecar is capped at 32 entries.
   - The sidecar is trimmed to fit the transport the **bare** result would use: the DM limit when the result is inline, the control-blob limit (#878) when it is already oversized. pulls.title: fix(forward): propagate FIN on EOF and finish denial replies (#961)
pulls.body:
## Root cause

`bridge()` in `src/forward.rs` ran `tokio::io::copy` in both directions and never shut down either writer. `tokio::io::copy` never calls `poll_shutdown`, so ant-quic's `SendStream::poll_shutdown`, which is `finish()`, was never reached. ant-quic 0.27.53 `SendStream::drop` resets any unfinished stream with `0xA17C0244` (`send_stream.rs:340-354`). As a result:
1. A TCP half-close never became a QUIC FIN, so `shutdown(Write)` + `read_to_end` clients hung.
2. Every exit dropped `send` unfinished. The reset threw away the unread tail.
3. The three denial replies (`write_all(denied)` then `return`) were reset as well, so the opener got a reset error instead of the diagnostic frame.

## Fix (surgical, no unwrap/expect/panic)

- **`bridge()`:** each direction is `copy`, then on `Ok` (clean EOF) `shutdown()` of the destination writer. For the QUIC side that means `finish()`, which queues a FIN. For the TCP side it means `shutdown(Write)`, a half-close. The two directions still run concurrently under `join!`, so one side's EOF propagates while the other keeps flowing. On a copy **error** the writer is left unfinished and Drop resets it, as before, so truncation still surfaces as an error and never as a well-formed short stream. On the clean path both writers are finished before `bridge` returns, so no unfinished send stream is ever dropped.
- **Denials:** a new `send_denial()` helper writes the denial frame and then calls `finish()`. It is used at all three sites (v2 gat

## Summary

`scripts/install.sh` (served at `https://x0x.md`) now verifies the release tarball before it installs anything.

**Decision (<person>, 2026-09-26):** always verify SHA-256. Verify the GPG signature whenever `gpg` is present. If `gpg` is absent, print a LOUD warning and continue.

What changed in `scripts/install.sh` (POSIX sh):
- **SHA-256 (always):** downloads `<tarball>.sha256` and compares it with `sha256sum` or `shasum -a 256`, whichever exists. A malformed or mismatched checksum fails closed. If neither tool exists, the script errors out.

  2. imports the key and verifies the signature;
  3. accepts only a `[GNUPG:] VALIDSIG` whose signing-key or primary-key fingerprint equals the pin.

- **Temporary keyring:** every `gpg` call uses `--homedir "$TMP/gnupg"` (mode 700) inside the installer's `mktemp -d` dir. The existing `EXIT` trap already removes `$TMP`, and `gpgconf --kill all` stops any agent started for it. The user's own `~/.gnupg` is never read or written.

pulls.title: fix(dm): unattested gossip DM claims never rebind routing (#927)
pulls.body:
## Root cause

`InboxPipeline::handle_incoming` (`src/dm_inbox.rs`) resolves the sender's machine in one of three ways: a fresh origin-machine attestation, an `AuthenticatedMachineBindings` entry, or, when neither exists, the sender-claimed `envelope.sender_machine_id`. The agent signature does not prove that the sender owns the machine. On the v2 (durable) path, `handle_payload` then called `self.dm.mark_connected(sender, envelope.sender_machine_id)` without any condition. `connect_to_agent` (lib.rs) copies that `DirectMessaging` entry into the discovery cache. As a result, an agent holding only its own key could rebind its routing entry to any machine it named. Found by omp's security review of #924 (finding 4).

## Fix

This mirrors #898 (`75a5d9b`, in #924), which applied the same gate to the raw-Direct path.

- The machine resolution now returns `(sender_machine_id, origin_authenticated)`. The flag is `true` for an attestation or an authenticated binding and `false` for a bare claim.
- The new `mark_gossip_dm_sender_connected(dm, agent, machine, origin_authenticated)` calls `mark_connected` only when the flag is `true`. An unattested claim logs at debug level and leaves routing unchanged.
- The message is still delivered. It uses the existing `verified` annotation (`DirectMessage.verified` and `DmTypedPayload.verified`), which is set to `origin_authenticated` on the v1 generic, v1 typed, v2 generic and v2 durable-typed deliveries. The pubsub-level signature gate is uncha

## What

Fixes the #878 r3 flake seen on #910: `completed_pull_sends_its_release_over_the_wire` asserted the intermediate `staged_len() == 1` immediately after the Reference handler returned, racing the self-looped pipeline (Reference → fetch → chunks → digest-verify → Release → release_staged) which can free the slot BEFORE the assert runs — observed as 'the reference is staged', left 0 right 1, on a PR touching nothing in named_groups.

## Fix (test-only + one cfg(test) accessor)

- Assert only the TERMINAL state: `release_staged` is the only remover of a staged entry inside the window (TTL prune is lazy, `PENDING_JOIN_RESULT_TTL` is minutes away), so staged_len reaching 0 IS the Release round trip. No sleep-and-hope: the bounded 30s poll was already there.
- New `cfg(test) released_notice_count()` counter (incremented only in `release_staged`'s successful-remove arm) pins the mechanism: exactly ONE Release freed the slot — not a TTL prune or any other remover.

## Verification (run locally at 6ff7345)

- 41 consecutive green runs (1 + 40 stress, 4 threads), 0 failures.
- Fail-before A (Release notice never sent): fails via the 30s deadline assert.
- Fail-before B (remove without counting): fails via the counter assert in 0.12s — the counter is load-bearing, not decoration.

## Summary

Fixes #849 using the issue's option 2: SelfKeyed quota evictions are now reported to the writer.

### ADR-0047 compliance
Admission is **unchanged**. Decision item 4 (deterministic lowest-N admission, with identical local and remote predicates) still applies:

- The `/state-sync` responder republished the **whole list** as `encode_delta(peer, &full)` on the main topic (formerly L1522-1526).
- The topic is the list id, so anyone who knows the group id can derive it and subscribe. Titles, descriptions and claim/complete state were all readable, and a non-member could send a `StateRequest` to get the full list.
- `EncryptedTaskListDelta` (`src/crdt/encrypted.rs`) had no callers. It also uses the legacy `crate::mls::MlsGroup` cipher, not the key a named group actually holds (GSS secret or TreeKEM ratchet), so it could not be wired as it stands.

pulls.title: fix(dm): preserve predecessor retries and ordinary prefix collisions (#903)
pulls.body:
A full predecessor typed channel could drop a payload after the sender received success, clearing the authority's relay outbox target. A verified ordinary DM whose bytes began with a registered typed prefix could instead be consumed by a handler that rejected it, leaving no generic delivery or durable history. This patch makes upgraded predecessor senders require gossip admission: a full or closed typed route leaves the v1 request unacknowledged and unclaimed in dedupe, so the authority can retry. All five typed routes validate the complete payload before diverting it; rejected prefix collisions return to generic delivery and history. Exact structural classification keeps malformed exec, group-public, and KV prefix collisions in outbound history.

The current feature head is `fcd88f70f1186e915ffc949076d16c112ccd4bca` (tree `3d33959b89d05d4e83038bf75fc834d9931c280d`) on acceptance candidate `b7158890bb2ed2067bfd73ea1dfdf53d98984661`. The hosted synthetic merge has that same tree. It includes merged #923 so the roster test precondition is deterministic. The initial nine focused #903 tests cover full-channel no-ACK/no-dedupe followed by same-envelope retry, all five colliding-prefix generic deliveries with persisted SQLite history, and genuine typed payload controls; three defect controls failed on pre-fix source. The CI history tests now use valid group-public, KV, and exec frames to assert ephemeral exclusion and malformed prefix collisions to assert durable generic delivery.

pulls.title: Protect per-topic preferred eager peers during mesh maintenance
pulls.body:
Full pubsub nodes can keep a connected group member lazy behind a saturated nonmember eager mesh, delaying encrypted group-store writes until IHAVE/IWANT repair. This PR adds an atomic, bounded per-topic preferred eager set. It keeps up to eight eligible group members eager while preserving the full connected eager/lazy membership and IWANT repair paths.

The topic's effective eager ceiling rises according to the retained preferred set and returns to the configured ceiling when the set is cleared. Cooling and score vetoes remain authoritative. Healthy preferred peers survive degree shedding, later maintenance, and duplicate-message demotion. Ordinary topics retain their configured behavior, and the existing single-peer API remains available.

pulls.body:
Fixes #811 (asks 1 + 2; ask 3 — the debug rerun — is e2e/Root's).

## Root cause (two interacting)
1. The retained-image pool caps in-flight images at **4 / 120 s TTL, no eviction across sender or epoch**. Four stuck bindings hard-reject every NEW image for the whole TTL — helsinki logged the refusal four times over ~100 s, unattributable (no store id in the line).
2. The state-request schedule fires at cumulative **1/6/21/51/81/141 s**; once early rounds burned against the wedged pool, the next retry (141 s) fell past the 120 s harness deadline.

## Fix (r2 form)
1. **Attribution** — the cap refusal reads `too many retained images are awaiting pages for store <hex8>`; displacement warns with both store ids, the idle seconds, and the victim's bytes.
2. **Grace-then-displace, idle-based** — after `INFLIGHT_DISPLACE_AFTER` (**30 s in every build**; tests back-date, never sleep), a NEW image displaces the **MAX-IDLE** pending image (`last_progress`, refreshed on every accepted page/manifest — a large image still receiving pages is protected). The displacement runs **after** the byte gates, so a victim is only evicted when the incoming page is otherwise certain to be admitted. Accounting is exact and test-asserted.
3. **Custody, explicit (Rule 7)** — displacement crosses endorser/epoch boundaries **within one store** for the 30 s grace (the R10 wedge was divergent bindings in ONE store); other stores keep independent custody. DoS note: authenticated non-reader writers only; one w

pulls.title: fix(sync): #863 — publish the local Home pointer before every sync session
pulls.body:
Fixes #863 (Home wait-for-sync residual from #826/#824, per ADR-0069).

## Root cause
The rank-0 wait treats a successful-but-empty session as "no Home exists". That rule was only sound if a peer's version vector could never understate a held Home — but **provisioning does not publish the pointer** (only a reconcile/sync pass does). A peer holding a freshly created, not-yet-published Home answered the exchange with an **empty HomePointer kind**, and the rank-0 peer created a duplicate.

## Fix (the issue's "publish before the session reports success" option)
`OwnerSyncService::session_with_home_publication` — the ONE composition both session directions run (`handle_inbound`, `dial_and_sync`): **definitively read** the local Home pointer (`home_pointer_definitive`: an AWAITED `named_groups` read — lock contention waits, it is never mistaken for "no Home"; an unreadable/no-owner view fails the session CLOSED, never an empty vector, never `set_session_status(true)`), mint it, then `run_sync_session`. An empty HomePointer vector is henceforth genuine proof of no local Home; the #824 release rule is sound as documented. **No wire change.**

## Mixed-version gap (deliberately documented, not gated)
The guarantee is ONE-SIDED: a peer on a **pre-#863 build** holding an unpublished Home still answers the exchange with an empty HomePointer kind — SyncV1 carries no capability signal to detect that. #863 therefore **persists in a mixed-version owner fleet until both ends run this build**

pulls.body:
Fixes #876 (the #850 regression; R15 Home 95/96).

## Root cause
Cert-carrying join events are ~51.5 KB — over the 49,152-byte DM limit — so they travel as staged control blobs. `PER_PEER_ENTRY_CAP = 4` with **TTL-only release** filled after two joins (2 blobs per recipient per join); the next MemberAdded + join event were refused (`control blob staging budget exhausted`) and **dropped**. The member's later role update was then **silently** rejected (member unknown, no log).

## Fix (all 5 issue items)
1. **Release on completed fetch** — new `control_blob_release` message: after a pull completes and the digest verifies, the recipient best-effort notifies the source, which removes the staged entry (only the blob's own recipient may release; exact reference keyed by digest+length). The per-peer cap now bounds **in-flight** blobs. Mixed fleet: an older source ignores the unknown type (listener `from_slice` fails → `continue`) and keeps TTL semantics; older recipients never send it. No existing wire variant changed.
2. **Never drop on staging refusal** — `send_reference` retries budget-exhausted staging 6× / 2 s before erroring (caller still warns on final failure). Other refusals return immediately.
3. **WARN + park late role updates** — `state.parked_role_updates` (bounded 32/group, drop-oldest): a `MemberRoleUpdated` for an unseated member warns, parks, and replays through the ordinary apply after any accepted `MemberAdded` (re-parking if still unseated; suppressed in replay c

pulls.body:
Closes #870 after release-candidate integration and acceptance.

A session bearer with no active local seat could read delegation metadata for a public group and see its `fork_quarantine` marker. The session could also receive that marker in history responses and WebSocket backfill or mention frames. pulls.title: fix: retry cold encrypted-store sync and classify rejection
pulls.body:
On R12, a cold encrypted-store joiner received the owner page after 54.6 seconds and the member page after 119 seconds; on R14 the owner page was still absent at the 120-second deadline. More importantly, a store opened before its joiner became an authorized reader could stop its cold requester forever when sealing a StateRequest returned `None`.

The requester now stays alive through denied seal slots, wakes on GSS membership/secret changes, and sends promptly once reader authorization arrives. Denied slots do not count toward the four **published** requests required before trusting served convergence evidence, so an early partial holder cannot end discovery before a complete holder responds. Later retries are at least the responder's 15-second cooldown even after jitter, with a persistent slow tail. Adds **ADR 0069 (Proposed)**, the ADR amendment that PR #826 flagged as a follow-up (item 3 on #826; Greptile P2).

## What it records
- **Decision.** An owned, owner-certified device that has owner sync available and knows no canonical `("home")` pointer defers creating a fresh Home at startup. It creates one only after the wait, and never if a pointer arrives first.
- **Creator rank.** `home_creator_rank` is the number of enrolled owner machines with a smaller machine id. A successful session that brings no pointer releases only the rank-0 device. Every other device falls back after `(rank + 1) × 90 s`.
- **Linearisation.** `quiesce_sessions` (bounded by `SESSION_TIMEOUT` + 30 s) and a read hold on `canonical_home_gate` run from the final pointer check through the create and stamp.
- **API.** `GET /home` returns 200 `provisioning_pending` while the wait is active. `POST ~` returns 409 `ambiguous_home` when the device is seated in several Homes and the pointer does not name the one it resolved.
- **Rationale and alternatives.** The rationale is the #824 duplicate Home. Two alternatives were rejected: enrollment hands over the Home (there is no product enrollment path yet), and accepting duplicates (every late device would add permanent residue).

pulls.title: fix(groups): TreeKEM catch-up adopts nothing unless the chain reaches the pending owner-attested head (#846)
pulls.body:
Fixes #846 (found in the #839 security review).

## Problem
`handle_treekem_catchup_response` verified only that the responder is an ACTIVE MEMBER of the joiner's current (stub) view, then applied the intervening commits through the ordinary path WITHOUT consulting the pending owner v2 attestation. A forking-but-active responder could get its own divergent intermediates adopted before the queued terminal failed to link.

## Fix (check-first, per the issue's preferred option)
While an owner-anchored stale-base gap is pending — detected as **a queued TreeKEM terminal + the durable #816/#839 anchored-gap audit record** on the lineage (the transient attestation entry is consumed at classification; the record's `head_state_hash` IS the attested head) — the handler simulates the served commit chain from the CURRENT state hash with **no state mutation** (`catchup_chain_reaches_attested_head`, extracted as a pure helper):
- every commit must link (`prev_state_hash` chain), AND
- the chain must reach the attested head hash.

A chain that breaks linking, or a prefix that never reaches the head, **adopts NOTHING and pages no further** — the pending record and queued terminal stay intact for an honest responder or the joiner's own retry volley. Groups without a pending anchored gap keep the previous behavior unchanged. The walk covers every event kind carrying a state commit (the generic `named_group_metadata_event_commit`), not just membership frontiers.

pulls.title: Keep Welcome retries and owner streams live through stalls (#841)
pulls.body:
An authorized joiner may retry a Welcome FetchRequest when its receipt or stream stalls. The owner previously ignored a second request while its first chunk stream was active, and the joiner dropped its receive waiter between attempts. Chunks arriving during the retry delay could therefore be lost, while retries stretched beyond the join poll window.

Keep one receive entry and waiter through a 115-second fetch window. Send retries at cumulative 0/5/25/85 seconds, skipping a resend when chunks have advanced. On a repeated authorized, unexpired request, stop the prior owner stream and its ACK slot before starting the replacement. Stream admission and shutdown drainage share a closed registry under one mutex, so a late request cannot start after shutdown. Expiry pruning is synchronized with staging to avoid aborting another joiner's fresh stream. Log a chunk with no pending receive state at WARN, and classify a real `DmError::Timeout` as an unconfirmed FetchRequest receipt.

pulls.body:
Fixes #842 (the R13 Home e2e blocker).

## Problem
The owner resolved joiner certificates ONLY from its discovery cache and announce-blob cache. When the joiner's certificate announce didn't propagate, nothing re-sent it until the 600 s identity heartbeat — the owner refused the join with `no agent certificate resolved` ~100 times across the whole 120 s window (R12 evidence: sfo announced 14:31:25, joined 14:36:59, nyc refused until 14:38:59; nyc's blob cache had every OTHER device's cert but not sfo's).

An absent certificate keeps the evidence path unchanged (#447 retained-pending machinery untouched).

Registered typed payloads, including ADR-0028 predecessor relay, were never dispatched to their handlers. Registered exec requests now also reach their existing typed handler over raw QUIC, with the same verified-binding and trust eligibility before that handler applies its own authorization.

Before the inbox service starts there is no registered typed-route list, so raw messages retain their existing generic behavior in that startup window. This patch covers the active-inbox path selected by a cold sender capability lookup; it does not make pre-start delivery durable.

pulls.title: Require terminal-bound owner attestation for gap adoption (#820)
pulls.body:
## Problem and behavior

For non-TreeKEM OwnerCertified groups, a joining member could adopt an across-gap state using the owner's v1 signature over the *parent* commit. An active admin could sign a different terminal on that parent and replay the genuine v1 signature; the joiner adopted the sibling.

Across-gap adoption now requires the owner's v2 signature over the exact terminal state hash, committer, and epoch. A chain-valid v1-only result remains pending without fork quarantine, with durable non-gating audit evidence and a separate first-seen record/count for each refusal reason. A present malformed or mismatched v2 signature continues through the fork classifier and quarantines the sibling. An inviter who can strip the v2 binding can downgrade a detectable fork to a pending result, but cannot make the joiner adopt that terminal. For TreeKEM, a v1-only result is deliberately not queued for replay/catch-up: the old signature does not bind the terminal, so queuing it would retain an attacker-supplied event. In a mixed-version fleet, a joiner waits for a v2-capable owner or a fresh invite to cross that gap.

## Regression evidence

pulls.title: fix(groups): a lost Welcome Offer ACK no longer aborts the TreeKEM Welcome stream (#825)
pulls.body:
Fixes #825.

## Protocol analysis
- The joiner's `fetch_treekem_welcome` registers `PendingWelcomeReceive` (source, byte_len, total_chunks) from the signed `WelcomeRef` **before** it sends `FetchRequest`.
- `handle_welcome_blob_chunk` needs only that entry. It checks the source, bounds `sequence < total_chunks` and dedupes by sequence. `Complete` then verifies the length, the chunk count and blake3 == welcome_id.
- The `Offer` is advisory. Its only effect on the joiner is a consistency check that can abort on a mismatch.
- `stream_welcome_blob` still returned on an Offer **receipt** timeout, before sending any chunk. The Offer travels gossip-inbox-preferred, and the ACK window was about 24 s under load, while the joiner may already have received the Offer. The owner had committed MemberAdded, so the joiner stuck at `pending_authority_commit` (R11, 2 of 2 runs).

## Change (option a)
- An Offer send error is now logged and the stream continues.
- Every other failure path is unchanged and bounded: chunk send errors, the 60 s window and final-ACK timeouts, and the `stream_duplicate_ignored` dedupe. The ACK slot is still released at the end, so a later FetchRequest can restart the stream. An unreachable joiner costs at most one more failed chunk send.
- Why not (b): re-arming on retry was already possible after an abort. In R11 every retry's Offer timed out the same way, so a retry-based fix alone would not converge.
- The stream body moves to `stream_welcome_blob_via(.., send)`.

pulls.title: fix(home): never mint a seat invite into a non-canonical duplicate Home (#824)
pulls.body:
Fixes the safety half of #824. The root cause is **not** fixed here, because it needs a design decision (see below).

## Mechanism
- A device that is given a copy of the owner key restarts with `user.key` and a certificate, but its Tier-1 owner-sync store is empty.
- `provision_home` runs at startup (`src/server/mod.rs`) before any sync round. It checks for a canonical pointer at step 3 (`effective_canonical_home`), finds none, and step 4 provisions a new Home. This is the optimistic provisioning that #449/ADR-0060 chose on purpose.
- The per-machine marker (#435) did not prevent this, for two reasons. First, it lives in each device's own data dir and only ever names *this* machine's Home, so a fresh device has no marker. Second, it is advisory and never suppresses provisioning. Only the pointer does, and the pointer arrives after startup.
- The device later joins the owner's Home and is now seated in two Home-shaped groups. With no pointer, `resolve_home` falls back to the smallest stable id, which can be the duplicate. `seat_home` then minted into that duplicate and returned 200.

## Change
`seat_home`: if `home_duplicates` is non-empty and the effective canonical pointer is unknown or does not name the resolved group, it returns **409 `reason: "ambiguous_home"`** (the existing `seat_conflict` shape, nullable `canonical_group_id`) and mints nothing. A pointer that names one of the held Homes still seats into exactly that Home. `docs/api-reference.md` is updated. No ADR chan

pulls.title: test(key-cache): skip replayed pre-restart frame in restart-recovery proof (#822)
pulls.body:
Fixes the intermittent #822 failure (about 4 in 25 runs).

**Mechanism:**
- Bob restarts, which wipes his in-memory seen set.
- On resubscribe, x0x's subscribe-time anti-entropy (`src/gossip/pubsub.rs:1440-1446`, #397) sends Alice an empty digest, **if** Bob already has Alice as a topic peer. That condition is why it's intermittent.
- Alice legitimately re-serves `initial-0` from her 60 s message cache (sg 0.5.85 `lib.rs:79`, ~10289-10318).
- The test's receive loop took the first frame on the topic, so it saw the replayed `initial-0` and failed at :185.

**Change:** test only. A frame whose payload isn't the one just published is logged and skipped. The 20 s delivery timeout and the origin assertion are unchanged, so a missing delivery still fails.

**Product note (not changed here):** delivery across a restart is at-least-once. The replayed message is the genuine signed original, not corrupted or forged. The WS `message` frame has no `msg_id` for app-level dedupe. This is documented on #822 as a follow-up.

pulls.body:
## Problem
R10 (2026-09-24, also a2/a3): the second Home joiner on a stale-base invite ends up `membership_state=active` but fork-quarantined (`classification: signer_only`, terminal = unsigned rev-2 stub header, conflicting = owner-signed rev 4). Because of that, every store open returns 409 "group is unavailable".

## Mechanism
1. The InviteV4 stub sets both of its clocks from `base_state_revision` (`named_groups.rs` ~15993). The MemberAdded `revision` comes from the authority's **roster** clock, which is behind its state clock. `treekem_state_frontier_gap_reason` (~6496) therefore sees no gap. The JoinResult's rev-4 MemberAdded is applied directly instead of being queued.
2. The apply fails with `PrevHashMismatch`. `try_adopt_member_added_across_gap` never adopts on TreeKEM (~4296).
3. The refused arm calls `classify_refused_joiner_fork_chain`. That walks the **owner's own** served chain (rev 3), which validates from the base. It finds no anchoring mandate and installs a `signer_only` quarantine. The owner head attestation carried by the JoinResult is never checked.
4. The unsigned rev-2 "terminal" is only the forensic `terminal_commit_header()` synthesized for a stub with no retained commit (`groups/mod.rs:873`). It is not what triggers the quarantine.
5. Later the joiner is seated gaplessly at rev 4. `owner_anchored_clear_permitted` requires a revision strictly greater than the evidence revision (4), so the marker stays.

pulls.title: fix(gossip): scope #807 lazy retention to Leaf; restore Full-node peer semantics
pulls.body:
Scopes the #807 lazy-retention change (#808) to **Leaf** nodes. Full nodes go back to their pre-#807 peer-set calls (as at 259ebb5 / 9b7ba64).

## Why
R10 testnet e2e (Full daemons): GSS nyc→sfo KV delivery took 110 s, against 0.7 s on R9, and a delete never reached sfo within 120 s. The #808 port changed Full behaviour in two ways:

pulls.body:
Fixes #807. Ports the pubsub half of #774 onto the #802 candidate (crates.io saorsa-gossip 0.5.85).

## Problem
On Leaf nodes, `ordered_leaf_peers` cut the connected peer set to `leaf_max_eager_degree` (2), sorted by PeerId bytes. Peers past the cut were neither eager nor lazy, so a DM-inbox or join publish could black-hole a directly connected recipient.

Seen live in the R9 synthetic Home e2e: an sfo→nyc join was held 134 s, and was released only when the peers sorting ahead of nyc shut down.

## Change (`src/gossip/pubsub.rs`)
- All four eager-set writers now pass the **full connected set** to sg `set_topic_peers_with_preferred_eager` (in sg 0.5.85, same API as #774's pin cde3c1b), plus the selected Full/bootstrap preference. sg keeps every connected peer eager or lazy and still caps eager fan-out at `leaf_max_eager_degree` (#504 budget intent kept).
- `initialize_topic_peers` replaces the topic's peer set rather than adding to it (from #774).
- Tests: #774's four membership/lazy-repair tests and its relaxed `slice1_*` assertions. `adr014_publish_with_signing_context_emits_outer_v2` seeded an unconnected peer and failed on #774's own CI; it now puts the peer on the recorded plane.

## Deliberately NOT included
A recipient-first eager slot. A connected recipient is now always at least lazy, so it gets an IHAVE within sg's 100 ms flush and one IWANT round trip, well inside join and DM deadlines. sg has only one preferred slot, and C5b already uses it.

pulls.title: feat(pubsub): reconcile full membership with preferred eager peer
pulls.body:
## Problem

A caller with three connected topic peers and an eager degree of two currently has to choose between passing the full membership set or preserving a preferred eager peer. Truncating the set to the preferred peer plus one neighbor removes the third connected peer from both eager and lazy pubsub membership, so IHAVE/IWANT repair cannot reach it. Replacing peers through remove/re-add also discards topic-local score, cooling, suppression, and IWANT state.

## Change

Add `set_topic_peers_with_preferred_eager`, an atomic topic-local reconciliation API that accepts the full connected membership and an optional preferred eager peer.

- Surviving peer state is retained.
- Newly connected peers enter as lazy.
- An eligible preferred peer can displace the lowest-scoring eager peer; the displaced peer remains lazy.
- Cooling, absent, or score-ineligible peers are not promoted.
- The configured eager ceiling and admission/budget behavior remain unchanged.
- Repeated identical calls are idempotent.
- Existing `set_topic_peers` behavior is preserved by delegating with no preference.

Five deterministic `RecordingTransport` tests cover full three-peer membership at degree two, repeated reconciliation, cooling preservation, preferred replacement after disconnect, and outstanding/deferred IWANT preservation.

This supplies the upstream API required by x0x #774 to retain every connected Leaf peer while keeping an actual Full/bootstrap peer eager when one exists.

pulls.body:
Older heads of the same pull request can keep the hour-scale Test Suite and Coverage Gate running after a newer head starts. On #774, both old-head jobs continued after new-head CI began because the workflow had no concurrency policy.

pulls.title: Keep test-runner event readers responsive during commands
pulls.body:
Slow test-runner commands currently execute inline on the SSE reader thread, so a blocked direct send can prevent that reader from consuming delivery receipts and later commands. This adds one bounded FIFO command worker: readers perform replay admission and deduplication promptly, then enqueue without blocking while commands remain serialized.

Queue-full and shutdown admissions fail explicitly and roll back their replay entries so retransmission can execute later. Shutdown serializes admission against its queue drain, accounts for commands that will never execute, and preserves existing in-flight deduplication and result pinning. Runtime behavior outside the runner lifecycle remains synchronous.

**Author model:** Claude Fable 5.1 (claude-fable-5-1)

When `KvStoreSync::cancel_sync_and_drain()` / `KvStoreHandle::retire_and_drain()` returns, **no background merge, ownership update or snapshot write for that store is in flight, and none can start.**

`adr0064_*` fault-injection tests in `fork_quarantine` failed non-deterministically under default `cargo test` parallelism (28/33 → 24/33 depending on run) because `SAVE_FAULT_INJECT` was a **process-global** `AtomicU8` static. | `SaveFaultGuard` (unit struct, Drop cleared global) | Now holds `Arc<AtomicU8>` clone of the instance cell; Drop clears THAT instance only |

pulls.body:
Closes the ADR-0066/0067 send-path §4 follow-up: coverage-map rows **1, 2, 4, 6** (outbound group public-message send, TreeKEM encrypt, GSS encrypt, GSS reseal), previously held visible as `PENDING_RECHECK == [1, 2, 4, 6]`.

## The rule

The entry gate already refuses when a marker exists at request start, so an operation is admitted **only** when the group carried no marker at that instant. The window it leaves is: a marker installed **after the entry gate and before the effect leaves the node**. It is not theoretical — between the gate and the effect these handlers await on the rider-token mutex, a revocation-record read, delegation verification, the TreeKEM per-group mutex and a pubsub listener spawn.

So: **capture the ADR-0067 lifecycle epoch token under the same read guard as the entry gate, and re-check its MARKER half immediately before the irreversible effect** — at the last point with no suspension between the check and the effect — using one short `state.named_groups` read lock. A marker present at the re-check that the capture did not carry (newly installed, or advanced to a different evidence identity) refuses with the slice-1 §5 body and the effect does not happen. One shared helper, `named_groups::reject_fork_quarantine_installed_before_effect`, is called from all four sites.

pulls.body:
Refs #732 — ADR-0066 slice 7 (§4, the lifecycle epoch token), plus the superseding **ADR-0067** the implementation turned out to need.

## The ADR contradiction, and the ruling

Slice 7 stalled on ADR-0066 contradicting itself. §4:

> The token is the tuple `(state_revision, quarantine_generation)`, where `quarantine_generation` is a process-local monotonic `u64` **on the group entry**, incremented on every marker install and every clear

R4:

> `(state_revision, quarantine_generation)` per §4, with no new persisted `lifecycle_epoch` field — no new serde surface, **no new #470 full-equality participant**, no new bootstrap-strip obligation

`GroupInfo` derives `PartialEq` (`groups/mod.rs:332`) and the comment above it makes that equality deliberately load-bearing:

> #470: FULL record equality — derived over EVERY field, including the `#[serde(skip)]`/local-only ones … The compare-and-restore rollback in `persist_named_groups_mutation_unlocked` uses this to decide whether a concurrent writer touched a key

So a field on the record — even `#[serde(skip)]`, which "no new *persisted* field" allows — is unavoidably a new #470 participant. A counter kept anywhere else contradicts §4. R4 is self-consistent only if the generation is not a `GroupInfo` field; §4 only if it is.

**A census made the choice for us.** Three production marker writers no process-local counter reaches:

| `named_groups.rs:24203` on-disk recovery install | writes

## Refs #611

## What the old oracle could not see

\`shape_diamond\` checks PLANE ADMISSION only. A mesh passes that gate while the PlumTree eager set has permanently collapsed from \`leaf_max_eager_degree = 2\` to 1. Every publication silently incurs pull-path latency; the \`#611\` failure was invisible to the existing harness.

## Mechanism (verified in source; sg#62 closes the crate side)

1. Under load a CPU stall blows the 2500 ms per-peer send budget; five timeouts in 30 s apply a ≥120 s cooldown.
2. The 1 Hz \`refresh_topic_peers\` re-adds the returning peer as **lazy** then \`can_graft_peer_at\` drops any cooled peer.
3. The cooling floor (sg#32) forbids suppressing the last eligible eager peer, pinning the set at **1** for the rest of the cooldown window.
4. The plane gate stays green; the old oracle never fails.

**\`check_eager_mesh_recovered(peer_scores_by_topic, topic, peer_ids, expected_degree)\`**
- All named peers hold \`role: "eager"\` on the topic
- \`eager_count == expected_degree\` (Leaf default = 2)

- \`last_cool_at_unix_ms\` (monotonic \`Option<u64>\`) did not advance. Note: \`cooling_events\` is f64; \`as_u64()\` returns \`None\` for float JSON and can never detect re-cooling on real snapshots.

## Mechanism

`LeafEgressLimiter` admitted recovery intents first-come-first-served up to `ORDINARY_MAX_INTENTS` (960) / `CRITICAL_MAX_INTENTS` (64) with **no eviction**. | | Decision | Outcome |
|---|---|---|

pulls.title: fix(e2e): poll Sydney roster convergence before asserting self-membership (#480)
pulls.body:
## Problem

In `tests/e2e_vps.sh` section [15/20] Named Groups, after Sydney does
`POST /groups/join`, the script immediately called `GET /groups/$NG` on
Sydney and asserted:

- body contains `$SYD_AID` — "Sydney space member list includes self"
- body contains `"Sydney Space Tester"` — "display name persisted"

Since #480, the invite join is committed by the authority (NYC): Sydney's
local `members` list stays in `pending_authority_commit` state until the
authority-signed `MemberAdded` propagates back over gossip. The immediate
GET returns before convergence, so both assertions reliably fail.

**Evidence:** 7 consecutive failures recorded since
`suite_vps_20260822T210443Z` (found during PR #736 testnet e2e run).

## Fix

Wrap the existing immediate `GET` in a poll loop identical in style to
the NYC roster wait loop a few lines below (lines 781–788). Poll up to
20 × 1 s for Sydney's own view to include `$SYD_AID`, then run both
`check_contains` assertions on the final response. The assertions are
**preserved** — they still fail loudly if convergence never arrives within
the window, proving the joiner's local view converges to include itself
with its display name.

- `bash -n tests/e2e_vps.sh` — syntax OK
- `shellcheck` — no issues at or near the edit
- Not run against the fleet (requires VPS)

Result delivery keeps the original 30-second budget from enqueue and first-20-second raw DM window. Four result coordinators feed four global daemon HTTP workers with a 16-task pending-plus-running bound shared by raw frames, small results, and fallback publication. pulls.title: fix(connect): preserve address-only dial budget
pulls.body:
## Problem

Address-only `connect_addr` calls use an adaptive direct-stage budget of `4 * RTT + 750ms`. With the default 333ms RTT estimate, Happy Eyeballs aborts after 2.082s even though the authoritative connection-establishment deadline is 30s. Under the CPU contention measured in x0x, valid loopback handshakes have taken 5.9s, so the inner transport returns a terminal error before the caller's remaining deadline can help.

Closes #292. Related downstream report: https://github.com/saorsa-labs/x0x/issues/623.

## Change

For automatically derived address-only strategies, give the direct race the remaining overall establishment budget while reserving time only for an enabled, populated relay route. Address-only calls cannot hole-punch because they do not carry an authenticated target peer ID. An oversized relay reserve is capped so it cannot reduce a viable direct route below its configured adaptive slice.

Explicit custom strategies remain authoritative, peer-oriented connection budgeting is unchanged, and every path remains bounded by the configured overall deadline.

## Validation

- Focused delayed-connector regression: a Happy Eyeballs attempt beyond the former adaptive cutoff succeeds within the overall deadline.
- Overall-cap regression: an attempt beyond the overall deadline still times out.
- Relay-reserve, oversized-reserve, custom-strategy, and peer-oriented budget cases are covered.

pulls.title: docs(network): the PubSub receive-pump shed is ADR 0013, not ADR 0010
pulls.body:
Comment-only provenance fix, split out of #706 so that PR stayed free of production-code edits. **Do not merge without independent review.**

## Why this is worth a PR

`src/network.rs` currently **contradicts itself**. Five comments cite ADR 0010 for the priority-aware PubSub receive-pump shed, while the log line emitted by the very function that performs the shed (`:1577`) cites ADR 0013:

```
"[1/6 network] shedding recoverable PubSub control frame (channel >90% full) to preserve EAGER delivery (ADR 0013; rate-limited; see recv_pump.pubsub.shed_priority)"
```

ADR 0013 is the correct one. `docs/adr/0013-priority-aware-pubsub-shed.md:1-5` records exactly why the collision existed:

> # ADR 0013: Priority-Aware PubSub Receive-Pump Shedding
>
> > Renumbered from 0010 → 0013 on 2026-05-30 to resolve a numbering collision with ADR-0010 (GSS Before MLS TreeKEM). Content unchanged; references to ADR 0009 below are to that separate ADR, not self-references.

ADR 0010 is *solely* the GSS ADR and says nothing about receive-pump shedding, so anyone following these citations to understand the shed policy landed on group cryptography instead.

## The five sites

All describe the same shed:

| site | context |
|---|---|
| `:722` | `shed_priority` field doc on `RecvPumpStreamSnapshot` |
| `:1365` | `channel_pressure_exceeds_shed_threshold` doc |

Refs #613, #501, #674. **Do not merge without maintainer review** — one of the two changes (the quiescence barrier) is a judgement call I am flagging explicitly below.

## What this is, and what it is not

This is **not** a threshold loosening and **not** a tolerance. The D5 oracle still requires non-zero bus dissemination (eager or IHAVE) and the O5 oracle still requires zero bus egress of any kind. The producer pin stays at `0.5.80` in all four places. Both changes fix how the meter *reads* the measured arms.

## 1. The record began at saorsa-gossip's decode (accounting defect)

`raw_sample` captured `egress`, `participation` and `stage_stats()`. Every one of those starts **after** x0x's own receive pump has handed the frame to the gossip dispatcher. That pump silently drops PubSub frames when its bounded forward channel is full (`src/network.rs`, `record_dropped_full`) and proactively sheds recoverable control frames near overload (`shed_priority`, ADR 0010).

So three physically different situations produced an identical failure line:

- the generator's frames never reached this host;
- they reached it and x0x's own queue discarded them;
- they were decoded and D5 refused to forward them.

Only the third is the defect the oracle is claiming to detect. This is why every occurrence has had to be hand-classified as "pre-existing #613".

pulls.title: chore(pubsub): WAN send-timeout tunables — threshold 8, 4 s budget, retuned 60 s window (PR #29)
pulls.body:
Split from the cooldown-bypass PR (#73, which replaces the closed #71) per the round-2 review: **these are live fleet constants** — every production send-timeout path reads them — unlike the two test-only fallback cooldown constants folded into #73. Closes the tunables half of #29.

## Change

Bootstrap nodes on public WAN paths (Hetzner→DigitalOcean, 330–560 ms RTT) accumulated 12k–33k budget-pressure/cooling events per day under constants tuned for low-latency meshes.

| Constant | Before | After | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PER_PEER_REPUBLISH_TIMEOUT` | 2500 ms | **4000 ms** | ~7 RTTs of headroom on the worst observed hop (Helsinki→Sydney, 560 ms). Nearly inert for warm peers (`adaptive_timeout` ignores the floor once RTT samples exist) but moves the x0x #613 stranded-publish retry 5 s → 8 s (it waits 2× the budget). |
| `PEER_TIMEOUT_THRESHOLD` | 5 | **8** | One more loss-episode of de-noising at the 4 s budget. |
| `PEER_TIMEOUT_WINDOW` | 30 s | **60 s** | Retuned WITH the threshold — see below. |

## Why the window must move with the threshold

The maximum inter-timeout interval that can still trip cooling inside one window is `window / (threshold − 1)` (the first timeout starts the window; N timeouts span N−1 intervals):

- 30 s / 5 = **7.5 s** (today's baseline)
- 30 s / 8 = **4.29 s** ← threshold 8 alone: retires timeout cooling for exactly the high-RTT WAN peers it targets (any peer whose p95 send duration sits above ~1.72 s at the 4 s budget)
- 60 s / 8 = **8.57 s*

```

pulls.title: fix(pubsub): shutdown lifecycle for background tasks — IHAVE flusher no longer livelocks after transport shutdown (#42)
pulls.body:
## #42 — background tasks get a shutdown lifecycle; the IHAVE flusher no longer livelocks

### Premise — verified against today's code

**Confirmed.** `spawn_ihave_flusher` (`crates/pubsub/src/lib.rs:8082-8102` on origin/main) does `tokio::spawn(async move { loop { interval.tick().await; flush_ihave_batches(...).await; } })` and **drops the JoinHandle**; there is no shutdown token, no cancellation path, and no `shutdown()` anywhere on `PlumtreePubSub`. Its four siblings (cache cleaner, degree maintainer, anti-entropy, connected-peers refresher) are the same shape. What livelocks: after transport shutdown every flush attempt fails instantly ("node not initialized", opaque `anyhow` from the transport trait), is logged at WARN and retried at flush cadence — the issue measured ~10 Hz per LAN peer, all 16 workers saturated, +700 MB RSS, ~10 MB of WARN logs, SIGTERM never exits (x0x #368/#371; x0x ships a 5 s force-exit watchdog). Since `ValidationAction::LazyForward` (0.5.79) the flusher is the relay's delivery path, so this is a delivery defect.

### Change

- Every background task `select!`s a `watch` shutdown token at its scheduling points — the initial jitter sleep and each loop tick — so it observes the token whenever it is between iterations (`lib.rs` — all five `spawn_*` fns). Once a tick arm wins, the task *body* runs to completion unguarded; that is bounded by the body's own awaits (per-peer send timeouts), and `shutdown`'s grace-plus-abort backstop covers the remainder.

PR #686 (commit `501aa7a`) fixed the blob-fetch retry gap in

pulls.title: feat(pubsub): ValidationAction::LazyForward — withhold eager re-publish, announce via IHAVE (#59)
pulls.body:
Closes #59

## Mechanism

`ValidationAction::LazyForward` (x0x #674 C2): a relay node delivers locally, caches and keeps the message IWANT-serveable, **withholds the eager re-publish** (the eager set is emptied exactly as `DeliverOnly` does), but still announces the msg_id via IHAVE — to the lazy set as usual **and** to every peer whose eager send was withheld.

- New per-topic `lazy_withheld: Vec<LazyWithheldEntry>` (`msg_id`/`targets`/`served`), bounded at `MAX_IHAVE_BATCH_SIZE` like `stranded_ihave` but deliberately **not** reusing it — that path's bounded retry re-sends cached EAGER wire bytes, exactly what this verdict withholds.
- `flush_ihave_batches` merges the withheld targets into `ihave_targets` and consumes them (lossy, same as `pending_ihave`); a pre-flush IWANT pull marks the entry served so it isn't re-advertised.

pulls.body:
## Decision: (b) — Invariant E is subsumed, not an independent property

Invariant E ("PlaneRefuse") exists only in #292 prose. After auditing the current code on main, it is fully subsumed by the composition of invariant A and the `disconnect_with_reason` ordering contract. No new product behaviour is needed; no gap exists.

## Proof

1. `plane_handle_hello` (`src/network.rs:3483`) detects a cross-plane mismatch and calls `disconnect_with_reason(&peer, PolicyRejection)`.
2. `disconnect_with_reason` (`src/network.rs:3128`) calls `self.suppress_reconnect(peer_id.0, reason)` at `src/network.rs:3133` **before** `node.disconnect()` — the tombstone is live before the QUIC close.
3. From that moment, `peer_admission` (`src/network.rs:3192`, invariant A) returns `Suppressed`, blocking all paths: per-frame drops (B), outbound dials (C), inbound accepts (D).
4. `PolicyRejection` has a `None` TTL (`src/network.rs:5537`): the tombstone never expires.

No window exists between mismatch detection and `Suppressed` admission status. The `PlanePending → Admitted` transition is permanently blocked.

`cross_plane_pair_does_not_exchange_gossip` already proves the full observable chain: authenticated `Established`, `PolicyRejection` disconnect event, tombstone, transport close, and stay-down across eager-set refresh ticks. A separate invariant-E test would be a duplicate.

Fixes #283

## Mechanism (per the issue, confirmed in code)

`NatTraversalEndpoint::shutdown` closed only the canonical `connections` entries. Superseded-but-alive lifecycle survivors were closed merely **implicitly** by the post-drain `connection_lifecycle.clear()`, immediately before `release_socket_for_shutdown` yanked the socket — so their CONNECTION_CLOSE frames frequently never transmitted. `shutdown` now explicitly closes **every** lifecycle-tracked generation (Superseded survivors included) **before** the bounded drain (`wait_idle`), so the close frames flush while the socket still exists and the remote observes the disconnect within the drain window (5 s). pulls.title: fix(p2p): disconnect must make the peer unobservable before teardown completes
pulls.body:
Fixes #278; refs saorsa-labs/x0x#277

## Root cause

`disconnect()` → `do_cleanup_connection(CleanupScope::Peer)` → `remove_connection_with_reason()` tears down **only the current winner generation**: it removes the winner-map (`nat_traversal_api.connections`) entry, marks that one generation `Closed`, and closes that connection. Surviving **`Superseded`** generations — kept open for their drain window under simultaneous-open churn — stay open with `close_reason() == None` and remain promotable.

The next `get_connection(peer)` that misses the winner map calls `repromote_surviving_connection()`, which **promotes the stale survivor back to `Live` and re-inserts it into the winner map**. Consequences:

- After `disconnect()` returns, `open_bi()`/`send()` can hand out streams on an old, half-dead connection: writes fail with `sending stopped by peer: error 0` (x0x#277 shape A) or succeed into a send buffer that the eventual teardown discards — no error surfaces, so application replay logic never fires (shape B).
- Racing a `connect_addr()`: `is_connected()` (backed by `connected_peers`) can report the peer live while the winner map still holds the old generation — and `candidate_wins` can even reject the fresh connection in favor of the repromoted stale one.

## Fix (local, no wire/API change)

- **`NatTraversalEndpoint::close_all_connection_generations(peer_id, reason)`** (`src/nat_traversal_api.rs`): marks every non-closed tracked generation `Closed` under the lifecycle write

pulls.title: fix(pubsub): dedup inbound EAGER before the ML-DSA-65 verify
pulls.body:
Refs saorsa-labs/x0x#674 (Design B). Target for 0.5.78. **No wire/format change.**

## Root cause

`PlumtreePubSub::handle_eager_admitted` (crates/pubsub/src/lib.rs) ran the full ML-DSA-65 signature verify (`verify_message_signature`, ~826 µs measured) **before** consulting the bounded msg-id cache (`has_message`), so every duplicate EAGER arrival was verified and then dropped four lines later. This includes **IWANT repair responses, which return as EAGER frames carrying the original msg_id** — a message arriving once via EAGER and again via repair was verified twice.

Measured on a live bootstrap (NYC testnet, 125 s window, x0x #674):

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| inbound EAGER | 158.4 /s |
| unique messages cached | 113.4 /s |
| duplicate EAGER verified-then-discarded | **45.0 /s = 28.4% of EAGER** |
| wasted verify CPU | 45.0 × 826 µs ≈ 37 ms/s = **5.9% of daemon CPU** |

The bounded, TTL'd msg-id cache already **is** the verify memo; the only defect was that it was consulted after the verify instead of before it. ~15 lines, no new data structure, no memory bound to choose.

## Change

In `handle_eager_admitted`, for **unregistered topics** (all production x0x traffic — x0x registers no topics):

## Root cause

ADR-0061 §3 states that *versioned templates and loaded-policy readback establish support, not a marker in isolation* — but the supervised-restart classification trusted `X0X_SUPERVISED=1` alone. `x0x autostart --repair` verifies `KeepAlive: true` **at repair time only**; nothing re-checks the job policy **at upgrade time**. pulls.body:
## Root cause (#656, "bonus" 0.42.0 regression)

`src/gossip/egress.rs` is new in v0.42.0. Its `track_iwant` — called from `handle_incoming` (`src/gossip/pubsub.rs`) on every inbound IWANT frame *before* the frame reaches `plumtree.handle_message` — performed a **full ML-DSA-65 signature verification** solely to decide whether the `iwant_matched_eager_attempt_msgs` / `iwant_matched_eager_attempt_bytes` diagnostic counters may track the frame's `(peer, topic, message)` keys. PlumTree verifies the same frame again immediately after and **ignores unauthenticated IWANTs before acting on them**, so the verify gated only a diagnostics counter. At the profiled 106 IWANT/s that is ~106 redundant verifies/s ≈ **4% of a core** of pure overhead.

Removed the verify (and the header re-serialization that existed only to feed it). The cheap structural gates stay: exact `GossipMessage` decode, `IWant` kind, v2 header, payload-hash binding (`blake3(payload)`), decodable id list. The tracking keys are now documented — in `track_iwant`'s doc comment, on the `repair_msgs`/`repair_bytes` fields, and in the `/diagnostics/gossip` `semantics` string — as **unverified frame fields that PlumTree itself authenticates**. A forged IWANT creates entries that can only misclassify a repair send sg would never originate for it (sg rejects the forged frame, sends nothing), so the counters cannot be inflated beyond the repair traffic the frame's own rejection already precluded. **The 0.42.0 counter na

One targeted (ADR-0030) capability request woke `DmCapabilityService`'s publisher loop and caused **three** signed publishes: the digest extension on `caps/v2/digest`, the answer on `caps/v1/response/targeted-v2`, **and** a copy of the full advert on the fleet-wide `x0x/caps/v1` (`respond_on_steady`). ## Fix — a targeted request now costs **two** publishes, not three

- The answer goes to the Critical `caps/v1/response/targeted-v2` topic the requester listens on.
- The `caps/v2/digest` extension **still publishes on every advert cycle** (deliberate — see below).
- The steady `caps/v1` advert rides its own cadence: startup burst, timer beat, or capability upgrade (`steady_cycle` wake-reason tracking replaces `respond_on_steady`, covering both periodic and on-demand modes). pulls.title: fix(blob): owner-only serving + per-digest coalescing in the blob responder
pulls.body:
## Root cause (#656, ranked fix 1 + 4)

`AnnounceBlobCache::serve_request` answered blob requests **cache-first**: any node that had ever cached peer X's blob became a responder for X. On the profiled 27-node fleet every miss drew a broadcast response from every cache holder — `announce/v3/blob` ran at **46.7 msgs/s, 825 KB/s** against a documented 0.045 fetches/s steady state, and each ~17.6 KB response is delivered to and ML-DSA-verified by all peers. The responder's coalescing window was one **global** `Instant` per task, so a busy blob silently dropped every unrelated digest's request for a second at a time, pushing requesters into the 5 s fetch-timeout retry loop — a starvation loop with positive feedback.

## Fix

- `serve_request` is now **owner-only**: it answers only when the requested digest matches this node's own current `(user_id, agent_certificate)` pair. Cached peer blobs are never served. Cuts responders from N to 1 per request.
- The responder's 1 s coalescing window is tracked **per digest** (bounded map, 256 entries, stalest evicted) instead of one global instant, so concurrent digests no longer starve each other.

~30 production lines in `src/announce_blob.rs`; `serve_request`'s only caller is `spawn_blob_responder`.

## Root cause

ant-quic 0.27.50 honours an explicit P2P `bind_address` exactly (ant-quic #274); before that, an interface-specific bind was silently widened to a wildcard socket, so every host interface address was *accidentally* dialable. #638/#649 fixed the agent card (`card_addresses` filters interface hints to the bound address for specifically bound listeners), but the three gossip announce producers — `HeartbeatContext::announce()` (src/lib.rs), `Agent::announce_identity()`, and `Agent::announcement_addresses()` — still enumerated every interface address (and the UDP-connect-probed global IPv6) unconditionally.

## Scope

Fixes #654 — the three non-blocking follow-ups recorded by the round-3 review of #652.

**Item 3 (the substantive one).** `merge_delta` decides ONCE whether an envelope-verified writer may apply content fields (`content_allowed`, issue #349 Layer A) — and since #643 that gate also covers removal evidence: evidence from a writer the policy rejects is neither applied nor recorded. Worse, the prune routes through `delta_remove_task`, which records the ids in the raise-only `known_removed` set, so the pruned replica would **forward the unauthorized deletion evidence fleet-wide** in its own serves.
