feat(history): ADR 0116 slice A — parse and validate the [history] rules
pulls.body:
ADR 0116 slice A (#1264 part 2): parse and validate the new `[history]` rules. Recording and retention behaviour do not change.

**What it does**
- New `src/history/policy.rs`:
  - rule types `DmRecording`, `TopicRecording`, `RetainedClass` (no `ephemeral`), and `ClassLimit` / `TopicRule`, both `deny_unknown_fields`;
  - `HistoryPolicy::compile`, which applies every ADR 0116 §1 check: duplicate class or prefix, unknown key or value, a class entry with no bound, an empty or over-256-byte prefix, more than 256 rules, and overflowing bounds. Zero bytes is a bound; zero age is not.
  - topic rules kept in prefix byte order, with a literal, case-sensitive, longest-prefix match that takes the whole winning rule.
- **Build guard.** A crate-private guard refuses every rule this build cannot enforce yet ("not supported by this build"). Only prefix-only topic rules and explicit `inherit` pass, so no release accepts a rule and silently ignores it. Slices B and C lift the parts they enforce.
- `HistoryConfig` gains `dm_recording`, `class_limits` and `topic_rules`. All are omitted when default, so a serialized default config is byte-identical. `HistoryConfig` itself stays permissive (ADR 0085 / ADR 0116 §5), so older binaries ignore the new keys.
- `HistoryService::open` validates before `Store::open`, so a refused config creates no `history.db`. `HistoryHandle::policy()` exposes the compiled policy.
- x0xd `load_config` validates `[history]` whether or not history is enabled (plan ruling

pulls.title: fix(server): drain the remaining detached group tasks at shutdown (#1274)
pulls.body:
Fixes #1274. Follow-up: #1288.

**Problem.** Group tasks spawned with a plain `tokio::spawn` captured `AppState`/`Agent` and were not part of the shutdown drain. After `shutdown_and_wait` returned they still held the daemon, so an in-process relaunch on the same directory (the iOS embedder path) failed with `history.db: database is locked`.

**Fix.** Every holder is now in the drain. Send-only work uses `spawn_detached` (2 s grace, then abort); work that persists uses `spawn_shielded`.
- **The three named holders, all send-only, now detached:**
  - public-group fan-out: the gossip leg and member unicasts. The message and its history row are cached before the race starts.
  - predecessor-relay fallback (`spawn_predecessor_relay_fallback_offer`). The durable `insert_requester_offer_obligation` is still awaited before the 201 and retried by the requester-offer worker. An aborted fallback offer may be lost; no worker retries it.
  - KeyPackage catch-up requests. The response is applied by the catch-up listener, which is already shielded (#1275).
- **Siblings found in the audit:**
  - KV delta direct delivery: detached.
  - file-chunk stream: detached; a refused stream marks its transfer failed, in memory.
  - owner-sync profile write: it persists, so it is now **shielded**.
- **ADR 0107 join-artifact egress** could hold AppState for up to 10 minutes.
  - A new egress is refused under the registry lock, before any clone or spawn, once `shutdown_started` is cancelled. A refused bod

pulls.title: fix(history): an unparseable scope_limits entry no longer stops the retention pass (#1286)
pulls.body:
Fixes #1286.

**Defect.** A `[[history.scope_limits]]` entry whose `scope` fails to parse made every retention pass return `Err` at phase 3 (`Scope::parse(&limit.scope)?`). Phase 4 (the #1264 part 1 whole-database byte cap), the scope limits after the bad one, and `cleanup_canonical_ids` never ran, so one typo let `history.db` grow without bound.

**Fix (option a, `src/history/store.rs`):**
- Phase 3 skips an unparseable entry and keeps going. The later limits, the global cap and cleanup run as before.
- `Store::skipped_scope_limits()` reports how many entries the latest pass skipped. It is overwritten every pass and does not accumulate.
- One `tracing::warn!` per open store names up to 16 bad entries. It is emitted only after the pass has released both the retention and connection mutexes, so a subscriber that reads the store cannot deadlock the pass. It is still emitted if a later phase fails.
- `HistoryService::open` is unchanged, so every config that opened before still opens. Valid configs run the same SQL in the same order.
- No public struct gains a field. The only API addition is the read-only method above.

**Tests** (inert; run in the loopback-only sandbox, with the test list checked first):
- The red test (7ef6d9b, tests only) fails on main with `Err(InvalidScope("not-a-scope"))` at pass 0. An orphaned canonical-id row planted after setup proves the cleanup phase now runs.
- `skip_warning_is_emitted_with_no_store_lock_held` fails on the round-1 fix with both locks

pulls.title: fix(#310): hole-punch winner check and insert under the lifecycle lock
pulls.body:
Addresses #310: fixes its first bullet (concurrent hole-punch winners). The coordinator bullet moves to #313.

**Problem.** Two successful hole-punch candidates for the same peer could both pass the unlocked `contains_key` duplicate check before either took the lifecycle lock. Both then inserted, the second displaced the first without closing it, and both connections stayed open.

**Fix** (`src/nat_traversal_api.rs`):
- New `insert_hole_punch_winner_parts` does the shutdown re-check, the duplicate check and the insert in one `connection_lifecycle.write()` section. The policy is unchanged: the connection already in the slot keeps it, and the later winner is closed as a duplicate.
- With this, all four production winner-map inserts hold the lifecycle lock, so each check-and-insert is atomic against the others. Lock order is unchanged.
- The accepted-coordination insert is byte-identical to master apart from a comment. It replaces the slot and closes nothing. Closing the displaced winner there can kill a connection the application is still reading, and the decision can go stale before the close runs (Codex round-1 P2-1 and P2-2). Retiring it safely needs reader handover, draining and two-ended arbitration; that is tracked in #313.

**Tests** (a `#[cfg(test)]` `WinnerInsertGate` parks the first winner just before the lock):
- `concurrent_hole_punch_winners_leave_no_orphaned_connection`: fails on master 3/3, passes on the fix.
- `coordinator_dial_leaves_a_displaced_untracked_winne

pulls.title: fix(server): shield listener-driven group-state applies from the shutdown drain (#1275)
pulls.body:
Fixes #1275: the server's group listeners applied events inline. At shutdown they were aborted after the 2 s grace, or at once in the member-certificate bridge's case, so an apply could be cut off while persisting roster or TreeKEM state. That leaves a torn write or a leftover temp file.

**Fix.** Each state-writing apply in ten listener paths (L1–L10) now runs through `AppState::run_shielded` (from #1278). The receive loops stay abortable.
- L1: per-group metadata
- L2: certificate-fetch responses
- L3: direct-channel metadata
- L4: join-result
- L5: TreeKEM catch-up
- L6: legacy bootstrap
- L7: predecessor relay
- L8: KV delta
- L9: v2 bootstrap
- L10: the member-certificate bridge

Shutdown never aborts a running shielded apply; it refuses new ones and waits up to 10 s.
- **Order:** each listener awaits each shielded apply before reading its next message, so its events still apply one at a time, in arrival order. Different listeners for the same group remain serialised by the per-group membership mutex. The existing #1256 queued-followup test passes.
- **Refused or panicking apply:** `run_shielded` returns `None` and the listener stops. Before, a panic inside an inline apply also stopped the listener.
- `ensure_named_group_metadata_listener` and `spawn_public_message_listener` refuse to install a listener once `shutdown_started` is cancelled, so a listener installed after the drain cannot hold AppState.
- `dispatch_join_result_message` returns `bool`, so the join-result li

pulls.title: fix(network): refuse session-registry inserts once teardown starts (#1277)
pulls.body:
Fixes #1277: a send racing network teardown could re-insert a session into `authenticated_sessions` after it was cleared, so a stale session handle outlived shutdown.

**Cause.** `current_session_for_peer` is the only insert. Its two callers in `send_to_peer_guarded` can hold a `LinkNode` that `require_node` returned before teardown started, and then insert after the teardown worker cleared the registry.

**Fix (`src/network.rs` only).**
- The registry holds a clone of the #1262 teardown token. `current_session_for_peer` checks it under the registry mutex, the same lock the clear takes, and returns `None` once teardown has started: no reuse, no insert.
- The coordinator cancels the token before the teardown worker starts.
- The worker clears the registry again after `try_shutdown`, as a backup.
- Behaviour change, during teardown only: a guarded send in flight fails instead of getting a session.

**Test.** `network::tests::issue1277_send_racing_teardown_cannot_reinsert_a_session` binds no socket. It uses the W3-H sim fabric with a test-only pause between the clear and the transport shutdown.
- RED on the test commit; GREEN with the fix.
- Also run: the 19 `issue126*` shutdown tests and the session and coordinator tests, 73/73. These ran from a nextest archive whose test list was checked, in the loopback-only sandbox.
- Mutation checks: disabling the lock check fails the test. Removing only the second clear still passes, so that clear is a backup.

**Review.** Claude authored;

pulls.title: fix(server): release AppState/Agent at shutdown after group joins and TreeKEM stores (#1269, #1250)
pulls.body:
Fixes #1269 and #1250: AppState and the Agent outlived `shutdown_and_wait`, so the exclusive `history.db` lock blocked an in-process relaunch on the same data dir for more than 60 s.

**User-visible effect.** An embedder (iOS, in-process `x0x::server::serve`) that relaunches the daemon after a group join or after opening a TreeKEM group store got `database is locked`. Now AppState and the Agent are released the moment `shutdown_and_wait` returns, and the relaunch succeeds immediately.

**Cause.** Two independent mechanisms; each one alone blocked the relaunch.
1. **Background group tasks that no shutdown step stopped.** These were the delayed and immediate group-event delivery, the chat announcement, join attempts (`pending_join_attempts`), the control-blob download, the join-result and Welcome fetch workers and their supervisors, and delegation redelivery.
2. **Arc cycles (#1250).** The TreeKEM store protector and the public-store refresh hook held `Arc<AppState>`, while AppState owns the store. The GSS hook cycle was fixed in #1273.

**Fix.**
- `AppState::detached_tasks`: shutdown closes admission, collects the tasks, gives them the existing 2 s grace, then aborts.
- `AppState::shielded_tasks`, with `spawn_shielded` and `run_shielded`, for applies that write roster or TreeKEM state:
  - the applied half of the control-blob pull;
  - the owner-certificate retry.

  Shutdown never aborts these mid-write. It refuses new ones and waits up to 10 s. The fetch half stays abortable

fix(kv): repair a survivor's store after the rekey gap; break the GSS hook AppState cycle (#1266)
pulls.body:
Completes the #1266 fix (#1270 kept a survivor's store during the rekey gap). This PR recovers records that arrived *during* the gap, and fixes a shutdown leak found on the way.

**User-visible effect.** After a member removal, a surviving member that received a sealed record before its new key share could not open the record. It dropped it and never saw it, until a restart. Now, when the store's key returns, it asks the group once for the current state, and once more after the responder cooldown. The missing record arrives.

**Changes.**
- `5be45a9` + `93dd602` + `63e2fdc`:
  - **Repair.** When a GSS store goes from KeyPending to Current, `KvStoreSync::request_state_repair` sends one sealed `StateRequest`, reusing the existing message and the bootstrap requester's sealing, publication gate and counters. After the 15 s responder cooldown it sends exactly one more, re-authorized and re-sealed. That is at most 2 per gap. If the first cannot be sealed, no retry is sent.
  - **Task lifetime.** The repair runs as an Agent-tracked task. Every wait ends on Agent shutdown or sync cancel, and the lookup is inside the 90 s deadline. It holds `Weak<AppState>`.
  - **Once per gap.** The latch is decided while the named-groups read guard is held, so concurrent refreshes start one repair per gap.
  - **Pre-existing leak fixed.** The GSS refresh hook held `Arc<AppState>`: AppState → store → sync → hook → AppState. So on main, an open GSS store kept AppState, the Agent and `history.db` alive

pulls.title: fix(history): reaper byte cap converges without over-deleting (#1264 part 1)
pulls.body:
Addresses #1264 part 1 (part 2 stays open): the history reaper's byte cap never converged.

**User-visible effect.** When durable history went over `history.max_bytes`, each reaper pass deleted most of the remaining history and still never reached the cap. In the embedder's repro on a 1.4 GB store, three passes went 600k → 55.8k → 20.5k → 10.4k rows while the file stayed at 224 MB or more. The reaper now reclaims space first and deletes close to the minimum needed.

**Cause.** The reaper measured the file size (`page_count × page_size`). Each delete fires the FTS5 `'delete'` trigger, which appends tombstone postings, so the measured size barely moved. The bundled SQLite 3.46.0 `incremental_vacuum` also moves only one page per statement, so freed pages stayed in the file.

**Fix (`src/history/store.rs`), C-1264-1/2 design.**
- Measure **live** bytes: `(page_count − freelist_count) × page_size`.
- One retention pass holds the retention mutex and the connection.
- **Reclamation** is time-bounded (named budget), with a deadline check before every statement:
  - positive-rank FTS `'merge'` slices;
  - bounded `incremental_vacuum` steps;
  - `wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)` between slices, so the WAL stays bounded.
  - A single in-flight statement can overrun; this is documented.
- **Eviction phases** that exist on main (pinned ceilings, per-scope limits, age) run to completion every pass, in bounded batches, at the same cost as main.
- **Global-cap eviction** deletes the oldest eligible

pulls.title: fix(network): in-process shutdown abandons in-flight dials and no longer stalls on node guards (#1262, #1263 part 1)
pulls.body:
Fixes #1262 (an embedded daemon's graceful shutdown leaks its UDP socket) and #1263 part 1 (shutdown stalls behind node read guards).

**User-visible effect.** Mobile and desktop embedders that run `x0x::server::serve` in-process, with several daemons in one process, often failed graceful shutdown with `shutdown socket release timeout ... weak_socket_owner_still_live`, and the relaunch then failed. Shutdown could also stall for up to 30 s (124 s in the reporter's field logs) behind a peer that stopped reading.

**Cause (#1262).** Several x0x tasks dial peers and were not stopped by teardown:
- detached bootstrap dials (15 s timeout, `src/lib.rs` ~13360);
- proactive reconnects, which checked the shutdown token only between attempts (~18591/18610);
- gossip-membership dials (`src/network.rs` ~6071);
- announcement auto-connects.

An in-flight QUIC handshake holds the endpoint's original socket, and ant-quic's shutdown closes only registered connections. The result was a 5 s `wait_idle` timeout, then the settle timeout. It shows up with several daemons in one process because relaunched peers come back on new ports and survivors keep dialling the dead addresses.

**Cause (#1263 part 1).** Node read guards were held across network awaits, so `try_shutdown`'s write lock waited behind a send blocked on a frozen peer.

**Fix.**
- `451b7f8`: a teardown token is cancelled before the node is taken. Every x0x dial site goes through `dial_until_teardown`, so in-flight dials are dropped w

pulls.title: fix(stores): keep a survivor's GSS store while its rekey share is pending (#1266)
pulls.body:
Fixes the production bug behind part of #1266: after a member is removed from a GSS group, a surviving member can permanently lose its encrypted group store.

**User-visible effect.** Alice removes Charlie. Bob is still a member, but if Bob's daemon applies the MemberRemoved before his new key share arrives, any read of the group store in that gap retires the store. From then on, Bob's `GET /stores/...` returns `404 store not found`, even after the share installs. Only reopening the store (`POST /groups/:id/stores`) or restarting the daemon recovers it.

**Cause.** Applying the newer removal epoch clears Bob's shared secret (`named_groups.rs` ~12404). The store refresh (`stores.rs` ~1293, ~1460, ~1509) treated "no secret" the same as "no longer eligible", so it retired the store and removed it from the registry. Nothing recreated it when the share installed (~13605).

**Fix (`src/server/routes/stores.rs`).** The refresh check now has three outcomes: Current, KeyPending and Ineligible.
- **KeyPending**: the member is still eligible and active but has no secret for the new epoch. The store stays registered and cannot seal, open or write. The old secret is dropped, and local reads of the existing copy keep working. The first refresh after the share installs re-arms it at the new epoch.
- **Ineligible** retires the store exactly as before: removed, banned, pending, withdrawn, fork-quarantined, plane or policy change, binding mismatch, or missing group.
- Opening or restoring a st

pulls.title: fix(history): boot backfill scans each row once; open off the async worker (#1263 part 2)
pulls.body:
Fixes #1263 part 2: boot stalls for about 2 min on a large history.db.

**User-visible effect.** An embedded or desktop daemon with a large durable history (hundreds of MB, many MLS plaintext rows) no longer rescans that history on every start. The open no longer blocks an async worker.

**Cause.** `backfill_canonical_ids` ran on every `Store::open` and rescanned every `scope_kind=1` row that had no canonical projection. Rows that `canonical_group_msg_id` rejects never get a projection (MLS plaintext rows from `record_mls_history`), so they were rescanned forever. With no `sqlite_stat1`, each 256-row batch also sorted every remaining candidate, making the scan O(n²).

**Fix.**
- A persisted progress cursor (`history_backfill_progress`, singleton). Every row is examined once; the cursor commits with each batch.
- The trigger `history_backfill_lower` lowers the cursor when any writer inserts at or below it, including older binaries, because triggers live in the DB file. Reused rowids are therefore rescanned.
- A projection table recreated empty resets the cursor, inside one setup transaction.
- The batch scan uses a forced rowid-range plan (`+scope_kind`, `ORDER BY id`).
- `AgentBuilder::build` runs the blocking open in `spawn_blocking`. It starts the writer and reaper only after the await, so a cancelled build leaves no unowned service.
- `HistoryService::start` stays synchronous; the public API is unchanged.
- `SCHEMA_VERSION` stays 4. The new table and trigger are additive d

pulls.title: docs: capture x0x architecture and 15-ADR consolidation plan
pulls.body:
## Summary

x0x has 100 numbered ADRs. The current set spreads the product scope and delivery guarantees across many records. This PR captures the architecture review and the agreed direction in 15 readable replacement drafts.

- Add A01–A15, with context, decisions, consequences, validation and source links. A04 and A07 specify scoped agent inboxes, push, restart recovery, consumer acknowledgments, and adapters for ACP or hosted model APIs.
- Retain the original HTML review byte for byte. Add a GitHub-readable Markdown copy, its research links, the documentation inventory and source hashes.
- Map all 100 source ADRs to a primary replacement slot. Keep the clause-level transfer review explicit.
- Limit the consolidated set to 15 current slots. Future decisions use new revisions of those slots. CI rejects an extra slot, an unindexed record, a missing record, duplicate slots and premature acceptance.

## What it does

fix(revocation): #1116 never overwrite an unreadable revocation store (ADR 0085 rule 4)
pulls.body:
Refs #1116 (P1), **slice A**. Accepted ADR 0085 rule 4: a file that doesn't decode is refused and left untouched; the software never overwrites a file it cannot read.

## Problem
All three revocation stores (v1 `revocations.bin`, v2 binding tombstones, v3 share-grant revocations) loaded an unreadable file as empty, and the next persist wrote the in-memory set over it. The original revocation evidence was destroyed.

## Fix
- Each store records when its file fails to read or decode. Every writer re-validates the existing bytes under a per-path lock and **refuses to overwrite** an unreadable file: the original bytes stay byte-identical. The writers covered are local revoke, the pre-encoded gossip saves, the binding writer, key-move persistence and the v3 merge writer. The check is structural (magic + strict bincode decode, no trailing bytes) and does no signature work under a lock.
- A missing file still allows first-run creation; an operator repair (the file becomes readable) unblocks writes.
- The new revocation stays **enforced in memory**, the subject is evicted, and the revocation is **gossiped**. WARN `persistence_blocked=true` repeats at most every 30 s per path.
- **Out of scope:** the load still fails open (ADR-0018 §Storage). Failing closed is ADR 0098.

## Behaviour changes (for release notes)
- When a revocation store is unreadable, a revoke is applied and published, but **not durable**:
  - `POST /identity/revoke` and the binding revoke route return **500 "applied

pulls.title: fix(gossip): #1114 deliver only verified, identified senders to apps
pulls.body:
**Red-first draft.** This push holds only the red tests (d2a01be). CI should fail exactly the three `issue1114_*` tests. The fix (3dc1ab2) follows after CI shows red.

Refs #1114 (P1, security; charter invariant I3).

## Problem
`decode_for_delivery` (src/gossip/pubsub.rs) delivered inner V1 payloads with `sender=None, verified=false`. Signature, revocation and Blocked checks were conditional on a sender, so an unsigned V1 payload inside a valid outer frame reached apps via the SDK, SSE and WS with no sender checks, and a revoked or Blocked sender could get through by downgrading to V1.

## Compatibility (verified in code)
- The only V1 emit site (`pubsub.rs` ~2222) runs only when a `PubSubManager` has no signing context. The production Agent build always passes one, in v0.45.0, v0.46.0 and v0.46.3. No released x0xd emits inner V1 on any topic, including `x0x.*`, the DM inbox and the legacy bus.
- 0.45.x/0.46.x peers publish V2/V3, which always decode with a sender. No product delivery is lost, so no compatibility window or flag is needed.

## Fix (3dc1ab2)
- `decode_for_delivery` delivers only `Some(sender)` with `verified`; the revocation and Blocked checks then run unconditionally.
- Test fixtures that read deliveries back are now signed (pubsub, dm_inbox, dm_capability, kv, crdt, tasks); negative tests gained liveness checks so they cannot pass vacuously.

## Follow-ups (to be filed)
- Remove V1 emission (changes the public `PubSubManager::new(_, None)` contract).
- Relay

Part of #1115, #1168, #1106 and #1104 (Track M-safety, goal M, slice M2). Docs only. The ADR is **Proposed**; only David marks it Accepted. M1/M2 are fixes to shipped behaviour and do not need R12 (D21).

**What it decides (summary):**

2. Before the swap, the OLD binary runs a side-effect-free probe of the candidate binaries. This covers a binary that cannot exec (#1168, the 7b(C) gap).

4. A stable launcher owned by the supervisor (systemd, launchd, Windows) recovers a binary that cannot exec.
5. Shutdown flushes before exit, with an acknowledgement and a time bound.
6. The daemon and the managed CLI roll back together (#1104).
7. StagedRollout is wired up, with one writer per host (#1106).
8. Recovery state is versioned, and the ADR 0085 downgrade rules still apply.
9. Exit test: crash-loop and cannot-exec in CI, plus the 7/7a/7b canaries for each v0.46.x and the first M2 release.

It supersedes ADR 0061 Decision §6 only, upon acceptance.

**Open questions for David** are in the ADR: the retry, readiness and health bounds; the rollout minimum; whether Windows recovery gates M-safe; backup retention and disk reserve.

pulls.title: ci: fix rustc 1.99 fetch_update deprecation and MSRV uuid pin
pulls.body:
## What broke and why

rustc 1.99.0 (stable, released 2026-10-01) deprecated `Atomic*::fetch_update`. With `-D warnings` in effect, this caused the pubsub crate's test-only helper `take_hang_slot` (crates/pubsub/src/lib.rs) to fail to compile, breaking the main CI lint and test jobs. Separately, the MSRV job began failing before compilation because a fresh `cargo resolve` now picks uuid 1.27.0, which declares `rust-version = "1.89"` — one minor above the workspace MSRV of 1.88.

## Changes

**1. Replace `fetch_update` with a `compare_exchange` CAS loop** (`crates/pubsub/src/lib.rs`)

The single call site is the test helper `take_hang_slot`. The replacement loop is semantically identical: it attempts to decrement a counter that is > 0, retries on spurious failure, and returns `true` iff the decrement succeeded. Ordering arguments (`SeqCst` / `SeqCst`) are preserved unchanged. No rename to `try_update` (which is not stable on the MSRV toolchain).

**2. Pin uuid to 1.26.1 in the MSRV CI job only** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)

uuid 1.26.1 carries `rust-version = "1.85.0"` and satisfies the `"1.6"` semver constraint already declared in `crates/transport/Cargo.toml`. The pin is a single `cargo update -p uuid --precise 1.26.1` step inserted before the `cargo check` step in the `msrv` job. No other job is touched. The workspace MSRV (`1.88`) and `Cargo.toml` dependency declarations are unchanged — raising the MSRV to 1.89 is David's call.

pulls.title: docs(adr): ADR 0088 group liveness contract (I8) — Proposed
pulls.body:
**Docs only. Status Proposed. Only David marks it Accepted.**

This is ADR 0088, the **group liveness (0088)** contract ruled by D37 for W3-0. It is not ADR 0104 (prov.), the transport liveness ADR.

## What it decides

- **L1:** admission and eviction complete when any one active admin is online. Catch-up and repair complete when any one holder is online. No operation depends on a particular device: the owner device, the inviter, the creator or the original sealer.
- **L2:** only the may-block-forever list (§2) may block an operation without bound. Any other indefinite wait is a defect.
- **L3:** a listed block ends in a typed terminal outcome, not a silent pending state.
- **L4:** no safety rule is traded. A slice meets L1 with verified evidence, and any new acceptance rule needs its own security argument.
- **§3 supersession table:**
  - superseded: 0038, 0060 and 0069;
  - superseded in part: 0064 Decision §3 and 0066 §2;
  - decided with S7: 0062;
  - amended by slices: 0016 §6, 0007 consent, and 0059 with 0064 §1a.
  - Each takes effect when its slice is Accepted. Accepted ADRs stay byte-identical, so this is recorded here and in the README only.
- **§4 slices S1–S8**, with an acceptance order. S1 is ADR 0106 (Accepted).

## Open for David (G2–G7)

1. The §2 list.
2. Fetch-by-hash or a persisted catch-up log.
3. Whether in-process red tests count as harness-first.

Fixes D39(A), David's ruling D39: fix now and re-tag v0.46.0. It is the hazard reproduced in #1147, from the #1146 family.

## Bug
A Home or named-group device whose join **failed or timed out after a state-only intermediate apply** keeps a durable `not_member` row. The intermediate apply is either the ADR 0106 carry or, before v0.46, the same commit arriving by gossip first.
- The pre-Welcome apply persists the row and clears `pending_join_stubs`.

- `x0x group leave` returns 403, because #446 requires active membership.
- A restart reloads the row.

So the documented 0106 fallback ("request a fresh invite") could never work.

Still under the membership guard already held there, `clear_stale_not_member_join_row` does two things, then the request falls through to the **ordinary fresh-join path**, which installs the stub, registers the attempt and fires the volley:
- it removes the in-memory row(s) for the group (key or `mls_group_id` alias), re-checking under the write lock that the joiner is not an active member;

Refs #1623 (first slice). Refs #1356 (ADR 0109 §2 rule (b), §7 (b), D82).

## Root cause

A pre-Welcome joiner has no TreeKEM group for the group. The `MemberRemoved`, `MemberBanned` and `JoinRequestApproved` applies need a local TreeKEM group to process the link's TreeKEM commit. ## Root cause

ADR 0110 §3 asks for the guard "immediately before each physical write". Since the issue was filed, #1664 moved every request-path write to `Agent::send_machine_addressed_dm`. The S4 carriers (`crypto_exclusion`, `rebind`, `owner_recovery` `serve_catchup`) use `guarded_admission` at each write. So the request path was already guarded at the write on main.

One write was not guarded: the response path's next-page ask. `handle_treekem_catchup_response` checks the sender's revocation at the top. This PR is the **authority-side part** of #1149. It does not close the issue.

David's ruling (4 Nov 17:43 GMT): "#1149: normal public PR, after a reviewer confirms the finding"

An independent reviewer confirmed the finding. The engineer ruled that this PR lands as the authority-side part, with "Refs #1149".

## Real impact

On main, the authority re-admits a **banned** agent:

- A banned agent redeems an unaddressed invite that was minted before the ban. The authority sets the banned row back to `active`.
- In a TreeKEM group the authority also adds the agent to the tree and sends it a Welcome. The banned agent gets the TreeKEM keys for the current epoch and reads messages that are encrypted after the ban.

With this PR the authority refuses the join. The row stays `banned`, the agent gets no keys, and the invite is not consumed.

pulls.title: fix(w3h): same-instant stream opens no longer reorder the trace (#1245)
pulls.body:
Refs #1245 (first slice).

## Summary

The W3-H canonical trace changed when two streams on one node pair opened
at the same virtual instant in opposite directions. Two causes:

- The sim fabric used one stream counter per unordered node pair. If A and O
  each opened a stream at the same instant, the task that ran first got
  `stream<n>` and the other got `stream<n+1>`. All later writes on those
  lanes then had different lane names.
- The `[links]` list of a pair kept task order for events at the same instant.

This PR changes only the simulated fabric (`src/network/sim.rs`, test builds):

- Stream ordinals are counted per opener direction. Even ordinals are opened
  by the lower node key, odd ordinals by the higher key. One ordinal still
  names one stream of the pair.
- `[links]` entries are sorted by virtual time. At one instant, connection
  events (`#n open`, `#n close`) keep their recorded order, because that
  order is causal. Stream events (`open`, `fin-read`) follow them in text order.

No daemon code changes. No wire or API change. Verdicts do not change (the
gate is verdict-only under D196); this only removes one source of distinct
traces.

## Status of the sources listed in #1245 (main c44bcdc14)

Evidence: `status-on-main.md` and the per-case table from CI run 41828700025.

- Entropy by spawn lineage and the `check-cfg` entry: done (#1636, #1641).

- Same-instant task ordering: partly done (#1647, #

pulls.title: fix(groups): #1652 the re-seat journal record digest is over a canonical encoding
pulls.body:
fix(groups): #1652 the re-seat journal record digest is over a canonical encoding

Fixes #1652 (the `ReseatJournalV1::digest_record` item; the other two items
are covered on main / on open PRs #1777–#1780, per the issue).

## Root cause

`ReseatJournalV1::digest_record` hashed `serde_json::to_vec(&GroupInfo)`,
which is not a canonical encoding. `GroupInfo` serialises two hash-table
fields — `issued_invites: HashMap<String, IssuedInviteRecord>` and
`issued_invite_secrets: HashSet<String>` (`src/groups/mod.rs`) — whose JSON
key and element order is per-process hash-table iteration order. So the
digest of an *unchanged* record changes across a restart, and the
originality guard in `staged_result_ready` ("the record is not the
journalled original (digest)") can stop recognising the journalled original
exactly when it matters: after the restart the guard runs on.

## Fix

`digest_record` now hashes a canonical encoding:

- the record as a `serde_json::Value`, which sorts every object's keys
  (`serde_json::Map` is a `BTreeMap`; this repo does not enable
  `preserve_order`);
- the invite-secrets array (a set — it has no order) replaced by the sorted
  set, failing closed (`None`) if the expected field is absent, so a future
  rename cannot silently hash a non-canonical encoding;
- prefixed with the `x0x.reseat-record-digest.v1` domain tag, in the style
  of `x0x.policy-hash.v1` / `x0x.group-genesis-hash.v1`.

Every other serialised collection reachable from `GroupInfo` is a
`BTreeM

pulls.title: fix(dm): #1455 — the Leaf's inbox EAGER seat goes to the recipient's own machine
pulls.body:
Fixes #1455

## Root cause

A durable DM publish (`dm_send.rs` → `PubSubManager::publish_topic_id`) seeds the **whole connected plane** as the recipient-inbox topic's membership and lets saorsa-gossip choose the Leaf's ≤2 EAGER targets (`leaf_max_eager_degree = 2`) by PeerScore. The gossip wire has **no SUBSCRIBE message** and the score carries no subscription signal, so for fresh peers (all tied at 0.7) the two eager seats resolve by **hash order over the plane**. The existing preferred-peer pass (`select_one_full_bootstrap_eager_peer`, #774/C5b) only prefers coordinators/relays/pinned bootstrap peers — `None` on a plane of plain Leaf daemons — and the recipient is never a candidate.

A bystander Leaf that receives the unsubscribed EAGER frame drops it (`refuse_leaf_unsubscribed_passthrough`, #380 C0), and its lazy set for the fresh topic contains only the sender, so its IHAVE flush goes nowhere. The recipient never sees the primary publish, the sender's `ACK_LEGACY_BUS_FALLBACK_DELAY` (250 ms) expires, and the legacy bus fires — the reported 260–355 ms sends. The asymmetry already existed on the ACK side (C5b pins a preferred eager before the durable ACK publish); the outbound send path pinned nothing.

Verified still present on current main: no eager-selection changes in `src/gossip/`, `src/dm_send.rs` or `src/dm_inbox.rs` between the measured `40e0f5d4` and `8596bb83d`; the saorsa-gossip pin is `=0.5.90` in both. The cause sits in x0x — the app owns exactly the knowledge

pulls.title: fix(groups): #1775 GSS share hold keeps unpinned secrets from ending its waits
pulls.body:
Refs #1775

This PR does not close #1775. Item 1 of #1775 (the MemberRemoved/MemberBanned arms keep an uncommitted same-epoch secret without a sender check) stays open on #1775. Its fix is the fenced `gss_removal_waits_for_share` arm in `src/server/routes/named_groups.rs`. Under the Engineer rulings of 3 Nov 22:45 GMT and 4 Nov 05:07 GMT, that change lands after #1781, in a later PR. No new issue is opened for it.

## Summary

The rule: **a head commit pins a secret value only when it commits with one.** `gss_share_hold::secret_unpinned` implements it. A secret is unpinned when a sealed share raised the local epoch above the epoch the head commits, or when a #1578 keyless commit's durable mark covers its epoch.

- **Item 4 (keyless commit window, Engineer ruling 3 Nov 15:58 GMT).** A #1578 keyless install writes a durable `KeylessMark { secret_epoch, actor, head }` in the hold file before the head moves. If the mark write fails, the install returns `LocalFailure` and the head does not move. The mark keeps the first installed foreign secret of that epoch replaceable, and keeps new ciphertext held, until the exclusion's own actor seals a share. pulls.title: fix(groups): a readmitted joiner's attempt ends typed when the sealer's Welcome is gone (#1661 s2)
pulls.body:
Refs #1661 (slice 2 of 3; slice 1 is #1773).

## What changes

A readmitted pre-Welcome joiner can lose the sealer's staged Welcome for its own seal. The sealer keeps that Welcome in memory only, for `PENDING_WELCOME_TTL` (10 minutes), and a sealer restart loses it sooner. On main the joiner then loops `catching_up` ⇄ `awaiting_attestation` with no end: each attested round replays the kept chain, the seal's Welcome fetch fails, and the node asks again.

With this PR, when all of these are true:

- the node entered `readmission_required {base_beyond_retention}` during this join attempt,
- its own seal (`MemberAdded` or `JoinRequestApproved` with a `welcome_ref` and no inline Welcome) did not apply because the Welcome **fetch** failed,
- `PENDING_WELCOME_TTL` has passed since the **first** failed fetch (the seal is older, so the Welcome cannot be served any more), and
- the node holds no keys (no active seat, no TreeKEM group) and has no recorded attestation conflict,

the recovery tick ends the attempt:

- `last_join_outcome` = `timed_out`, reason `rearm_original_result_unavailable` (ADR 0107, existing values);
- `recovery.state` = `readmission_required`, `cause` `base_beyond_retention`, `exit` `manual_remove_and_reinvite` (D43, existing values);
- the node sends no more requests and applies no later ATA for that attempt;
- the attempt bookkeeping (polls, inviter pin, registry entry) is retired, so the D43 re-invite is not refused `join_already_pending`.

pulls.title: fix(groups): #1766 GSS crypto-only exclusion keeps an uncommitted secret only from its actor
pulls.body:
## What

Fixes #1766. Refs #1721, #1597.

The GSS `CryptoExclusionV1` install (`install_gss`) kept a local secret of
the frame's epoch when one was already installed. That secret is always
uncommitted (the frame binds the parent's committed epoch + 1), and any
Active admin can install it with an early `SecureShareDelivered`. The
install did not check who sealed it. If another admin `B` sealed its own
secret of that epoch first, the survivor installed the frame's head over
`B`'s key: the group split, and `B` chose the key.

## Root cause and fix

The share path recorded no sender, so the keep path had no provenance to
check. Now:

- **Record.** The share path records the sender of an installed share
  whose epoch no head commits yet (`gss_share_hold::note_share_sender`).
  The record is durable in the existing per-group GSS hold file, as an
  optional `share_sender` field. A crash between the share and the frame
  keeps it, so the restarted survivor still installs with the author
  offline (`a_crash_before_the_exclusion_install_keeps_the_frame_durable`).
- **Check.** `install_gss` keeps that secret only when the frame's actor
  sealed it (`share_sent_by`). Otherwise the frame takes the existing wait
  path: durable hold, `WaitingForShare`, frame kept for the retry.
- **Recover.** While a verified transition of that epoch waits, a share of
  the same epoch from a different sender may replace the uncommitted
  secret (`replaces_uncommitted_secret`). So the actor's resent share

pulls.title: fix(groups): cap join-carry ATA signing at the §11 budget and per-requester rate (#1651)
pulls.body:
Fixes #1651

## Root cause

`join_carry_attestation` (`src/server/routes/named_groups/group_recovery.rs`) signed one ML-DSA ATA per `(attempt_id, from_revision)` — the 256-entry cache only deduped repeats of the same attempt — and never called `ResponderBudget::may_sign()`. The request path (`sign_ata`) is capped at 32 signatures per minute (ADR 0109 §11, D83); the join-carry path was uncapped, bounded only indirectly by the ADR 0107 serving guard.

## Fix

The join carry now draws from the same §11 responder signature budget as the request path:

- A cache hit on `(attempt_id, from_revision)` serves the cached ATA — no signature, no budget spent, same as `sign_ata`'s cache.
- On a miss the 60-second window rolls and `may_sign()` gates the signature. A join result passes no `admit()` (that is the request path's roller), so the window rolls here; without that, a pure join-carry workload would turn the per-minute budget into a lifetime cap of 32.
- Over budget, the `JoinResult` is still sent, without the ATA: `join_carry_attestation` returns `None`, the `JoinResultMessage` carries `admin_attestation: None` (the field is already an `Option`), and the joiner falls back to the §2 stale-base pending path and `awaiting_attestation` — the handling it already has for every other no-carry cause.

pulls.body:
Fixes #1765

## Problem
ADR 0110 §5, "Memory-only durability" (line 378), and the `s4_sidecar_rebuild` row (line 451) say: while the `.evs` sidecar runs memory-only, S4 seals only a trigger that is durable elsewhere. Any other trigger must show `waiting_for_durable_intake`. On main, a live Agent revocation reaches S4 before its revocation-store write. That write runs in a detached task, and the task drops its errors. `revocation_eviction.rs` (old line 1454) also treated every trigger as durable under a memory-only file. The result: S4 sealed a revocation that was not on disk, and a failed write was not retried.

Note: Agent subjects are stored in the v1 store `revocations.bin`, not in `revocations-v2.bin` (`to_bytes_v2` keeps only binding records). The fix therefore gates on the v1 store write.

## Fix (durable path, reliability first)
- `RevocationIntake` (`src/groups/eviction.rs`) keeps the hash of each live-route record (`note_verified`) as not durable until a store write succeeds. A startup-loaded record is already durable. All its durability methods are `pub(crate)`.
- `persist_s4_revocations` (`src/lib.rs`) reads the pending hashes and encodes the store snapshot under one read guard of the set. It marks durable only the pending hashes that are in that snapshot. Each live route notes its record under the set's write guard, after the insert. So no hash becomes durable unless it is in the bytes written. A record that the 90-day TTL sweep takes from the set before any write

pulls.title: fix(upgrade): bring the acknowledged flush owner to Windows (#1588)
pulls.body:
Fixes #1588. Part of #1374 (follow-up from #1566).

## Problem

A supervised apply (`X0X_SUPERVISED=1`) on Windows was refused with
"acknowledged shutdown owner unavailable". The acknowledged shutdown flush
owner was Unix-only: it needed a suspend-inclusive boot clock, the Unix
record directory barrier and the Unix `upgrade-flush.sock` listener. The
Windows wrapper also ended the service on exit 75 (`EX_TEMPFAIL`), so a
failed flush could not restart on the restored binary.

## Change

This brings the flush owner to Windows with the Unix contract. It does not
bypass the flush gate.

- **Clock** (`src/upgrade/shutdown_flush.rs`): Windows uses `GetTickCount64`
  (ms since boot, includes sleep and hibernation, ignores wall-clock
  changes) with the kernel `BootId` registry value as the boot identity
  (`windows-boot-<n>`). A missing `BootId` is a clock error, so the flush
  refuses before stop and the daemon keeps serving.
- **Record barrier** (`src/upgrade/journal.rs`, `src/upgrade/mod.rs`):
  `journal::open_for_sync` opens with write access and directories with
  `FILE_FLAG_BACKUP_SEMANTICS`, so `sync_all` (`FlushFileBuffers`) is a real
  directory barrier. A file system that refuses the flush refuses the
  barrier. The restore path and arm recovery use the same helper.
- **Control channel** (`src/server/upgrade_flush.rs`, `src/server/mod.rs`):
  the module is no longer `cfg(unix)`. Windows serves the same
  newline-delimited JSON arm-and-flush protocol on the local named pipe

fix(home): #824 POST ~ resolves to the canonical Home the register names

Fixes #824

## Root cause

The Tier-1 `("home")` register stores the canonical Home's **stable id**
(`home_pointer_from_state`, `src/server/routes/sync.rs`), but the roster map
is keyed by the id the group was created or joined under — and a pre-pin
legacy record carries a map key that **differs** from its stable id
(`GroupGenesis::with_existing_id`, `src/groups/mod.rs`). The
prefer-canonical branch of `resolve_home` matched the pointer against the

canonical Home therefore missed the canonical entry, fell through to
`find_home`'s smallest-stable-id rule — which answers with the duplicate —
and `POST ~` refused with `409 adoption_pending` (or, with no
pointer at all, the `ambiguous_home` path) instead of resolving to the
canonical Home the register had already named. That is the #824 class of
wrong-Home answers: the seat not landing in the owner's canonical Home.

`resolve_home` now matches the pointer against the map key **and** the
stable id, exactly as `is_provably_retired` and the seat guard's own match
(`canonical == group_id || canonical == info.stable_group_id()`) already
do, so the three surfaces can no longer disagree about which group the
register names. When an aliased record matches twice (one group under two
keys), the choice is deterministic (smallest stable id, then map key). The

## Summary

pulls.title: fix(upgrade): refuse a transactional socket flush with no restart-capable owner (#1670)
pulls.body:
Refs #1670

## What

An arm request for a participant whose frozen restart mode is `TransactionalHandoff` is now refused at admission, before any shutdown, with an error saying no restart-capable owner is established. The daemon keeps serving, and nothing is armed, restored or resolved, so a retry refuses the same way.

## Why

A completed transactional socket flush ends the old participant with exit 0, and no supervisor restarts it. The durable receipt proves the flush only. Reaping the old participant and starting the candidate need an owner outside the stopped process, and none exists today: the arm-and-flush path spawns no helper and the #1375 launcher is not implemented. Until that owner lands, refusing before the stop is the only safe behaviour.

This is an interim guard, so it says `Refs #1670`, not `Fixes`. #1670 stays open for the full acceptance (an established, retained restart owner verified against the frozen transaction, generation, participant identity and restart binding, plus the Linux/systemd harness evidence), which arrives with the #1375 launcher and #1376 recovery work.

- `src/upgrade/restart.rs`: `transactional_flush_owner()` refuses every binding until a launcher is verified.

- `hang`: the candidate never becomes healthy.
- `restart`: the launcher dies right after a real exec failure.
- `restart-child`: the launcher dies while the child lives.

The marker proves that a child of the restored argv runs and that the installed bytes are the previous release by hash. It does not hash `/proc/<pid>/exe` of the child; that is on the S3c list.

pulls.title: S3b s1: durable launcher trial reserves attempts before exec (#1375)
pulls.body:
Adds the stable launcher binary target (`src/bin/x0x-launcher.rs`) and the dormant S3b engine's trial record (`src/upgrade/launcher/mod.rs`). The module is compiled into the bin through a `#[path]` include; no library, installer or daemon apply path calls it, and nothing activates it.

`Trial::reserve` persists the attempt through the journal's auxiliary-record fsync barrier **before** the candidate spawn, so a launch that cannot exec (exit 203/EXEC) is still charged (#1168): the candidate would have to run code to count its own boot, which is exactly what a broken binary cannot do. The code's constants are D192's named values — 30 s flush, 3 attempts of 120 s readiness + 60 s stable health, 10 s reap, 10 s gap — under the 660 s trial ceiling, whose remaining allowance covers D192's restore allowances.

The record cannot be replaced or reset: a fresh trial with a later start never overwrites the original deadline, `load` re-establishes the fsync barrier, and a corrupt or wrong-transaction file never resets the budget.

Tests: inert unit tests (`cargo test --bin x0x-launcher`), including `attempts_survive_reload_and_exec_failure` — reserve, a real failed exec, reload, attempts == 1.

pulls.title: fix(discovery): #1643 a same-second anonymous announce no longer drops a disclosed certificate
pulls.body:
Fixes #1643

## Problem

A peer could lose an owner certificate an agent had just disclosed with
`POST /announce` (`announce_identity(true, true)`). Owner trust for that agent
then read false on the peer until the next cert-carrying announcement, and the
owner-trust gates (remote GUI show, owner-only routes) refused in that window.
CI saw this in PR #1533's Coverage Gate:
`server::gui_show_pair::remote_show_opens_on_the_other_owner_daemon` returned
`target_needs_upgrade` after its readiness loop had already seen `trusted=true`.

## Cause

- `announced_at` has one-second precision.
- `upsert_discovered_agent` accepts an incoming announcement at
  `incoming.announced_at >= existing.announced_at`, and a cert-less announcement
  that commits to a different `cert_digest` drops the cached certificate (the
  ADR-0038 round-2 freshness rule). An equal timestamp was enough.
- `announce_identity` recorded consent only after the disclosure was published,
  so every announcement built while the call was in flight (the startup announce,
  the 3 s delayed beat, a heartbeat tick, the owner-connect re-announce) was
  anonymous. Its anonymous digest differs from the disclosure's digest, so when
  gossip delivered it after a same-second disclosure, the merge deleted the
  certificate the disclosure had just landed.

## Fix — the issue's options 1 + 3 (no wire change, no API change)

**Consent ordering (main's rule, kept)** — `announce_identity` records
consent only after the disclosure publish

Setup S0, then three runs on three groups in one simulation. In each run, A mints invite I at r, renames `n` times and seals J. The gap is `n + 1` links, because the seal is a link too.

pulls.body:
Fixes #1685.

## Root cause

The hot loop had exactly one timer-free edge: the `was_truncated` branch of `handle_treekem_catchup_response` re-requested the next page **at once** (`request_treekem_catchup_page`), with no throttle, no bound and no progress check. In the H-S3-c/c2 shape a fork-stranded node's head does not link to the responder's fork commits, so every served event is correctly retained as pending (`treekem_state_frontier_gap_reason` → `state_hash_gap`), the catch-up cursor `(state_revision, secret_epoch, state_hash)` never moves, and the responder's page is a pure function of that cursor (`frontier.revision > from_revision || frontier.epoch > from_treekem_epoch`, sorted, capped) — the identical request re-fetches the identical truncated page forever:

apply-nothing → `replay_pending_treekem_events` → `requeue_treekem_pending_events` → immediate re-request → identical truncated response → repeat.

No timer anywhere in the cycle, so the CPU spins on both peers (the macOS `sample` shows `handle_treekem_catchup_response` → `replay_pending_treekem_events` → `requeue_treekem_pending_events` hot, and `handle_treekem_catchup_request` hot from serving the same page), and a paused tokio runtime never parks, so virtual time cannot advance — nextest SIGTERMs the simulated case and no receipt is written. The responder never self-loops; its heat was this same edge (the requester's re-ask).

## The fix

`handle_treekem_catchup_response` captures the cursor and whether the pag

pulls.title: fix(groups): #1597 GSS owner recovery rotates from the committed secret epoch
pulls.body:
## What

Item 1 of #1597, plus the `docs/api.md` row from item 5. Refs #1597 — not
Fixes: item 2 belongs to #1581, item 4 landed with #1714, and item 3
(quarantined-sidecar diagnostics listing) is separate work, so the issue
stays open.

## Item 1: GSS `OwnerRecoveryV1` epoch baseline

Both sides of a GSS owner recovery used the **local** `secret_epoch` as
the rotation baseline: the receiver's L4 rule
(`validate_against_parent`'s GSS arm) required
`next_secret_epoch == parent.secret_epoch + 1`, and the author's GSS arm
rotated from `next.secret_epoch`. A sealed early share can raise the
local epoch before the commit of that epoch arrives, so in that window
the author bound `local + 1` while a receiver whose local epoch still
matched the head expected `committed + 1` — a valid recovery was refused
with `recovery_proof_invalid` (fail-closed availability, not an
unauthorized install; the mandate, signature and named-seat checks all
still ran).

Both now use the **committed** epoch — the epoch the retained head
commit binds, the same baseline `CryptoExclusionV1` established
(`committed_secret_epoch`, `src/groups/crypto_exclusion.rs:461`):

- receiver: the GSS arm requires
  `next_secret_epoch == committed_secret_epoch(parent) + 1`;
- author: `try_commit`'s GSS arm sets
  `next.secret_epoch = committed_secret_epoch(info)` before
  `rotate_shared_secret()`, as the GSS crypto-exclusion author already

pulls.body:
Fixes #1663

## Round 7 (Claude takeover, 3 Nov 2026): ZCode F1 fixed

The Engineer ruled (3 Nov 04:05 GMT) that ZCode's minor F1 is fixed in this PR.

**F1.** A share debt is armed under the republished key K1. Before the carrier accepts a K1 share, the member is removed and admitted again with a new join key K2, and no round runs between the two. The round never sees the member leave the Active roster, so the K1 debt stays. The rounds seal to the roster key K2 only, so the K1 debt can never end. It held the delivery row open for ever.

- `CeDelivery::gss_shares_unseated` holds the debtors whose armed key the durable write has not seated yet. `owe_gss_shares_after_republish` adds the actor. `retract_gss_shares_after_republish` restores the set on a failed save. The new `seat_gss_shares_after_republish` removes the actor after a successful persist (`receive` calls it under the membership guard).
- Each round calls `end_reseated_share_debts`. A seated debt whose armed key is not the seat's roster key now ends. The member then follows the ordinary path: the arm reset it to `Sent`, so it converges only on a head report after a share sealed to its curre

pulls.title: refactor(groups): a re-seat staging slot behind the group map guards (#1699 part 1)
pulls.body:
## Summary

Part of #1699 (1 of 3). ADR 0109 §3 step 2 says the re-seat subject joins into a staging record **outside the live map**. On main the staged join runs in the live map, so the contained original leaves containment before the keyed swap (#1699).

This PR adds the type that the fix needs, with no behaviour change:

- `ScopedGroupMap<V>` (`src/server/reseat_scope.rs`) is now the type of `named_groups`, `treekem_groups` and `mls_groups`. It holds the live map and a staging slot.
- `read`/`write`/`try_read`/`try_write` keep the `RwLock` guard API. They select the staging slot only for a task that runs inside `in_reseat_scope` (a tokio task-local). Every other task selects the live map. So the ~2,000 call sites do not change.
- `live_*`/`staging_*` ignore the scope, for the swap (part 2).

pulls.title: fix(groups): take join-artifact and Welcome deadlines on tokio's clock (#1699 part 1)
pulls.body:
Part of #1699. Refs #1689.

## What this fixes

In the H-S3-c and H-S3-c2 rows (#1689), the re-seat subject J was never keyed, so the §3 swap never ran and the worker rolled the re-seat back. Root cause: A's Welcome stream ran under `tokio::time::timeout_at(pending.created_at + PENDING_WELCOME_TTL)`, with a `std::time::Instant` converted by `.into()`. The conversion keeps `std`'s reading. With paused tokio time (W3-H sims) tokio's clock runs ahead of `std`'s by all the advanced time, so after the 30-minute advance the deadline had already passed. The stream sent the Offer and both chunks, then the timeout dropped it before the final ack. A logged `chunk_ack_recv matched_pending=false` and sent no `Complete`. J's Welcome fetch timed out, its join poll ended `timed_out`, and `reseat_progress` called `rollback_reseat(.., "staged_join_ended")`.

The change: `tokio_deadline()` measures the time left on `std`'s clock and adds it to tokio's now. It is used at the three `timeout_at(<std deadline>.into(), ..)` sites: the Welcome stream, the join-artifact egress task and the pinned single exchange. Without paused time the two clocks agree, so production timing does not change. No wire or API change.

## Proof

- `server::routes::named_groups::tokio_deadline_tests::a_std_deadline_keeps_its_time_left_after_paused_time_advances`: red with main's `.into()` (mutation run, `unit-red-mutation-into.log`), green here.

## Cause

`classify_refused_joiner_fork_chain` (`src/server/routes/named_groups.rs`) checked `mandate_anchors_commit_under_trusted_owner` before the chain walk, and it returned `false` there. | Mandate, chain does not validate | `false` | `false` |
| Mandate, v1-only or no attestation | `false` before the v1 audit and fork evidence | same |
| No mandate | — | unchanged |

pulls.title: fix(w3h): store the admission count the finish hook checked
pulls.body:
## Summary

Under W3-H paused time, a counted blocking task that has already returned does not hold the clock until Tokio marks the pool thread idle. The finish hook stores the admission count it compared with the finish count. It does not read that counter again. A task admitted after that check is outside the stored excuse, so the paused clock stays still while the new task runs.

The counted set is `counted_spawn_blocking`: the harness `spawn_blocking` and `spawn_blocking_on` wrappers, and `history::run_blocking` on a `tokio_unstable` test build. The closure registers its task id before the body runs. `blocking_finished` moves only for those ids. Raw `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` and `tokio::fs` are outside the set. `ReadDir::next_entry` batches entries, and `File::write_all` can spawn more than once per call, so one count per call is not one pool task. An outside finish does not publish and does not move either counter. While an excuse is armed, one extra busy thread from outside the set can still let the clock step. `AutoAdvanceHold` stays outside the set. `clear_idle_wait` can zero the counters while the runtime is still running; that drops a publish.

## Fix round 4

- `publish_wind_down` stores the count the finish hook already checked. A gate sits between that load and the store. `w3h_admission_counted_before_publish_keeps_the_checked_count` admits the next task in the gate, on the same pool thread, with an empty queue. Before the fix the stored count was 2 after a c

pulls.body:
## Summary

The idle recheck no longer publishes `ready`. It wakes the reactor with a loopback datagram, and only the park hook on the runtime thread publishes. A recheck tick in the gap after the driver wakes and before `after_unpark` clears `parked` cannot poll the barrier ahead of a task the pool completion already queued.

The W3-H runtime sets `event_interval` to `u32::MAX`, so `block_on` polls its future when the ready queue is empty rather than every 61 tasks. A `spawn_blocking` completion no longer resumes the barrier in the middle of that chain.

pulls.body:
Fixes #1648

Follow-up to ZCode's exact-head review of #1533 (finding 1, P3). Branch is exactly current main (7335c5d, #1533 merged) plus this change.

## Root cause

In `reseat_group_member` (`src/server/routes/named_groups/group_recovery.rs`) the re-seat invite was minted durably first (owner path through the shared `mint_invite_transaction`, promoted-admin path through `mint_reseat_invite`), and only then was the signed authorisation recorded in the `.grecov` sidecar. ## Root cause

`legacy_store_view` runs inside every roster save. For each placeheld group it first makes the group's authoritative record durable in the `.grecov` sidecar (`sync_authoritative`). Only the affected group is held back. Its containment stays.

- When a group's authoritative write fails, its legacy entry keeps its **last durable form** (`unsynced_legacy_entry`):

  - If neither is known, the save fails as a whole, as before.
- The group is marked `authoritative_failed` and `legacy_pending`. The other groups are saved.

The Vulnerability Scan job in the Security workflow fails on master because of RUSTSEC-2026-0387. That advisory, published 2026-10-23, reports that crypto-bigint operations meant to be constant-time could branch on secret values. Only crypto-bigint 0.7.6 and later are patched.

ant-quic reaches crypto-bigint 0.5.5 through one path only:

crypto-bigint 0.5.5
└── elliptic-curve 0.13.8
    ├── p256 0.13.2

pulls.title: fix(gossip): fail fast when membership egress stalls (#1395)
pulls.body:
Fixes #1395

## Root cause

The membership dispatcher lane (4 workers, 5 s `MEMBERSHIP_MESSAGE_HANDLE_TIMEOUT`
watchdog) timed out — and the watchdog **cancels real protocol work mid-handler** —
because handler completion was coupled to unbounded egress:

1. Every inbound HyParView/SWIM frame is answered with egress *inside* the handler
   future: Ping → Ack, Join → ForwardJoin fan-out (sequential to the whole active
   view), Neighbor → NeighborReply, PingReq → Ping.
2. saorsa-gossip-membership 0.5.90 awaits those `send_to_peer` calls **with no
   timeout** — only the pubsub lane bounds its per-peer sends upstream
   (`PER_PEER_REPUBLISH_TIMEOUT` = 4 s in saorsa-gossip-pubsub 0.5.90).
3. The send parks in ant-quic `open_uni()` when the remote stops returning
   uni-stream credit: the remote's QUIC stack still ACKs, so the connection looks
   healthy, but its app is no longer draining the recv queue, so ant-quic's
   per-connection reader parks its 64-stream accept budget ("backpressure to the
   peer's advertised stream credit", ant-quic 0.27.61 `p2p_endpoint.rs`).
4. The parked send outlives the 5 s watchdog, which cancels the handler (Ack
   unsent, fan-out truncated) and counts it in `timed_out`. One stalled remote
   pins all four workers; the 4 000-slot membership queue heads toward
   `dropped_full` and SWIM itself degrades.

This is exactly the live #288 fleet signature (2026-07-30): `bytes=2` membership
frames at `elapsed_ms=5001`, two peers pinning all four worker I

pulls.body:
Fixes #1578

## Problem

Since #1508, a GSS survivor whose roster seat carries no KEM public key never
receives the re-sealed share of the rotated secret: every author skips the
seal for that seat (`spawn_gss_share_to` logs "no KEM key on record for a
survivor" and moves on), exactly as for a ban. The verified S4
`CryptoExclusionV1` GSS frame installs only with its share, so on such a
survivor the frame stayed `WaitingForShare` for ever: the group head stayed at
the parent, the frame stayed pending in the stash, and the author's delivery
row kept resending because the survivor's head report never showed the result.

## Root cause

`install_gss` has exactly one recovery for a frame whose share has not
arrived: wait for it. That is correct for a seat that *can* receive the share
(a KEM-seated survivor, offline or lagging, converges when the share lands).
It is wrong for a seat that *cannot*: the wait has no exit, because the event
it waits for is the one every author refuses to produce.

## Chosen recovery path

The frame installs keyless, with a typed, observable pending state, and the
share arrives later through the existing path. No wire format change and no
public API change beyond the approved 409 (below).

- `own_seat_cannot_take_a_share` recognises the stranding case on the

pulls.title: fix(upgrade): Windows supervision classifier gates the X0X_SUPERVISED marker on wrapper-script readback (#621) [1/2]
pulls.body:
## What

The Windows half of ADR-0061 clause 3 (#621, deferred from #415): on Windows, `X0X_SUPERVISED=1` no longer classifies a `SupervisedExit` on its own. The upgrade-time resolver now runs a **wrapper-script loaded-policy readback** and refuses the apply on every path it cannot confirm.

Part 1 of 2 — stacked; part 2 (1611) is the versioned wrapper template and `x0x autostart` wiring on top of this branch.

## Root cause (verified on main at 75aba5f)

`plan_restart_mode` accepts the marker on every platform, and `resolve_restart_identity` gates the marker only through the **launchd** readback, which returns `Unavailable` on non-macOS — "the marker stands". So on Windows, `X0X_SUPERVISED=1` + `stop_on_upgrade=true` exits 100 into whatever the operator's wrapper (WinSW/NSSM/SCM) actually does. That is the "marker in isolation" failure ADR-0061 §3 rules out: nothing verifies the wrapper restarts after 100, so a misconfigured wrapper means the daemon goes down and stays down, silently, with new bytes on disk.

## The fix

- `WindowsWrapperReadback` — the Windows twin of `LaunchdPolicyReadback` (#615) and `SystemdPolicyReadback` (#690). Windows has no `launchctl`/`systemctl` to query, so the **loaded policy is the wrapper script itself**, named by an explicit `X0X_WRAPPER` binding that the wrapper (template in part 2) sets to its own path at runtime. Explicit deployment binding per §3 — no ancestry sniffing, no name matching.
- `readback_windows_wrapper_script` — a platform-fr

pulls.body:
Fixes #1595 (second of a two-PR split; #1609 is the first — rebase this PR onto main when #1609 merges).

## What this fixes

**1. One slow request at upgrade time no longer holds a release forever (issue #1595 item 4 / Claude #1565 finding 4).** A started-flush failure caused *only* by unfinished producers at the drain bound — the exact receipt refusal `finish` reports (`shutdown producers remain unfinished`, now a shared `pub(crate)` constant so the marker cannot drift) — previously wrote the per-release hold immediately. Such a failure is transient, so it now draws a fixed bounded retry budget: **two retries per release**, a constant, not a config key (same ruling as the 30 s flush budget), counted in `<data_dir>/upgrade-flush-producer-retries.json`. Each budget failure still restores and exits `EX_TEMPFAIL` (item 1's contract is unchanged — the restart is what retries); the difference is no hold is written for the first two, so the service-manager restart retries the release. The third failure of the same release holds it. A failure of a different release resets the count, any other failure cause never touches the budget, and a count that cannot be persisted holds immediately (no unbounded retry loops). Both failure paths (supervised exit in `trigger_restart`, arm-and-flush in `arm`) share one policy helper, `hold_or_retry_started_failure`.

Fixes #1599

## Verdict: test bug, not a teardown bug

The reauth loop honoured the ADR-0074 §4 bound in every observed execution — in the failing CI shape it fail-closed the stalled pass at exactly `event + 5 s` on the paused clock. What failed was the test's **sole control of the paused tokio clock**: `World::revoke_grant` ran the real v3 gossip ingest (`ingest_share_grant_revocations`), whose durable `revocations-v3.bin` write (`tokio::fs`, fsync, cross-process `.lock`) parks the test task on real async file I/O. The test resumes with the stream already torn down and the "stream must still be open while the stalled pass awaits the deadline" assertion fails — the exact CI panic.

Reproduced in-repo by replacing the revoke's park with a timerless, inhibit-free park (helper task + oneshot): the clock walks 150 ms → 4 850 ms → teardown, and the first assertion panics with the exact CI message. pulls.body:
Fixes #1239

#1590 moved the share-grant evaluation's evidence Lookup and usable reads onto the tracked bounded workers, but the evaluation still took its candidates snapshot — `ShareGrantStore::candidates_for_local_agent`, a synchronous std-RwLock read of the whole grant state — inline on the caller's Tokio worker. Every caller of the evaluation (the inbound DM gate `ShareGrantDmGate::dm_allowed`, `Agent::share_grant_access`, and the owner-trust grant evals) could still be stalled by a held store lock, a stall no tokio deadline can interrupt. This was the "ShareGrantStore std-RwLock reads on the share-grant eval" item from the 23 Oct reopen note, and it answers the Greptile P2 on #1590.

- `ShareGrantStore::candidates_before` runs the candidates snapshot on a blocking worker. Admission is a 16-permit semaphore reserved before spawning, so readers queued behind a store writer cannot grow the blocking pool without bound (the evidence runtime's reader-cap pattern). A read still waiting at the deadline fails closed (`Err(())`, so gates report Busy) and the next evaluation retries; the timed-out worker stays queued behind the writer and, once the lock frees, reads a snapshot, drops it and returns its permit. Dropping the caller aborts a queued worker; a running synchronous read cannot be aborted — exactly the evidence readers' semantics.

Fixes #1239

The share-grant evaluation still ran its borrowed EvidenceRuntime inline on the caller's Tokio worker: `evaluate_grant_access_with_evidence` awaited `EvidenceRuntime::lookup` (a full inline Lookup whose `usable` store read and responder-policy reads are synchronous) and called the blocking `usable` for its local views. - One five-second internal budget (`EVIDENCE_READ_BUDGET`, matching the load barrier and the ADR-0074 bound) covers the Lookup and both usable reads. Contention past the budget fails closed (`Err(())`, so gates report Busy / empty access) and the next evaluation retries — the typed retryable failure the issue asks for. pulls.body:
Fixes #1390

## Summary

- A grantee with `ShareGrant` `Connect { ports: [P] }` reaches the shared machine's `P` through `add_forward` and through the loopback SOCKS5 listener. The other port, listed on the same `principal = "grant"` entry, is denied on both. After `revoke_share_grant`, both live tunnels unblock within 5s and a new attempt at `P` is denied.

pulls.title: fix(owner-sync): keep not_after on synced issuance journal lines; stop the re-mint spin
pulls.body:
Stops a re-mint spin between owner devices in released owner-sync code.

Fixes #1542

## What and why
`apply_journal_line` (src/owner_sync.rs) wrote every synced `IssuanceJournal` line with `not_after: None`, while the synced value carries `Some(not_after)`. The receiving owner device's `reconcile_local_state` then minted `IssuanceJournal { not_after: None }` for the same key, and the issuing device minted `Some(..)` again. Each mint bumps the store generation, and `generation.changed()` starts the next `sync_all` pass at once. The two devices replaced each other's record in a loop that never idles. In production this is a CPU spin and a sync-traffic storm between owner devices after any certificate with an expiry is issued. Under paused W3-H time it starves auto-advance (found as the `w3h_1357_s4_certificate_rebind_pre_cutoff` stall on #1508).

## How
- `synced_journal_line`: the synced line keeps the value's `not_after`.
- `latest_journal_values`: a digest names one certificate, so a line with the same digest as a kept line but no `not_after` keeps the known expiry (in either order). A newer issuance still wins.
- `apply_journal_line`: a local line without an expiry (written before this fix) gets a new line that carries the synced expiry.
- `synced_line_needed` (Codex review at 4dc5b8b): a synced line is never appended when this owner already has a newer issuance for the agent. The owner roster (`Agent::owner_issued_certificates`) reads the journal's last line per agent, so

## Summary

Fixes #1537.

The test used the first `Poll::Pending` as proof that the blocking worker had reached the held lock. The test then fails its custody assertion even though the worker exited safely.

pulls.title: fix(security): reject oversized Retry tokens (GHSA-wppq-2f6r-wfvm)
pulls.body:
<!-- CURSOR_AGENT_PR_BODY_BEGIN -->
## Summary

Ports the quinn-proto 0.11.19 fix for [GHSA-wppq-2f6r-wfvm](https://github.com/quinn-rs/quinn/security/advisories/GHSA-wppq-2f6r-wfvm) (Retry packet with a long token panics or exhausts client memory).

The impact on ant-quic is unconfirmed. The forked `PacketBuilder` has the same `debug_assert!(max_size >= min_size)` the advisory describes, and a Retry token was stored with no length check. This does not prove that the release-mode multi-gigabyte allocation happens in this tree.

## Limit

Copied from quinn-proto 0.11.19, not a new cap:

- [`74c33ff752`](https://github.com/quinn-rs/quinn/commit/74c33ff752) rejects an Initial whose token prevents packet construction
- [`a6e78d1c8b`](https://github.com/quinn-rs/quinn/commit/a6e78d1c8b) is the threshold that shipped, and the close-path ACK budget: `max(Crypto::SIZE_BOUND + 1, ConnectionClose::SIZE_BOUND)`

In this tree those constants are 17 and 25, so the remaining-frame requirement is **25 bytes**. When an Initial header leaves less than that, or `max_size < min_size`, the datagram is truncated.

- An oversized **Retry** token closes the connection with `PROTOCOL_VIOLATION` ("Initial token leaves insufficient packet space"). The check runs before `debug_assert!(max_size >= min_size)` and is compiled into release builds.
- An oversized **cached NEW_TOKEN** is dropped. The header is rebuilt with the packet number already allocated, and the client sends the Initial without the toke

pulls.title: fix(upgrade): refuse superseded staged releases before admission
pulls.body:
Fixes #1513
Refs #1106 (M2 S2b)

An older startup waiter could reach apply after a newer eligible release had stored its receipt. The gate now durably selects the latest release for the actual participant, binding canonical install/data/identity roots, MachineId, version and original manifest/archive digests. Stale, conflicting, corrupt or unresolved selection refuses before receipt or probe mutation. Equal-precedence versions with different strings or payload bindings also refuse.
